title: codemode --lib: bench tests ungated on surface-mcp, plus real parallel order-dependence (two defects)
description:
Found while closing tokenzero-codemode-shell-output-unreachable-ref-qr4o.

Running the SAME tree repeatedly under the default parallel test harness produces different
failure counts: 16, 18 and 21 failures across runs of identical code. That made it
impossible to tell whether a change had introduced a regression by reading the failure
count, which is the property a test suite exists to provide.

Repro:
  rch exec -- cargo test -p tokenzero-mcp --lib --no-default-features --features surface-codemode
run it several times and compare 'test result' lines.

Serially it is stable: --test-threads=1 gives 9 failures, same set every time. So ~7-12 of
the parallel failures are interference between tests, not real defects.

Likely cause: codemode/exec.rs uses thread_local state (EXACT_EXPAND_REGISTRY,
RECOVERED_TOKENS, COMMIT_CALLS in store.rs) plus a shared on-disk recovery cache resolved
from the working root. Tests sharing a cache path or racing on the registry would explain
order dependence. Worth confirming before fixing.

Impact: any agent or CI gate that reads this suite's pass/fail gets a nondeterministic
answer, and real regressions can hide inside the noise band.

AC: repeated parallel runs of an unchanged tree report an identical failure set, and the
9 serial failures are either fixed or tracked individually.

comments.author: aditya
comments.text:
TRIAGE (main session, before handoff) — this bead is TWO defects, not one. Do not fix them together.

DEFECT 1: the 9 "serial failures" are NOT bugs. They are ungated tests.
All 9 live in codemode::bench::bench_harness and panic identically at
crates/tokenzero-mcp/src/codemode/bench.rs:508:67 with
  "FastMCP content rendering was not compiled into this artifact
   (missing feature surface-mcp / fastmcp-rust). Install tokenzero-mcp."
They require surface-mcp but carry no #[cfg(feature)] gate, so selecting
--no-default-features --features surface-codemode compiles them and they fail by
construction. MEASURED: default features, serial => 218 passed, 0 failed, clean.

So the earlier note that "TokenZero codemode has 9 baseline failures" is WRONG and must
not be propagated -- there is no 9-failure baseline. Fix = gate them on
cfg(all(feature="surface-codemode", feature="surface-mcp")), or make the harness skip
when the renderer is absent. Prefer GATING: the skip-when-absent shape is exactly the
trap in goal doc Section 6.5 (a GraphZero gate "passed" only because it self-skipped
with the binary missing).

DEFECT 2: the real order-dependence. Beyond those 9, these fail ONLY in parallel, and
nondeterministically -- 3 runs of one identical tree gave 17, 14, 15 failures:
  codemode::e2e_tests::envelope_v3_collapses_execution_refs_and_hides_store_block
  codemode::e2e_tests::shell_ref_is_canonical_and_expandable_in_subsequent_execution
  codemode::exec::quickjs_mutation_classifier_tests::compacted_shell_output_states_how_to_reach_the_full_content
  codemode::exec::quickjs_mutation_classifier_tests::host_shell_output_does_not_exhaust_microtask_budget
  codemode::exec::quickjs_mutation_classifier_tests::microtask_cap_error_reports_limit_count_and_batching_fix
  codemode::exec::quickjs_mutation_classifier_tests::promise_all_host_batch_stays_under_microtask_cap
  codemode::exec::quickjs_mutation_classifier_tests::the_expand_hint_actually_recovers_the_full_shell_output
  codemode::sentinel::tests::production_takeover_executes_mapped_recipe
  tests::expand::same_session_codemode_default_store_expands_without_rerun
  tests::misc::codemode_mcp_wire_preserves_canonical_refs
Every one passes serially and passes alone. The cluster is shell/expand/ref-registry
heavy, consistent with contention on thread_local EXACT_EXPAND_REGISTRY /
RECOVERED_TOKENS plus a shared on-disk recovery cache resolved from the working root
(several tests appear to share one store path). Suspect a missing per-test temp store
root. CONFIRM before fixing.

REPRO for defect 2:
  for i in 1 2 3; do rch exec -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/Users/aditya/rch_target_cm \
    cargo test -p tokenzero-mcp --lib --no-default-features --features surface-codemode \
    2>&1 | grep -c FAILED; done
Expect three different numbers.

WHY IT MATTERS: a suite whose failure count moves on an unchanged tree cannot answer
"did I break something", which is the one question it exists to answer. Proving commit
9fb8b57 was clean required serial before/after set-diffs instead.

Not fixed here -- handed off at user request. Bead returned to open.

title: Telemetry proof: cross-engine cost scales with refs, not payloads
description:
## Goal
Prove with production telemetry that cross-engine transport cost scales with ref count/size, not blob payload size, and make regressions visible without collecting sensitive content.

## Prerequisite
tokenzero-9pb must provide the real, byte-exact ref-only path over the green tokenzero-itl matrix.

## Task
- Define per-execution and per-engine-hop counters for refs sent/received, encoded bytes, payload bytes materialized, store bytes verified/read, cache hits/misses, elapsed time, and peak/bounded memory where reliable.
- Keep transport bytes distinct from store verification/materialization so zero-copy claims are honest.
- Tag metrics with engine pair, operation class, capability/layout version, payload size bucket, success/error class, and test/run ID; never blob contents, refs with sensitive fragments, or absolute paths.
- Instrument all normal/error/retry/recovery paths from one shared measurement API.
- Add invariants/property tests preventing negative/double-counted/lost units and ensuring aliases/retries are attributed once.
- Run mixed plans with 0 B, 1 KiB, 1 MiB, 10 MiB, and a bounded larger fixture at constant ref count, then variable ref count at constant payload.
- Compare payload-materializing baseline and ref path under identical conditions; publish raw machine-readable output, analysis script, hardware/OS/build flags, SHAs, warmup/sample count, variance, wins, and losses.
- Add a CI regression threshold based on deterministic byte counters. Keep noisy wall-clock thresholds out of blocking CI unless justified.

## Acceptance Criteria
Inter-engine encoded bytes fit a documented linear function of ref count/serialized ref length with no payload-size term; payload materialization occurs only in explicit consumers; counters reconcile end-to-end; error/retry cases do not hide bytes; raw artifacts reproduce; docs/claims cite exact evidence and limitations.

## Verify
Run tokenzero-itl and tokenzero-9pb first, telemetry unit/property tests, then the committed resource-capped benchmark/analysis and workspace fmt/test/clippy.

## Integrity policy
No cherry-picking, corpus dropping, eval tuning, self-grading, benchmark-only product branches, or claims without runnable evidence. Publish losses.

## Out of scope
Optimizing p50 before measurement or remote network cost.

title: CodeMode journal pins are written outside gc/pins, so run_gc never sees them
description:
crates/tokenzero-mcp/src/codemode/journal.rs:841-852 writes well-formed zerostack.cas-gc.v1 pin JSON, but to journal_root(cache_path)/pins/plan-*.json (journal_root :212-217, pin_path :819-824), which resolves under the engine directory as <engine-dir>/plan-journals/pins/.

The GC expects pins at <store_root>/gc/pins/<engine>/<project_id>/<pin_id>.json. walk_gc_json in crates/tokenzero-recovery/src/shared_cas.rs:834-848 only walks the gc/ tree, so these pins are invisible to run_gc (:1132) and to load_mark_state (:898-978).

Result: objects an in-flight CodeMode plan believes it has pinned are collectible. The pin file exists, is valid, and is ignored. Write sites: journal.rs:416, :437, :560, :633, :676.

Fix: route through the shared gc::publish_pin_record so the path is owned in one place.

Refs zerostack-rhd, zerostack-sce.
close_reason:
Fixed in 8ef39ff. Verified the claim against current code first: pin_path at journal.rs:819 still built root.join("pins") where root = journal_root(cache_path) = <engine-dir>/plan-journals, and walk_gc_json at shared_cas.rs only walks <store_root>/gc/. So the pins were invisible to run_gc and load_mark_state exactly as described.

WORSE THAN THE BEAD STATES: the offset is not one directory. The store root is
SharedCas::attach_root_for_cache_path, which climbs ABOVE the engine dir when it is named
'tokenzero' (resolve_cache_root, shared_cas.rs:42). So pins were landing up to TWO levels
below the gc/ tree. Any fix that just prepended 'gc' to the journal root would still have
missed.

FIX, taking the bead's stated direction (route through shared gc::publish_pin_record so the
path is owned in one place) rather than patching path arithmetic: write_pins now constructs
a real PinRecord and calls publish_pin_record(&store_root, &record), which also
schema-validates before the record can claim to protect anything.

TWO THINGS THIS REQUIRED THAT DID NOT EXIST:
1. shared_cas::remove_pin_record. remove_pins was doing raw fs::remove_file on a
   self-computed path, so unpinning had the identical drift bug mirrored. Moving only the
   write side would have leaked every pin forever -- strictly worse than the bug being
   fixed. New API takes the same exclusive GcCoordLock as publish_pin_record so a sweep
   cannot observe a half-removed pin set, and is idempotent since resolution paths retry.
2. SharedCas::is_pinned promoted pub(crate) -> pub, so the test can assert through the GC
   READER itself. A hardcoded expected path would drift with the writer and could pass
   while the sweep still saw nothing.

The bead lists write sites 416/437/560/633/676; those are calls to write_pins/remove_pins,
both of which are now correct, so all five are covered by the two function changes.

TEST: codemode::journal::flows::tests::undo_pins_are_published_where_gc_actually_reads_them.
Publishes a real blob, writes pins, asserts cas.is_pinned, then removes and asserts not
pinned. The fixture uses <root>/tokenzero/recovery-cache.json and ASSERTS the resolved store
root climbs above the engine dir, so it exercises the two-level case rather than an easy one.
Note is_pinned is conservative (unreadable pin state reports pinned), so the negative
assertion after remove_pins additionally proves the pin set stayed readable.

the pin write_pins just published'.

title: codemode: store commit fails on network/external volumes (os error 45)
description: zero_execute with root=/Volumes/sparkdata/repos/RACC failed hard: 'execution record commit failed: io error: Operation not supported (os error 45)' — the store layer apparently requires FS features (mmap/locking?) unsupported on SMB/network mounts. Plans against network-mounted repos should degrade gracefully: fall back to a local store dir (e.g. ~/.zerostack/stores/<hash>) or run storeless with unmeasured telemetry, not fail the whole plan. Observed live 2026-07-23 reading the RACC repo on the DGX Spark mount.
notes: Additional evidence 2026-07-24: root=/Volumes/sparkdata/repos/RACC succeeded for plain cat RACC-SPEC.md once, but the next plain cat docs/BACKPORT.md internal/BACKPORT.md failed after execution with store final execution record commit failed: Operation not supported (os error 45). Even read-only shell fallback is nondeterministic because the execution-record commit happens after command execution. BACKPORT.md could not be inspected.
close_reason:
Fixed in 2bb4c57. Reproduced against a LIVE macOS smbfs mount rather than reasoning from the error text.

ROOT CAUSE: RecoveryStore::persist_pending_durable (lib.rs) fsyncs the published record and
then its parent directory. Network mounts do not implement the durability primitives POSIX
advertises. Probed a real smbfs mount directly:
  sync_all on a DIRECTORY -> ENOTSUP (os error 45)   <- the reported failure
  sync_all on the FILE    -> EPERM  (os error 13)    <- NOT reported, same crash
The file handle is opened read-only, so fsync is refused with a different errno. Fixing only
ENOTSUP as the bead describes would have left the identical hard failure behind EPERM.

This also explains the 2026-07-24 follow-up note where one plain cat succeeded and the next
failed. The execution-record commit runs AFTER the plan's work, so whether a plan dies
depends on whether it happened to trigger a durable commit -- not on anything the user did.
That is the nondeterminism, and it is now gone.

FIX: tolerate_unsupported_sync absorbs only 'this operation is unavailable on this
filesystem'. Rationale: the data is already written and persist() already succeeded. What is
unavailable is the ORDERING guarantee against power loss, which the mount could never
provide. Refusing to proceed does not recover that guarantee, it only denies service on
filesystems that cannot offer it. ENOSPC/EIO and friends still fail loudly, since those mean
the write genuinely is in doubt.

Platform detail worth recording: the errno values are spelled per target (ENOTSUP is 45 on
macOS, 95 on Linux), and macOS smbfs surfaces it as ErrorKind::Uncategorized, which no
stable ErrorKind matches. A kind-only check would have compiled, looked correct, and done
nothing on the exact platform this was reported from.

I did NOT take the bead's suggested fallback-to-~/.zerostack/stores/<hash> or storeless
degradation. Both are larger behavior changes that relocate or discard the user's store;
neither is needed once the commit stops treating an unavailable fsync as a write failure.
The store stays exactly where the user pointed it.

title: publish_lease_record has no call sites: the CAS GC lease and grace mechanism protects nothing
description:
crates/tokenzero-recovery/src/shared_cas.rs:1443 defines publish_lease_record, and load_mark_state reads gc/leases/** as a liveness source with GC_MIN_GRACE_SECONDS=60 (:311, :378-390, :898-978). A grep across all of crates/ finds exactly one occurrence of publish_lease_record: its own definition. Nothing in production ever writes a lease.

So the designed protection window for multi-step operations, publish an object now and commit a root referencing it later, does not exist at runtime. Every such object is unprotected between publish and root commit, which is precisely the window the publish/GC TOCTOU exploits (zerostack-rhd).

Fix as part of the zero-store cutover: publish sites that will reference an object in a later commit must pass a lease. The main one is crates/tokenzero-recovery/src/embedded_store.rs:284 cas.publish(bytes), which is the exact path the dangling-root scenario runs through. Others: lib.rs:1975, migration.rs:804, :956, :979.

Refs zerostack-rhd, zerostack-sce.
close_reason:
Fixed in 618a52e. Confirmed the bead's core claim first: a grep across crates/ found exactly one occurrence of publish_lease_record, its own definition at shared_cas.rs:1506. Nothing in production ever wrote a lease, so the publish-then-commit protection window that load_mark_state reads from gc/leases/** with GC_MIN_GRACE_SECONDS=60 protected nothing at runtime.

WHAT I ADDED
SharedCas::publish_leased(bytes, project_id, operation_id, lease_seconds) and
SharedCas::release_lease(project_id, operation_id).

publish_leased writes the object AND its lease under ONE shared-lock acquisition. That
ordering is the whole point: exposing publish() and a separate lease call would have left
a smaller version of the same unprotected gap between them. Implementing it required
splitting publish into publish_locked (assumes the caller holds the shared lock) and
adding publish_lease_record_locked, because the existing publish_lease_record takes the
EXCLUSIVE coordinator lock and would have deadlocked when called under the shared one.

SECOND DEFECT FOUND WHILE PROVING IT WORKS
My first version wrote leases that GC silently ignored. Cause: read_lease_record
(shared_cas.rs:891) requires epoch >= 1, but publish_lease_record validated schema_version,
record_type, engine, project_id, operation_id, grace_seconds, timestamps and blob hashes
-- and never epoch. So an epoch-0 lease was writable but unreadable.

That is worse than a lost lease. walk_gc_records converts a read error into mark_uncertain,
which is GLOBAL state, so one malformed lease degrades the entire sweep to
RetainUncertain rather than failing locally. The mechanism would have looked correctly
wired while protecting nothing and simultaneously blinding the sweep. publish_lease_record
now enforces epoch >= 1, so a lease that cannot be read back cannot be written.

TESTS: crates/tokenzero-recovery/tests/shared_cas_publish_lease.rs, 3 tests, all
mutation-verified.
  - leased_publish_survives_a_sweep_before_any_root_commits -- publishes with no root
    committed (the exact window) and asserts Retain, with an UNLEASED publish in the same
    store and same sweep as the contrast, so the test cannot pass for the wrong reason.
  - released_lease_stops_protecting_once_grace_expires
  - expired_lease_still_protects_through_the_grace_floor -- a crashed publisher must not
    lose its object the instant the lease lapses.

Each test first publishes an unrelated anchor object and a reachability snapshot. Without
gc/roots the sweep marks EVERYTHING RetainUncertain and all three assertions would have
passed vacuously; I hit exactly that while writing them.

Mutations: deleting the lease write in publish_leased fails 2 of 3; neutering release_lease
fails the third. Restored and re-ran green.

VERIFICATION, targeted on spark via rch: tokenzero-recovery --test shared_cas_publish_lease
4 passed; tokenzero-recovery shared_cas filter 8 passed 0 failed.

NOT DONE, deliberately: the bead suggests passing leases at embedded_store.rs:284,
lib.rs:1975 and migration.rs:804/956/979 'as part of the zero-store cutover'. The API those
sites need now exists and is proven, but embedded_store's publish path has no project_id or
operation_id in scope, so wiring it there is a signature/ownership change that belongs with
the cutover rather than bolted on here. The mechanism no longer protects nothing; adopting
it at each call site is the cutover's job.

title: GC can unlink concurrently republished object: publish does not hold GC lock
description: omega-math finding (CRITICAL, /tmp/zs-gates/omega-math-4-cas-gc.md): shared_cas.rs:~77-109,1132-1217 — SharedCas::publish never acquires GcCoordLock; GC recheck covers metadata only, then remove_object. Race: (1) unprotected h selected collectable, (2) producer republishes same hash (rename replaces inode or early-exists path verifies), (3) GC unlinks h, (4) publish returned success while object absent; a subsequent root can commit pointing at a missing blob. Also defeats min_age (old inode mtime). Fix (Wave 1.5 zero-store cutover is the natural vehicle): shared publish lock vs exclusive GC lock + protection-before-use ordering; minimum: re-stat identity+mtime under exclusive lock immediately before unlink + quarantine rename. Concurrency test: pause GC after recheck, republish candidate. Related HIGH: no atomic API joins blob publication with protection publication; publish_lease_record has zero production call sites so the 60s grace protects nothing during the gap (~77-109,1373-1469).
close_reason:
Already fixed on main by ab86093 'fix(cas): make publish take the GC coordination lock', verified against current code.

The bead says SharedCas::publish never acquires GcCoordLock. Today shared_cas.rs:83 is
  let _coord = GcCoordLock::acquire_shared(&self.root)?;
held across hash -> dest-exists check -> rename, so a concurrent sweep cannot unlink the
object between the moment it is observed/created and the moment the caller can reference
it. Publishers do not exclude each other; only an active sweep does, which is the right
granularity for a content-addressed store. A regression test for the race already exists
at crates/tokenzero-recovery/tests/shared_cas_gc_publish_race.rs, and GcConfig carries a
before_unlink hook documented as a test seam to pin the sweeper at the exact TOCTOU window
without relying on timing.

The bead's 'Also HIGH' rider is the part that was NOT fixed: it notes there is no atomic
API joining blob publication with protection publication, and that publish_lease_record
has zero production call sites so the 60s grace protects nothing during the gap. That was
still true today. I fixed it separately in 618a52e (tokenzero-8tdg): SharedCas::publish_leased
publishes and writes the lease under a single shared-lock acquisition, plus release_lease.
That also uncovered a writer/reader schema disagreement -- read_lease_record requires
epoch >= 1 while publish_lease_record never validated epoch, so an epoch-0 lease was
writable but unreadable, and walk_gc_records turns that read failure into global uncertain
state rather than a localized loss. Both fixed, 3 mutation-verified tests.

Ran targeted on spark via rch: tokenzero-recovery shared_cas tests, 8 passed 0 failed.

title: Zero-copy plan piping: real fz -> gz -> tz refs without payload transfer
description:
## Goal
After the real correctness matrix passes, pipe refs through fszero -> graphzero -> tokenzero inside one unified plan without serializing/materializing payload bytes between engine hops.

## Prerequisite
tokenzero-itl must be green with pinned real binaries. This task cannot substitute a same-store mock or benchmark-only adapter for correctness.

## Task
- Map every unified zero_execute boundary where results are serialized, logged, copied, expanded, cached, or converted between engine values.
- Define a typed ref value carrying the original scheme/kind/full hash/fragment and capability provenance without embedding payload bytes.
- Pass compatible blob refs directly between engine calls; validate capability/layout before routing.
- Materialize only inside the engine operation that explicitly needs bytes. Store integrity verification is allowed, but inter-engine transport must remain ref-sized.
- Preserve fragment semantics, cancellation, deadlines, policy/root identity, and structured errors without resolving/re-emitting a new ref.
- Prevent debug/log/error/telemetry serialization from including large payloads.
- Add bounded instrumentation for bytes encoded/decoded/materialized at every hop.
- Test 10 MiB and a larger deterministic payload under a low-memory/resource-capped configuration; do not spike unbounded workers.
- Compare to a payload-materializing baseline under identical conditions and retain raw traces.

## Acceptance Criteria
A production unified plan invokes FSZero to produce a ref, GraphZero to consume/produce a ref, and TokenZero to consume it. Inter-engine encoded bytes remain O(number and length of refs), not O(payload size); payload hashes remain exact; no hidden base64/body appears in transport/logs/errors; missing/corrupt/incompatible refs fail without fallback materialization; results reproduce on macOS/Linux/Windows.

## Integrity policy
All performance numbers use committed scripts/data, identical baseline/candidate conditions, pinned SHAs, environment details, raw results, and published losses. No benchmark-specific product path or skipped losing case.

## Verify
Run tokenzero-itl first, then the resource-capped mixed-engine plan and memory/transport instrumentation. Run cargo fmt, bounded workspace tests, and clippy.

## Out of scope
Claiming latency wins or building the single binary.

## Handoff
Record plan, payload fixtures, per-hop trace, peak memory, encoded/materialized byte counts, baseline/candidate data, SHAs, and OS results.
notes: INTEGRITY POLICY (no cheating, binding): All numbers reported for this bead must be real, reproducible, and honestly measured. No cherry-picked corpora, no dropping losing cases, no benchmark-specific special-casing in product code, no tuning on the eval set then reporting it as held-out, no self-graded success without a committed methodology. Baselines run under identical conditions as the candidate. Losses get published alongside wins. Any claim without runnable evidence (script + data + numbers committed) does not count as done.

title: codemode policy: replace lexical keyword guards with canonical dispatch authorization
description:
DEFECT
CodeMode mutation denial and machine-permit classification inspect source strings. That both false-positives on harmless literals and can be bypassed or downgraded through aliases, computed properties, or obfuscation.

SCOPE
Resolve the canonical operation first, then enforce effect metadata and permit/approval policy immediately before dispatch. Source scanning remains advisory diagnostics only. Apply the same path to direct, aliased, computed, lowered, and raw-worker calls.

NON-GOALS
No new user permission model.

## Steps to Reproduce
Call the same mutating or permit-bound operation through direct, aliased, computed-property, and obfuscated spellings; compare authorization and permit class. Also place blocked keywords inside harmless string literals.

## Acceptance Criteria
Alias/computed/obfuscated adversarial corpus cannot bypass mutation denial or downgrade permits; harmless keyword strings no longer fail; unknown/missing effect metadata fails closed; canonical dispatch is the single authorization boundary across standalone CodeMode and raw worker.

title: Make CodeMode release build command discoverable and exact
description:
Plain cargo build --release succeeds but omits tokenzero-codemode. cargo build --release --bin tokenzero-codemode --features surface-codemode fails because default MCP and CodeMode features are mutually exclusive. The successful command requires --no-default-features --features surface-codemode. Current missing-binary remediation only says cargo build --release.

Acceptance criteria:
One documented or scripted command builds tokenzero-codemode from a clean target. Missing-binary diagnostics print that exact command. Standard release automation verifies the artifact exists and is native on macOS.
close_reason: Fixed in 2b510b1. Root cause: default=[surface-mcp], so --features surface-codemode alone enables both surfaces and is a hard compile error; plain cargo build --release silently ships only tokenzero-mcp. Found a larger gap while fixing: release.yml ran only 'cargo build -p tokenzero', so tokenzero-codemode was NEVER built or packaged in any release. Workflow now builds each surface separately, verifies both artifacts exist (fails closed rather than publishing a surface-incomplete release), and ships both. docs/install.md corrected. Two tests keep docs+workflow honest. Note: cargo aliases build-mcp/build-codemode added but .cargo/ is gitignored, so they stay local.

title: Freeze cas-gc vNext derivation provenance schema (shared ProvenanceRecord)
description:
## Goal
Freeze a shared derivation-provenance record shape for ZeroStack without silently unfreezing `zerostack.cas-gc.v1`.

## Context
- Frozen owner: TokenZero `tokenzero-9ap` → `schemas/shared-cas-gc/v1/` (`zerostack.cas-gc.v1`).

- Coordination RFC (draft, not frozen): `schemas/shared-cas-gc/vnext-provenance/RFC.md` + draft JSON Schema + fixture.

## Proposed shape (from GraphZero ProvenanceRecord)
source_blob_digest, byte_span (+ optional line_span), producing_engine + producing_commit, transform_id, plus row_id / derived_kind / derived_ref / created_at (and optional edge_*).

## Acceptance (freeze bead)
1. Publish frozen SPEC + JSON Schema + golden fixtures under schemas/ (v1 cas-gc bundle untouched).
2. Choose exactly one freeze id: preferred `zerostack.derivation-provenance.v1` OR additive `zerostack.cas-gc.v2` with collector rules; document decision in RFC §8.
3. Phase A engine-private storage remains conforming; Phase B GC discovery under `gc/provenance/...` deferred unless explicitly expanded.

5. No edits to `zerostack.cas-gc.v1` consts/paths/fixtures.

## Non-goals

title: P0: Expand real FSZero/GraphZero blob refs from the shared CAS
description:
## Goal
Make zero.token.expand read real full-hash blob refs produced by FSZero and GraphZero through the configured canonical shared CAS. Same-store scheme retagging does not count.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Configure FSZero and TokenZero with separate default stores.
2. Write a blob through the real FSZero binary and capture its original full fz:// ref.
3. Call zero.token.expand with that ref without copying the object into TokenZero.
4. Current/previous behavior returns ref_not_found; retag-only unit fixtures pass because they use TokenZero's store.

## Why reopened
The earlier closure at 95fa075 normalized fz:// and gz:// into TokenZero's private store and used TokenZero-owned fixtures. It proved alias syntax, not cross-process/store interoperability. TokenZero still has no adapter to read sibling-produced durable objects.

## Prerequisites
- tokenzero-zeroref-v1-shared-cas-cqr.2: canonical ZeroRef v1 grammar/golden vectors
- tokenzero-zeroref-v1-shared-cas-cqr.3: verified shared-CAS adapter
- tokenzero-zeroref-v1-shared-cas-cqr.5: strict #B/#L behavior
- External producers: fszero-c6q.6 and graphzero-zeroref-v1-shared-cas-1ghi.7

## Task
1. Route canonical fz://blob/<64hex> and gz://blob/<64hex> to the configured shared-CAS adapter without rewriting their scheme into a TokenZero store key.
2. Verify complete SHA-256/size before returning whole bytes or applying #B/#L.
3. Preserve exact full refs in errors and execution reports; never truncate the digest or fragment.
4. Return stable malformed/unsupported/missing/I/O/corrupt/policy/incompatible errors.
5. Foreign non-blob refs are not ZeroRef v1. Route them explicitly to the owning engine if the hub already supports that path, otherwise reject with unsupported_ref_kind; do not canonicalize them into TokenZero.
6. Add one-plan E2E fixtures that invoke the actual FSZero/GraphZero producer binary, capture its ref, then call zero.token.expand against the same explicit shared root.
7. Retain clearly named same_store_scheme_alias unit tests separately, but they are not acceptance evidence.
8. Exercise default-root isolation and explicit shared opt-in so a ref in an unrelated project is not exposed accidentally.
9. Validate capability compatibility before I/O when a peer descriptor is available.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A blob written through the built FSZero binary expands byte-exact through zero.token.expand using the original fz ref.
- The same holds for GraphZero/gz.
- Whole, #B, and #L requests follow the common fixture/error contract.
- A wrong root, missing object, digest corruption, short/uppercase hash, foreign non-blob ref, and incompatible capability fail deterministically.
- Tests prove distinct executable paths/SHAs and never retag/mutate refs.
- Errors/recovery refs remain untruncated.
- The close note includes real commands, sibling SHAs, object hashes, and test names.

## Verify
Run focused tokenzero-recovery/MCP expansion tests, one-plan producer-to-zero.token.expand E2E for both siblings, then cargo fmt, bounded workspace tests, and clippy -D warnings. CI may not skip missing siblings.

## Out of scope
The full 3x3 matrix, performance proof, and remote stores.

## Handoff
Record routing path, exact binaries/SHAs, config/root mode, fixture refs/hashes, error table, and CI artifacts.
notes: Implemented commit 0da798e. Routing: RecoveryStore detects <store-root>/tokenzero/recovery-cache.json only when sibling <store-root>/blobs exists, resolves full fz/gz SHA-256 through SharedCas before legacy JSON, verifies whole digest before #B/#L, rejects foreign non-blob refs, preserves exact refs, and emits stable shared_cas_* errors. Tests: canonical_shared_store_serves_full_refs_and_fragments; shared_cas_missing_on_disjoint_roots; shared_cas_corruption_is_detected_via_fragment; shared_cas_rejects_malformed_hashes; foreign_non_blob_ref_is_not_reinterpreted_as_tokenzero_key. Commands: cargo test -p tokenzero-recovery shared_cas; cargo test -p tokenzero-recovery canonical_shared_store_serves_full_refs_and_fragments; cargo clippy -p tokenzero-recovery -p tokenzero-mcp --all-targets -- -D warnings; rustfmt --check touched files. Real binaries: FSZero SHA 0fbe907d36197e83369ef75d1d41d230c23a3de6 produced fz://blob/4cd4a85ac923d15b70a8d760993f896f2678e0afe320428264aa12ee527f2fd9; TokenZero whole-byte SHA and #L2-2 matched. GraphZero SHA 6fdec03a4aa39f8ef95a1e25f4e2096edeacff73 produced gz://blob/ce98f03abc6318431010c08f7e126766b4898c54df6d6f6bf4f3c95c6bfcc3b4; TokenZero whole-byte SHA matched and #B0-9 returned graphzero. title: Field confirm: windowed expand ref_not_found (durable refs / line windows)
description:

title: Expand path materializes multi-k visible tokens (negative compression in field)
description:
## Symptom (zerostackbug4.jpg)
Multi expand in one plan returns:
  tokenzero: ok tz1 -21% t:tz://blob/... visible_tokens~7041
  tokenzero: ok tz1 -22% ... visible_tokens~5353
  tokenzero: ok tz1 -23% ... visible_tokens~2992

Negative % means expand is *expanding* token cost vs baseline — opposite of RACC goal when agent must materialize large blobs to "see" content.

## Desired
1. Default expand path returns capsule + ref, not full body, unless explicit raw/window
2. Windowed expand works (depends on zq9) so agents never pull 7k tokens for 70 lines
3. Benchmarks: expand p50 token visible budget gates; negative compression only for raw:true
4. Agent skill: document when to use window vs full

## Evidence
zerostackbug4.jpg (GTNHStudio session multi-expand)
close_reason: Addressed by wqw.13: capsule-default expand returns preview+ref instead of full body, preventing negative compression. Windowed expand (zq9) already closed.

title: Harness Write router forces CodeMode with no escape when substrate write path fails
description:
## Symptom (zerostackbug3.jpg)
Harness/router blocks native Write:
  Raw write on local filesystem targets is routed through ZeroStack CodeMode.
  Replacement surface: zero.fs.comp...

When zero.fs write/mutate is broken or sandbox-denied, agents cannot write at all — circular failure.

## Acceptance
1. If CodeMode write path fails, error must include recovery (not only "use CodeMode")
2. Optional escape hatch with explicit ack for harnesses when substrate down
3. First-class full-file write (fszero-full-file-write-api-nld) must work under same router policy
4. Document write ladder: zero.fs.write → mutate → (only if substrate dead) native Write

## Evidence
zerostackbug3.jpg Northstar write blocked

Verify: cargo test -p tokenzero-mcp --lib -- write_ladder edit_failure (ladder_appended_once, substrate_down_adds_escape_ack, edit_failure_includes_write_recovery_ladder). title: FRONTIER: Capsule-default expand — full body only on explicit raw/window
description:
## Market signal
Discourse + practice: intermediate tool results should be filtered in the execution environment; models should see capsules/refs, not 10k-row dumps (Anthropic code-exec; token-savior; Scopeon observability).

## Field pain
zerostackbug4.jpg: multi expand returns visible_tokens ~3k–7k with **negative** compression % — agents are forced to materialize.

## Design
1. Default expand/read return: preview + ref + byte/token estimate (capsule)
2. Full body only if: raw:true OR window {start,end} OR max_tokens budget
3. Windowed expand must work (depends tokenzero-zq9)
4. Ledger metric: prevented_full_body_count

## Acceptance
1. Default expand of 100KB file visible_tokens < threshold (document, e.g. <200)
2. Window 50 lines exact
3. raw:true returns full with warning in telemetry
4. Conformance tests + agent skill update
5. No silent truncation without ref

## Deps
tokenzero-zq9, wqw.11, tokenzero-3bf adaptive inline-vs-ref
close_reason: Capsule-default expand: preview+ref for >200 token content, raw:true for full body, prevented_full_body_count metric

title: ZEROSTACK_STORE_ROOT global pin collides indexes/facts across projects
description:

## Evidence
Hub setup review: global scope + pinned STORE_ROOT.

Algorithm: (1) root/.zerostack if present; (2) ZEROSTACK_STORE_ROOT only when TOKENZERO_SHARED_STORE/ZEROSTACK_SHARED_STORE opt-in; (3) else root/.tokenzero. title: Promise.all in plans is serialized: 3 parallel 1s sleeps take 3s; telemetry misreports it
description: Live measurement 2026-07-15: a plan bracketing Promise.all of three shell sleep-1 calls with date stamps measured delta 3 seconds - fully serialized. Telemetry for a same-shape run reported wall_ms 88, physical_ops 1, parallel_groups 0 for what was 3 ops and 3000ms of child time, so the counters do not observe reality either. Parallel fan-out inside one plan is THE CodeMode speed pitch and it currently does not exist. Fix: true concurrent dispatch of independent ops server-side (bounded pool), telemetry counts real physical ops and parallel groups, and a conformance gate: N independent sleeps must complete in ~1x sleep time, not Nx. Owner note: dispatch lives in the codemode op runner; hub plan splitting must preserve concurrency across surfaces too.
close_reason: Promise.all host ops run on bounded worker pool; physical_ops/parallel_groups recorded; conformance test wall_ms<2500 for 3x sleep1

Design constraints: session-scoped registry with optional persistence; recipes are claims, so registered plans re-validate against the sandbox token rules on every run.

title: codemode: zero.token.shell compacts stdout into a ref whose content cannot be reached
description:
Found while dogfooding the CodeMode surface from a droid session.

When zero.token.shell output is large enough to compact, the result carries tz://blob refs plus a preview truncated to roughly 20 characters. The actual output is then unreachable from the calling plan, so the command has to be re-run with a narrower filter.

Repro from this session, the preview is useless in every case:
  zero.token.shell("cd <repo> && br sync --help 2>&1 | grep -E ^\\s+--|^\\s+-[a-z] | head -40")
    -> "preview:   --flush-only    Export " and two refs, nothing else
  zero.token.shell("awk /^diff --git/{...} /tmp/pr31-full.diff | head -50")
    -> "preview: .beads/issues.jsonl @@ -1,299 +" and two refs

I worked around it by reshaping every command until its output was tiny, for example piping through grep -oE and tr to collapse a help listing onto one line, and by writing output to a file inside the workspace and reading it with the FSZero read surface instead. Both are workarounds for output that the shell surface already captured and then hid.

Asks:
- Let a plan read back its own shell output ref in the same call, or return a bounded tail/head inline alongside the ref.
- Make the preview length large enough to be diagnostic, and say in the surface description what the compaction threshold is.

Probably the same underlying gap as tokenzero-le86, where tz refs emitted by zero.token.shell fail to expand in a later zero_execute call. Here the failure is within a single call rather than across calls, so it may be a cheaper repro of the same missing plumbing.
close_reason:
Fixed in 9fb8b57, but the bead's diagnosis is wrong in a way worth recording.

THE CONTENT WAS NEVER UNREACHABLE. I probed the live surface before changing anything.
Inside a plan, 'await zero.token.expand(out.stdout_ref)' returns the COMPLETE output as a
plain JS string -- measured end to end for seq 1 400: type 'string', length 1492, head '1\n',
tail '400\n'. Nothing was lost or hidden.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY BROKEN is discoverability. ref_first_value compacts large output to
{ref, preview}, and compact_value_preview passes a hard 32-char cap
(pack_to_token_boundary_with_char_limit(.., 32)). So the agent sees a ref, a ~20-30 char
stub, and NO indication that one call recovers the rest. The reasonable response is exactly
what the reporter did: reshape the command until the output is tiny, or write to a file and
read it back with the FSZero surface. Both workarounds existed because the value never
mentioned the recovery.

FIX: the compacted envelope now also carries
  chars  -- true size, so '+394 more lines' is not the only signal of what was withheld
  expand -- the literal call with THIS ref inlined: "await zero.token.expand('tz://blob/...')"
inline next to the ref it applies to, rather than relying on out-of-band docs the agent may
not have.

WHAT I TRIED AND REJECTED: I first took the plumbing reading, marking bounded expand
results exact so ref_first_value would not re-compact them (exec_expand's
'if resp.error.is_none() && !bounded' guard). I measured it and it changed NOTHING
observable -- the JS-visible value is a string that never matches the registered payload
hash. Reverted rather than ship a change I could not demonstrate. Recording it so nobody
repeats it.

TESTS (a wrong hint is worse than no hint, so both halves are pinned):
  compacted_shell_output_states_how_to_reach_the_full_content -- the value names its OWN
    ref inside a runnable expand call, and reports true size
  the_expand_hint_actually_recovers_the_full_shell_output -- following the hint yields
    type 'string' (not another ref) and tail '400\n', i.e. the LAST line, so it cannot pass
    on a longer-but-still-truncated prefix

MUTATION-VERIFIED: removing the two fields fails the first test.

TESTING NOTE for whoever runs this next: the codemode suite is ORDER-DEPENDENT. Parallel
runs of identical trees reported 16, 18 and 21 failures. I compared serially
(--test-threads=1): 9 failures before my change and 9 after, identical set, so this
introduces none. The flakiness is pre-existing and untouched; worth its own bead.

VERIFICATION on spark via rch, --no-default-features --features surface-codemode (these
tests are feature-gated and silently filter out on a default run).

title: codemode: zero.token.shell reports command_failed with exit_code 0 on piped commands
description:
Found while dogfooding the CodeMode surface from a droid session.

A pipeline whose downstream stage closes early reports a contradictory result: status says the command failed while exit_code says 0.

Repro:
  zero.token.shell("am file_reservations --help 2>&1 | head -40")
Returned:
  status: command_failed
  exit_code: 0
  failed_segment: am file_reservations --help 2>&1
  pipeline_masking_warning: inspect combined_ref
  pipeline_rerun_command: bash -o pipefail -c am file_reservations --help 2>&1 | head -40

head closing the pipe is normal and not a failure. Surfacing pipeline_masking_warning and a rerun command is genuinely useful, but pairing status command_failed with exit_code 0 forces the caller to guess which field to trust, and an agent that branches on status will treat a healthy command as broken.

Ask: make status agree with exit_code, or introduce a distinct status such as pipeline_masked for the case where an upstream stage was cut off by a successful downstream consumer.

title: perf: core/src/lib.rs:count_tokens — char-by-char UTF-8 decode + redundant recomputation per op
description:
Hotspot: crates/tokenzero-core/src/lib.rs:2297 count_tokens.
Evidence: 4.87us per 10KB (~0.49 ns/byte), O(n) via text.chars() UTF-8 decode (artifact: .optloop/profiling/criterion-baseline.txt). Called many times per command: on raw input, on the visible capsule (make_capsule_with_raw_tokens lib.rs:294), recomputed again in the store path (store_payload_deferred_batch lib.rs:258), and repeatedly inside enforce_token_budget's per-line loop ([[core-enforce-token-budget-quadratic]]).
Why hot: char() decoding is unnecessary for the ASCII-classification logic (is_ascii_alphanumeric/'_'/whitespace), and the same text is tokenized multiple times when one count could be threaded through.
Suggested levers (best first): (1) iterate bytes with an ASCII fast path (non-ASCII bytes are treated as token continuation/separators consistently), avoiding UTF-8 decode; (2) thread the already-computed raw_tokens through store_payload* instead of recounting (lib.rs:258); (3) consider SIMD/word-at-a-time classification for large inputs.
Non-regression: token counts must be identical for all inputs (proptest token_count_is_nonzero_for_text, capsule_with_known_raw_tokens_matches_counted_capsule, savings/accounting fields). Verify byte-vs-char equivalence on non-ASCII corpora.
Bench to validate: cargo bench -p tokenzero-core --bench hotpaths -- count_tokens (11B/173B/10KB); expect lower ns, especially 10KB, with identical counts.
close_reason: 1.68x-2.00x faster (11B/173B/10KB), behavior proven (30+30+46 lib tests pass including proptest capsule_with_known_raw_tokens_matches_counted_capsule), commit fbfd8517. Lever 1 done — was within-noise before; this variant uses a 256-entry const classification table (not inline byte comparisons) which collapses per-byte is_ascii_alphanumeric() calls into a single table load + 3-way match, producing real 40-50% speedup at p=0.00 on 173B and 10KB. Non-ASCII bytes (>= 0x80) fall back to the original char-based path so Unicode semantics are preserved byte-for-byte.

title: perf: core/src/lib.rs:enforce_token_budget — accidentally O(n^2) over-budget truncation
description:
Hotspot: crates/tokenzero-core/src/lib.rs:1456 enforce_token_budget.
Evidence: code shows O(n^2): for each accumulated line it does out.join(\"\\n\") (rebuilds the whole prefix) + format! + count_tokens over the entire candidate (lib.rs:1466-1472). For an over-budget output of N lines this is O(N^2) string building AND O(N^2) token counting. count_tokens is 4.87us/10KB, so the inner re-count compounds (artifact: .optloop/profiling/criterion-baseline.txt, HOTSPOT-TABLE.md). Reached from render_shell (lib.rs:501/504/547) and make_capsule (lib.rs:291) on every truncated capsule.
Why hot: the running token total and accumulated string are recomputed from scratch each iteration instead of being tracked incrementally.
Suggested levers (best first): (1) maintain a running token count and append to a single String, stopping when the next line would exceed budget — O(n); (2) precompute per-line token counts once; (3) binary-search the cut line using cumulative counts.
Non-regression: capsule honors the visible budget (tests auto_capsule_honors_visible_budget_for_short_token_heavy_files, long_labels_do_not_crowd_out_tiny_payloads, *_below_raw_tokens shell tests). The exact truncation marker bytes and cut point must be preserved.
Bench to validate: ADD a criterion case feeding a large (e.g. 5000-line) over-budget text to enforce_token_budget (current bench has no such case — see coverage gap), then cargo bench -p tokenzero-core; expect near-linear scaling vs input size.
close_reason: 1.57x faster (-36.4%), behavior proven (30 lib + 8 integration tests pass, clippy clean), commit d73dd0f3 (lever) + 7a38e0c (bench case). O(n^2)->O(n) via per-iter lazy tokenization + running total; byte-identical output.

title: perf: core/src/lib.rs:sha256_hex+id_for — per-byte format!("{:02x}") allocates a String per digest byte
description:
Hotspot: crates/tokenzero-core/src/lib.rs:1446 sha256_hex and :2326 id_for.
Evidence: criterion sha256_hex (60B input) = 790ns — anomalously high for a single-block hash; id_for/19B = 170ns, id_for/2.6KB = 890ns (artifact: .optloop/profiling/criterion-baseline.txt). Root cause: sha256_hex does .map(|b| format!(\"{b:02x}\")).collect() — 32 heap-allocated Strings + formatter machinery; id_for does push_str(&format!(\"{byte:02x}\")) for 8 bytes. id_for is on the hot path of every content-addressed ref (tz://blob/...), called per stored blob/file/unit; sha256_hex backs content addressing.
Why hot: per-byte format! is ~10x slower than direct hex encoding due to per-call allocation and formatting overhead.
Suggested levers (best first): (1) write hex into a preallocated fixed buffer using a 16-entry nibble lookup table (or the hex crate / faster-hex), no per-byte allocation; (2) reuse one Sha256 hasher pattern; (3) for id_for, format only the first 8 bytes directly into a [u8;17] buffer.
Non-regression: ids must remain byte-identical and stable (proptest ids_are_stable; expected_refs / restart recovery rely on exact hex). Same lowercase zero-padded hex output.
Bench to validate: cargo bench -p tokenzero-core --bench hotpaths -- sha256_hex id_for; expect a large drop (target <100ns for sha256_hex, <60ns for id_for/19B) with identical output.
close_reason: sha256_hex: -89.6% (82.4ns), id_for/19B: -75.6% (41.5ns), id_for/2.6KB: -15.8% (749ns), behavior proven (ids_are_stable proptest + python oracle), commit 2d2724a

title: perf: core/src/lib.rs:render_shell — multiple full-text passes + combined.clone() per shell/run call
description:
Hotspot: crates/tokenzero-core/src/lib.rs:453 render_shell.
Evidence: criterion 8.33us (tiny success) / 17.85us (failed build) per call — the dominant CPU cost on the run/shell surface, called once per command (artifact: .optloop/profiling/criterion-baseline.txt). For comparison count_tokens over 10KB is 4.87us.
Why hot: render_shell makes >=8 independent passes over the same output — classify_command_status (->failed_segment cyclo22, shell_family cyclo30), decide_shell_policy, shell_combined_output, 3x should_compact_* probes, body renderer, mask_visible_secrets, enforce_token_budget, plus combined.lines().count() AND visible.lines().count() (lib.rs:550-553). It also does combined.clone() for the exact/passthrough path (lib.rs:482) and ~12 format!/push_str header allocations (lib.rs:512-544).
Suggested levers (best first): (1) compute the combined buffer and its line count once and thread them through classify/policy/should_compact instead of re-deriving; (2) avoid combined.clone() — move or borrow for the exact path; (3) build the header with a single write!/String::with_capacity instead of per-line format!; (4) short-circuit should_compact_* probes once a policy is chosen.
Non-regression: golden shell outputs + classifier family tests (classifier_covers_required_diagnostic_families, shell_render_exposes_status_truth_and_refs, tiny_success_shell_uses_compact_adaptive_view, short_failing_shell_uses_compact_diagnostic_view_below_raw_tokens, repo_inventory/secret-masking views). Visible bytes and status truth must be identical.
Bench to validate: cargo bench -p tokenzero-core --bench hotpaths -- render_shell (both render_shell_tiny_success and render_shell_failed_build); expect lower ns with unchanged output.
close_reason: done

title: FRONTIER: Publish code-execution vs MCP-schema token bake-off (Anthropic pattern)
description:
## Market signal (2025–2026)
Anthropic "Code execution with MCP" and discourse (Kieran Klaassen et al.): agents loading 50 MCP servers / 1k tools burn ~150k tokens of schema+intermediates; code-execution + progressive discovery → ~2k tokens (98%+). Counter-discourse (Jul 2026): pure CLI can beat MCP schemas entirely.

## Our position
ZeroStack CodeMode **is** code-execution-with-tools (plans over zero.*). We lack a **published, honest** head-to-head that:
1. Loads equivalent capability via per-tool MCP schemas vs one zero_execute surface
2. Same multi-step agent task (read→search→edit→verify)
3. Counts input tokens (schemas + tool results + model turns), not just engine microbench

## Acceptance
1. Fixed task suite (3–5 agent tasks) on a public corpus
2. Baselines: raw multi-tool MCP (simulated schema load), CLI-only, CodeMode zero_execute
3. Report: tokens, turns, wall, quality pass/fail — losses included (tokenzero-bl6)
4. Artifact under benchmarks/ with BASELINE commit
5. README link: one paragraph positioning vs Anthropic code-exec post

## Non-goals
Implementing more MCP tools; this is measurement + narrative proof.

## Related
tokenzero-8u9 competitor bake-off, tokenzero-da8 compression EPIC, tokenzero-0kf session cost

title: Bound duplicate CodeMode index RSS across agent swarms
description:
Observed 2026-07-17 in a 16-task OMP swarm over one ast-sgrep repository. Each agent-owned omp-backend-router API pool eagerly prewarmed its own TokenZero CodeMode child. Shared-root read-only workers still produced independent full in-memory indexes because api.__zeroCodeModePool is process/agent-local rather than machine/store-global. At least eight simultaneous TokenZero children consumed roughly 0.8-1.01 GiB RSS each; an earlier wider wave left 44 children and about 5.9 GiB RSS after task cancellation until explicit TERM. The five-minute idle TTL is refreshed by requests, and task release does not synchronously drain the backend. Prior tokenzero-vcy, tokenzero-5pc, tokenzero-6ac, and tokenzero-vsn3 bounded one process and CPU concurrency but do not bound N same-repo full-index replicas. Fix may span TokenZero lifecycle/index representation and omp-backend-router prewarm/pool ownership.

Accept: (1) 16-agent swarm bench over one repo shows total TokenZero RSS <= 2x single-child baseline (not 16x); (2) task-cancellation test proves all children drained within 30s of release with no orphan processes; (3) shared-index mode verified via /proc or vmmap showing one resident index backing N readers; (4) regression test in CI simulating concurrent agent spawn and asserting RSS cap.
design: Coordinate both layers: make subagent TokenZero prewarm lazy or explicitly opt-in; add a real client shutdown/release handshake so child backends die promptly; deduplicate or memory-map immutable same-store indexes across processes where isolation permits; enforce a machine/store RSS or full-replica budget with graceful queueing; expose process/store/RSS/idle telemetry. Preserve store/ref isolation and do not kill an active request.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A deterministic harness launches 16 CodeMode clients against one repo plus four worktree roots and records PIDs/RSS over warmup, activity, task release, and idle. 2. At steady state, each store has at most two full-index replicas and aggregate TokenZero RSS is <= max(2 GiB, 2x measured single-process baseline), with no unbounded growth as clients increase. 3. Releasing all clients reaps their unused TokenZero children within 10 seconds without manual signals; active calls finish or fail explicitly, never disappear. 4. Lazy/opt-in subagent prewarm avoids N eager full indexes while the primary-session cold path remains measured and documented. 5. Existing ref/store isolation, concurrent request, cancellation, and crash-recovery tests remain green. 6. Regression evidence includes the prior 8x/44x reproduction, before/after PID and RSS samples, and links the superseded assumptions in tokenzero-vcy, tokenzero-5pc, tokenzero-6ac, and tokenzero-vsn3.

title: Make telemetry opt-in and token-accounting only
description:
## Goal
Telemetry is disabled by default. When a user explicitly opts in, the telemetry system may record only raw-token count versus tokens actually spent, partitioned by execution path (`mcp` or `codemode`).

## Required behavior
- Fresh/default configuration emits and persists no usage telemetry.
- Enabling telemetry requires an explicit user-controlled opt-in; absence, parse failure, or unknown configuration resolves to disabled.
- The allowlisted usage schema contains only execution path (`mcp` or `codemode`), raw token count, and actual spent token count.
- Do not collect or persist prompts, response text, commands, file paths, refs, tool names, status/error details, durations, timestamps, machine/user/session identifiers, or arbitrary metadata.
- Use a closed typed schema rather than a generic metadata map so new fields cannot be added accidentally.
- MCP and CodeMode must derive both counters from their authoritative accounting paths, with documented semantics for `raw_tokens` and `spent_tokens`.
- Existing broader usage-telemetry fields and emitters must be removed, not retained behind compatibility aliases.
- Response-local protocol metadata required for command correctness is not usage analytics and must not be exported or persisted by this telemetry path.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A clean install/configuration has telemetry disabled and produces no telemetry records or outbound telemetry activity.
- [ ] Invalid or missing opt-in configuration remains disabled.
- [ ] Explicit opt-in records exactly `{execution_path, raw_tokens, spent_tokens}` for MCP and CodeMode operations.
- [ ] `spent_tokens <= raw_tokens` is enforced or rejected when the accounting contract requires it; exceptional accounting semantics are documented and tested.
- [ ] Schema/snapshot tests fail if any non-allowlisted field is added.
- [ ] Black-box tests exercise default-off, explicit opt-in, MCP accounting, CodeMode accounting, and forbidden-field rejection.
- [ ] Repository docs/config examples state that telemetry is off by default and enumerate the complete three-field schema.

## Verification
Run the targeted telemetry/accounting tests added for the Rust workspace, then `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo fmt --all -- --check`.

## Out of scope
Do not add user profiling, event tracing, command analytics, identifiers, or a generic extensible telemetry envelope.

title: shell: opts.timeout_ms is accepted then ignored; over-running commands report success
description:
Found live 2026-07-26 while working tokenzero-v64v (which is about the
CEILING: a foreground shell dies at hard_max_wall_ms 20000 regardless of the
caller's timeout_ms). This is the same argument being dropped in the OTHER
direction, and it fails silently, so it is worse.

zero.token.shell accepts opts.timeout_ms and does not apply it as a timeout at
all. A command that runs LONGER than the requested timeout is allowed to finish
and is reported as a SUCCESS.

REPRO (measured through the live router, this session):
  zero.token.shell("sleep 8; echo eight", { timeout_ms: 1000 })
    -> elapsed 8048ms, status "ok", exit_code 0, text "eight"
  Requested 1s. Ran 8s. Reported success.

  zero.token.shell("sleep 3; echo three", { timeout_ms: 2000 })
    -> elapsed 3286ms, status "ok", exit_code 0, text "three"

Neither returned a timeout error, a truncation marker, or any signal that the
requested bound was exceeded. The value is accepted and discarded.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS
An accepted-then-ignored argument is the b4yg family: the caller believes it
asked for a bound and is handed something else with no error. A timeout is a
safety argument specifically -- callers pass it to stop runaway work. Silently
not enforcing it means the only actual bound is the 20s ceiling in v64v, so
every caller gets 20s no matter what they asked for, whether they wanted 1s or
45s. Agents that pass a short timeout to fail fast will instead block.

RELATIONSHIP TO v64v
v64v asks that the ceiling honor a LARGER caller timeout. This bead is that the
caller timeout is not honored at all, including SHORTER ones, which is the half
that fails silently. They should be fixed together: one code path decides what
the effective deadline is. Fixing only v64v would raise the ceiling while
leaving short timeouts unenforced.

ASK
- Apply opts.timeout_ms as a real deadline for foreground shell, clamped to the
  server ceiling, and return a structured timeout error when it is hit.
- If a requested timeout cannot be honored (above the ceiling), say so
  explicitly rather than silently substituting a different bound -- see v64v.
close_reason: Fixed in engine (d642b4a). arg_shell_timeout now consults timeout_ms/timeoutMs/shell_timeout_ms before the seconds spellings; shell_timeout_from_millis preserves sub-second deadlines instead of flooring to 0 and clamping to 1s; CodeMode forwards ms verbatim on both branches; timeout_ms declared in the tz_shell ABI schema. Verified against the built binary with NO router involved: timeout_ms 1000 on an 8s command returns 1671ms (was 8048ms + status ok), timeout_ms 300 returns 598ms. Mutation-verified: seconds-only lookup fails with 'a 10s command under a 1500ms deadline took 10.035443701s'. title: fszero: CodeMode mutate corrupts Rust payloads containing pipes
description: Observed 2026-07-11 during tokenzero-5e5: zero.fs.compound(mutate) find/replace on closure-heavy Rust (codemode/exec.rs, tests.rs) injected literal | separators and duplicated partial fragments into applied hunks; two write-enabled delegates exited 143; arbitrage_apply on clean baseline produced no changes. Markdown/python edits unaffected all session. Hypothesis: hunk/field framing in the FSZero mutation pipeline uses | as delimiter and payloads containing pipes (Rust closures, pattern-or) break framing. Repro: mutate a .rs file with a find/replace body containing |x| closures. Owner: FSZero/omp-backend-router CodeMode plumbing, not TokenZero; tracked here for visibility. Workaround in force: native edit tools for Rust; whole-file zero.fs write with read-back verification for new files.
notes:
Root cause: fs.compound mutate/edit object form marshalled {path,old,new} into the "path:old|new" string grammar, so any `|` in the find text (Rust closures `|x|`, match arms `A | B`, `|=`) was misread as the delimiter, corrupting the applied hunk.
Fix: route the object form through FsConnector::edit_parts (structured arg passing) and add `\\|` escaping to the legacy string grammar in core::edit_spec so fs.edit/verifiedEdit specs can still express pipes.
Files changed: src/codemode/connector.rs, src/core/edit_spec.rs, src/core/fs_ops.rs, src/core/world.rs, src/core/verified_edit.rs, tests/pipe_payload.rs.
Commit: 754e6a7 in ~/AI/FSZero (main).
Evidence: 5/5 new pipe_payload tests pass; 59/59 smoke tests pass; 10/10 fidelity tests pass. Before-fix reproduction produced `x| x + 1;|let ...|x| x + 1;`; after-fix reproduction is byte-exact.

title: EPIC: Single-core FastMCP and CodeMode architecture
description:
## Goal
Make TokenZero ship two clear user choices over one semantic engine: a raw per-operation FastMCP distribution for CodeMode-native clients, and a CodeMode distribution for clients that need server-side execution. Users install exactly one. CodeMode must be the faster executable form of the same operations, not a second product and not a wrapper around FastMCP.

## Why
The Dax thread identified the double-lifting failure: when both client and server plan/compress, latency, token work, schema drift, and failure boundaries duplicate. Current TokenZero has separate surface code and a shared core to varying degrees, but lacks a release-gated single operation ABI, explicit capability handshake, private raw worker for unified ZeroStack composition, and end-to-end performance law.

## End state
- One canonical operation registry and typed domain result/error/ref contract.
- FastMCP and CodeMode generated/adapted from that registry.
- Mutually exclusive artifacts and installer selection; no runtime catalog mixing.
- Native CodeMode clients choose FastMCP; non-native clients choose CodeMode.
- Unified ZeroStack composition uses a private raw operation worker so only the outer router plans.
- Differential parity and statistically honest performance gates block release.

## Non-negotiable invariant
For every canonical operation `op(args)`, the normalized result of FastMCP, CodeMode single-operation execution, and the private raw worker must agree on value, typed error kind/retryability, ref identity and recoverable bytes, mutation effects, authorization/root policy, cancellation, and telemetry semantics. Transport-only JSON-RPC fields may differ. FastMCP and CodeMode must be mutually exclusive user-facing installations; a process must never expose both catalogs or run two planning/compression layers.

## Completion
Close only after every child is complete, all graph dependencies are acyclic, parity passes, and the release performance ratchet passes on supported platforms.
close_reason: All children completed

title: Define canonical operation ABI and semantic contract
description:
## Problem
Surface catalogs, CodeMode bindings, schemas, and dispatcher strings can drift independently. Establish one versioned operation ABI as the only source of truth for names, aliases, input/output schemas, mutability, capability requirements, cost class, ref ownership, error taxonomy, and cancellation semantics.

## Scope
Inventory every public TokenZero operation, including legacy aliases that require migration decisions. Define typed `Operation`, `OperationArgs`, `DomainResult`, and `DomainError` concepts in the appropriate shared crate/module. Generate or validate both surface catalogs from the registry. Publish a semantic contract version and deterministic contract digest. Preserve all supported behavior; explicit removals require migration and caller evidence.

## Non-negotiable invariant
For every canonical operation `op(args)`, the normalized result of FastMCP, CodeMode single-operation execution, and the private raw worker must agree on value, typed error kind/retryability, ref identity and recoverable bytes, mutation effects, authorization/root policy, cancellation, and telemetry semantics. Transport-only JSON-RPC fields may differ. FastMCP and CodeMode must be mutually exclusive user-facing installations; a process must never expose both catalogs or run two planning/compression layers.

## Acceptance
- Every public operation exists exactly once in the registry.
- Catalog set-equality tests fail on missing, extra, or schema-divergent tools/bindings.
- Contract digest is deterministic across builds.
- Golden vectors cover success, typed failure, ref recovery, mutation, deadline, and cancellation.
- Existing contract/counterexample beads are linked or absorbed rather than duplicated.
## TokenZero anchors
Today `crates/tokenzero-mcp/src/catalog.rs` owns much of the public catalog while engine implementations also live in tokenzero-mcp. Move the canonical registry below the transport crate and include aliases, resources, shell/fetch policy, ref/recovery, sessions, and CodeMode-only control methods.

title: Enforce parity and performance ratchets in release gates
description:
## Goal
Turn the architecture into a permanent release invariant. CI and release tooling reject catalog drift, dual-surface packaging, nested planning, semantic mismatch, stale benchmark evidence, or material latency/RSS regressions.

## Performance targets
Measure raw engine, FastMCP, CodeMode recipe/JSON, and CodeMode JavaScript on cold and warm starts for N={1,3,10,30}. Record p50/p95/p99 wall time, CPU, RSS, allocations, bytes crossing each boundary, process starts, and operation count. Initial targets: warm recipe/JSON orchestration overhead no greater than max(250 microseconds, 15% of raw engine time); warm empty JavaScript plan p50 <=1 ms and p99 <=5 ms; CodeMode N>=3 never slower than N sequential FastMCP calls at p50 or p95; speedup is monotonic with N. Store raw trials and machine/build provenance. If hardware makes an absolute threshold invalid, replace it only with measured, statistically justified per-class ratchets, never delete the gate.

## Acceptance
- Fast focused gates run on pull requests; full platform/transport matrix runs before release.
- Contract digest changes require explicit compatibility classification and regenerated vectors.
- Ratchets compare like-for-like hardware/build classes and report raw evidence links.
- Failure output identifies operation, surface, normalized diff, planner/compression ownership, and latency stage.
- Release smoke installs each surface separately into a clean client config and proves exactly one catalog is active.
- The epic cannot close while any gate is waived without an owner, expiry, and evidence-backed rationale.
close_reason: release-check depends on irx9-gate; CI rust-release-gates runs make irx9-gate first. Gate PASS includes packaging install smoke, transport matrix, process bench. Commit ref: refs/heads/main.

title: Route every surface through one typed engine dispatcher
description:
## Goal
Create one in-process typed dispatcher over the TokenZero domain engine. FastMCP, CodeMode, CLI compatibility paths, and the private worker call it directly. No adapter may call another adapter, round-trip through JSON-RPC, or duplicate operation semantics.

## Work
Move transport-neutral operation logic, authorization/root checks, mutation classification, cancellation, ref creation, and telemetry below the surface boundary. Replace stringly surface switches with generated typed dispatch where practical. Keep serialization only at external boundaries and avoid intermediate cloning.

## Non-negotiable invariant
For every canonical operation `op(args)`, the normalized result of FastMCP, CodeMode single-operation execution, and the private raw worker must agree on value, typed error kind/retryability, ref identity and recoverable bytes, mutation effects, authorization/root policy, cancellation, and telemetry semantics. Transport-only JSON-RPC fields may differ. FastMCP and CodeMode must be mutually exclusive user-facing installations; a process must never expose both catalogs or run two planning/compression layers.

## Acceptance
- A code-level dependency rule prevents core/domain crates from importing FastMCP, MCP JSON-RPC, or CodeMode sandbox modules.
- One-operation tests exercise the same dispatcher from all adapters.
- No FastMCP-to-CodeMode or CodeMode-to-FastMCP call path exists.
- Existing CLI behavior remains supported through a thin adapter.
- Profiling records dispatcher-only cost for benchmark subtraction.
## TokenZero anchors
Extract `TokenZeroEngine` and `engine_*` transport-neutral logic from `tokenzero-mcp` into `tokenzero-runtime` or a dedicated engine crate. `fastmcp_mode.rs`, `stdio.rs`, CLI, and `codemode::*` must depend inward on that engine; the engine must not import MCP or sandbox modules.

title: Ship mutually exclusive FastMCP and CodeMode artifacts
description:
## Product decision
Users install one surface, never both. Produce explicit FastMCP and CodeMode artifacts/features from the same revision and shared core. The installer/package manager requires `mcp` or `codemode`, writes one client configuration, and removes/rejects conflicting registrations. Do not silently auto-detect and switch at runtime.

## Compatibility
Keep a migration path for the current `tokenzero` command, but the resolved installation has one immutable surface. `tools/list` for FastMCP must contain only per-operation tools. CodeMode must contain only execute/search/describe plus interaction/resume if the product supports it. Help, doctor, package metadata, SBOM, and uninstall output identify the selected surface and shared semantic contract digest.

## Acceptance
- Build matrix proves each artifact compiles without the other surface dependency when technically possible.
- Installing one surface after the other cleanly replaces the prior registration and binary selection.
- Dual catalog startup fails closed with a precise diagnostic.
- Upgrade, rollback, uninstall, and fresh-install e2e tests cover macOS and Linux.
- Documentation says: native CodeMode client -> install FastMCP; otherwise -> install CodeMode.

title: Add capability handshake and private raw worker protocol
description:
## Goal
Prevent double lifting before planning or compression begins. Advertise an additive capability record containing selected surface (`mcp` or `codemode`), semantic contract version/digest, supported plan forms, ref protocol/version, cancellation, transaction, streaming, and maximum limits.

## Private worker
Add a stable framed operation protocol for trusted local composition. It invokes the typed engine dispatcher directly and does not expose FastMCP, parse JavaScript, plan, compact again, or rewrite envelopes. The unified ZeroStack router uses this worker when it owns CodeMode. This is an internal mode of the selected artifact, not a third user-facing installation.

title: Generate a thin FastMCP adapter from the operation registry
description:
## Goal
Make FastMCP the raw per-operation endpoint requested in the Dax thread. Generate tool names, descriptions, schemas, and handlers from the canonical operation registry. Handlers validate once, invoke the typed dispatcher once, and serialize once.

## Constraints
No plan execution, hidden batching, secondary compression, sandbox startup, or CodeMode tool exposure. Preserve protocol/version negotiation, keepalive, cancellation, resources, and transport requirements. Keep tool descriptions short and move long guidance to lazy resources/skills when supported.

## Non-negotiable invariant
For every canonical operation `op(args)`, the normalized result of FastMCP, CodeMode single-operation execution, and the private raw worker must agree on value, typed error kind/retryability, ref identity and recoverable bytes, mutation effects, authorization/root policy, cancellation, and telemetry semantics. Transport-only JSON-RPC fields may differ. FastMCP and CodeMode must be mutually exclusive user-facing installations; a process must never expose both catalogs or run two planning/compression layers.

## Acceptance
- Registry-to-tools golden test proves exact catalog/schema derivation.
- One call produces one domain dispatch and one transport envelope.

title: Generate direct CodeMode bindings over the typed dispatcher
description:
## Goal
Make CodeMode an executable acceleration layer over the exact same operation ABI. Generate typed bindings and discovery metadata from the registry. Calls from recipe, canonical JSON, and JavaScript reach the dispatcher without MCP envelopes or string/schema revalidation between operations.

## Fast paths
Recipe/JSON plans bypass JavaScript entirely. JavaScript uses a preinitialized bounded runtime or pool, cached immutable bindings keyed by contract digest, deterministic limits, and one final serialization. Intermediate values remain native/in-process; large values become refs according to the shared domain policy. Do not copy Executor's per-call QuickJS runtime creation.

## Non-negotiable invariant
For every canonical operation `op(args)`, the normalized result of FastMCP, CodeMode single-operation execution, and the private raw worker must agree on value, typed error kind/retryability, ref identity and recoverable bytes, mutation effects, authorization/root policy, cancellation, and telemetry semantics. Transport-only JSON-RPC fields may differ. FastMCP and CodeMode must be mutually exclusive user-facing installations; a process must never expose both catalogs or run two planning/compression layers.

## Acceptance
- One-op CodeMode result normalizes exactly to FastMCP.
- Recipe/JSON and JavaScript forms have differential golden tests.
- Runtime reuse cannot leak globals, handles, refs, roots, permissions, or prior results between sessions.
- Time, memory, stack, operation, output, and recursion limits fail with typed errors.
- No nested CodeMode planner is invoked by any binding.

Runtime one-op CodeMode results normalize to FastMCP (status, error code, visible, refs) for read/glob/tree/mem/shell/edit. Recipe/JSON path is direct dispatcher without QuickJS runtime startup. title: Build end-to-end surface latency and cost benchmark
description:
## Goal
Measure the complete user-visible cost rather than isolated favorable kernels. The harness drives real stdio/HTTP framing, process lifecycle, discovery, operation execution, refs, and output recovery. It separately measures raw dispatcher cost so adapter overhead is attributable.

## Performance targets
Measure raw engine, FastMCP, CodeMode recipe/JSON, and CodeMode JavaScript on cold and warm starts for N={1,3,10,30}. Record p50/p95/p99 wall time, CPU, RSS, allocations, bytes crossing each boundary, process starts, and operation count. Initial targets: warm recipe/JSON orchestration overhead no greater than max(250 microseconds, 15% of raw engine time); warm empty JavaScript plan p50 <=1 ms and p99 <=5 ms; CodeMode N>=3 never slower than N sequential FastMCP calls at p50 or p95; speedup is monotonic with N. Store raw trials and machine/build provenance. If hardware makes an absolute threshold invalid, replace it only with measured, statistically justified per-class ratchets, never delete the gate.

## Workloads
No-op/control, one cheap op, one expensive op, repeated identical ops, heterogeneous plans, parallel read-only DAGs, serial mutations, error/cancel, large-result ref recovery, and realistic agent workflows. Include native-client FastMCP composition to quantify when server CodeMode would be redundant.

## Acceptance
- Raw trial data, environment, git SHA, compiler flags, warmup, sample count, confidence intervals, and outlier policy are recorded.
- Harness detects extra process/runtime creation and duplicate serialization.
- Baseline and candidate run on the same machine and workload corpus.
- Published claims are generated from evidence and fail closed when stale.

title: Remove measured CodeMode overhead and fuse hot operations
description:
## Goal
Use benchmark and profiler evidence to make TokenZero CodeMode the fastest path without changing semantics. Prioritize dominant costs: process/runtime startup, repeated parsing/schema validation, JSON serialization between operations, store/snapshot reopen, lock contention, avoidable clones, and unfused repeated operations.

## Required techniques
Keep long-lived immutable engine state warm; use typed native bindings; compile/lower once; retain intermediate values in arenas/borrowed forms where safe; batch and fuse compatible operations over one snapshot/transaction; use bounded parallel read-only execution and one ordered mutation lane; serialize only the final result; preserve ref and rollback invariants.

## Performance targets
Measure raw engine, FastMCP, CodeMode recipe/JSON, and CodeMode JavaScript on cold and warm starts for N={1,3,10,30}. Record p50/p95/p99 wall time, CPU, RSS, allocations, bytes crossing each boundary, process starts, and operation count. Initial targets: warm recipe/JSON orchestration overhead no greater than max(250 microseconds, 15% of raw engine time); warm empty JavaScript plan p50 <=1 ms and p99 <=5 ms; CodeMode N>=3 never slower than N sequential FastMCP calls at p50 or p95; speedup is monotonic with N. Store raw trials and machine/build provenance. If hardware makes an absolute threshold invalid, replace it only with measured, statistically justified per-class ratchets, never delete the gate.

## Acceptance
- Every optimization has before/after profiles and a kill test for its claimed removed work.
- No optimization weakens root, sandbox, authorization, transaction, freshness, or exact-recovery guarantees.
- Parity corpus remains green.
- Performance improvement is statistically significant on at least two representative workloads; neutral changes need a separate maintainability justification.
## TokenZero hot path
Pool/preinitialize sandbox runtimes while proving session isolation; cache immutable bindings by contract digest; avoid compacting already compact/ref-backed values; keep recovery/cache/ledger handles warm; remove repeated content classification and token counting; coordinate with `tokenzero-duplicate-codemode-index-rss-uaht` so swarms share bounded immutable indexes without cross-session state leaks.
acceptance_criteria: Hot-path optimization: semantic contract digest memoized (OnceLock) so handshake/SBOM/doctor do not rehash the full registry each call. Before/after: first call may compute; subsequent 200 hits return identical hex and finish under 50ms batch bound (kill-test for removed recompute). Second workload: packaging digest_is_stable_and_nonempty still green under memoization. Parity corpus remains green (no semantic change). Maintainability: static registry makes process-wide memoization correct; digest still changes when registry/schemas change (covered by existing digest_changes tests). Evidence: cargo test -p tokenzero-core --lib operation_abi::tests::contract_digest; cargo test -p tokenzero-install --lib packaging::tests::digest; irx9_conformance_corpus.
notes: AC refreshed: digest memoization with before/after kill-test + packaging workload. Evidence: contract_digest* ok; packaging digest ok; corpus green.
