title: Conformance: real 3x3 ZeroRef v1 binary/store matrix
description:
## Goal
Own the canonical, real three-binary ZeroRef v1 conformance matrix. The same bytes written by TokenZero, FSZero, or GraphZero must yield the same full SHA-256 identity and be expanded byte-exact by each other built binary.

## Why
The previous bead text allowed synthetic scheme retagging and did not require distinct processes/stores. That can pass while cross-engine use is broken. This suite is the release evidence gate for all broad interoperability claims.

## Local prerequisites
- tokenzero-zeroref-v1-shared-cas-cqr.2, tokenzero-zeroref-v1-shared-cas-cqr.3, tokenzero-zeroref-v1-shared-cas-cqr.4, tokenzero-zeroref-v1-shared-cas-cqr.5, tokenzero-zeroref-v1-shared-cas-cqr.6, tokenzero-zeroref-v1-shared-cas-cqr.7
- tokenzero-codemode-field-reliability-wqw.1: real foreign expansion through zero.token.expand
## External prerequisites
- FSZero fixture: fszero-c6q.6
- GraphZero fixture: graphzero-zeroref-v1-shared-cas-1ghi.7
The close note must identify the exact sibling commits used.

## Harness design
Commit a deterministic orchestrator that builds or receives absolute paths to the three binaries, creates isolated project roots plus one explicit shared CAS, queries each capability descriptor, and records commands/versions/commits. Each writer must use its production API/CLI, not a private test insertion path. Each reader receives the original ref unchanged and returns exact bytes separately from JSON diagnostics.

## Required matrix
For each of 3 writers x 3 readers, cover:
- empty bytes, UTF-8 text, LF/CRLF/final-unterminated text, arbitrary non-UTF-8 bytes, deterministic 10 MiB payload, and concurrent identical writes;
- full ref, #B first/last/empty window, #L first/last/multi-line;
- restart persistence and clean first invocation;
- missing object, wrong root, digest corruption, wrong bytes under requested hash, short/uppercase/malformed/ambiguous hash, range overflow/reversed/OOB, foreign non-blob ref, incompatible/disabled capability;
- two default project roots isolated, then explicit shared-root interoperability;
- legacy TokenZero migration enabled/disabled and upgraded-store smoke.

## Anti-cheating and evidence
Never retag a scheme, invoke one binary under multiple names, mock a sibling store, copy bytes directly into private stores, skip a required CI row, or accept matching text without byte/digest assertions. Record executable paths, SHAs, descriptors, original refs, expected/actual hashes/sizes, exit/error classes, OS, and commands. Do not retain secrets or arbitrary blob contents. Add a deliberate wrong-store/corruption test proving the harness catches the original false positive.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All 9 writer-reader cells pass on macOS, Linux, and Windows with no required skip.
- Identical content has exactly one full lowercase hash across engines.
- Every fragment/error/isolation/corruption row agrees with the shared fixture.
- Concurrent identical writers converge safely.
- Failure artifacts are machine-readable and reproducible.
- Sibling SHAs and capability/schema/fixture versions are pinned.
- The release claim test consumes the retained matrix artifact.

## Verify
Run the committed orchestrator from a clean temp base with CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 and test threads <=2, plus cargo fmt, bounded workspace tests, and clippy. CI commands and artifact links belong in the close note.

## Out of scope
Zero-copy/latency metrics, single-binary embedding, remote/team storage, and GC.

## Handoff
Provide one-command reproduction, matrix artifact/schema, pinned SHAs, fixture version, OS links, all failures/losses, and exact test names.

title: zero.token.expand returns silent empty object {} for valid tz refs from shell results
description: Repeated this session (2026-07-24): refs emitted by zero.token.shell results (both the result-level ref and combined_ref) frequently expand to {} with zero actions and 'savings unmeasured' telemetry on first expand in a fresh plan; retrying the identical expand alone in a new plan sometimes succeeds, sometimes stays empty (raw:true also returns {}). No error is surfaced, violating the one-round-trip self-correction contract. Distinct from le86 (recoverability): here the ref IS recoverable but expand silently no-ops when batched with other expands or called with {raw:true} on non-file blobs. Repro: shell command -> take returned blob ref -> expand two refs in one plan -> both {}. Expected: content or a structured error naming the correct call shape.
notes: CRITICAL evidence update: the {} results are NOT no-ops. A 4-call batch (2x br update, 2x br create) returned all {} with telemetry '1 action', yet ALL FOUR side effects landed on disk (beads claimed + created, verified via br show). So expand/shell results are silently dropped while actions execute — an agent retrying on {} would double-execute mutations. Severity: mutation-unsafe, not just lossy.
close_reason: Root cause: tokenzero-codemode and tokenzero-mcp had no expand subcommand and no unknown-arg guard, so 'expand --raw <ref>' fell through every packaging branch into run_stdio(), hit EOF on a non-tty stdin, and exited 0 with no output. Valid refs, garbage refs, and wrong-binary mistakes were all indistinguishable empty successes. Fixed by adding packaging::reject_non_stdio_args, called in both surface binaries after every supported subcommand returns; unknown args now exit 2 with a diagnostic naming the argument and pointing at the tokenzero CLI. Verified: new crates/tokenzero/tests/surface_arg_rejection.rs fails on the unfixed binaries (exit 0 observed) and passes after; mutation-testing the guard turns it red again; tokenzero-install 111/111; rustfmt clean on all touched files. The router's actual spawn path (--mode=codemode) is unaffected. Commit 1f5613b.

title: test-suite rationalization: failure-first authoring + verification purpose gate
description: Adopt a test-value policy across the repo instead of unbounded test accretion. Two paid skills exist for this (do NOT run them yet; adoption comes later as an explicit pass): 'failure-first-test-authoring' (aka the-setup) — a test only counts if it first fails RED for the named contract reason on today's code, then goes green from production change alone; and 'verification-purpose-gate' (proof-gate) — before shipping any test/oracle/harness, classify it as (a) session scaffolding for an AI's dev-time confidence loop or (b) a durable artifact that meaningfully verifies the shipped program; default minimal program-only. Many existing tests are category (a): they assert miniscule internals, snapshot incidental structure, or restate the implementation — they exist because an AI wrote them to convince itself, not because they catch real regressions. Work when scheduled: (1) audit the suite with the proof-gate lens, classify every test file/fn as contract-bearing vs scaffolding; (2) delete or fold scaffolding tests into the meaningful suites (deleted code, not ignored); (3) keep golden vectors, conformance corpora, equality gates, crash-safety and concurrency tests — those are the program's contract; (4) for new tests going forward, follow failure-first: prove red for the named reason before green; (5) since the shared foundation lives in zerostack, contract tests belong in the shared crates ONCE (e.g. zero-ref golden vectors) instead of duplicated per engine — engines keep only their engine-owned policy tests. Success = smaller suite with equal or better regression-catching power; every kept test can name the bug class it catches. title: EPIC: 1TP — one-token-per-action protocol for ZeroStack
description:
EPIC: 1TP — one-token-per-action protocol for ZeroStack

The 1TP program makes context cost scale with decisions made, not bytes touched. Server-side plans return decision atoms (1 token each) instead of raw payloads; refs, paths, and symbols collapse to dense ordinals; acks are silent or 1-atom; the model spends output only to deviate from predicted defaults. The protocol spans all three engines via the ZeroStack hub and is the active moonshot for the TokenZero northstar.

Rings (dependency-ordered):
- Ring 0 (foundation, ready now): 4yuq (atom harness), ewnl (tz-meter + TA registry)
- Ring 1 (durability + measurement): rg2d (RACC durability, in_progress), 84ie (pulse spend fractions), dkqk (ref ordinals), zm0i (cache-meter), fram (ACK/2 grammar)
- Ring 2 (rendering + eviction): g5hn (working-set dedup), 3zy2 (context-as-view), niuw (TZ-EVICT adapters), kw0a (prefix-stability contract), xg83 (ref emission diet), w4mj (path/symbol ordinals)
- Ring 3 (policy + optimization): onit (cache-aware eviction), qvzz (compress-vs-cache), rk22 (breakpoint optimizer), n3py (SPRT residency), epqj (warmkeeper), tw98 (USL fleet fit), gvkv (CI cost locks), k75i (cache-uptime SLO), 6aee (fleet economics), i7c7 (cross-provider matrix)
- Ring 4 (composition + frontier): 3ymb (recipe registry), 87ew (sentinel channel), d5mp (micro-plan DSL), r899 (server-side control flow), a9la (menu offers), r47f (context volumes), vko7 (session codebook), apyp (RG expansion ladder), 6mzp (COW forking), cp50 (negative-latency speculation), j20d (decision-equivalence replay), ym8g (working-set knee), 2kyt (protocol spec)

Acceptance (epic-level): (1) 1TP protocol spec (2kyt) committed to ZeroStack workspace with conformance fixtures referenced by FSZero and GraphZero; (2) replay-corpus bench shows per-session visible tokens bounded by decisions x zeta-codebook-size, not bytes touched, with Amdahl spend fractions from 84ie; (3) CI cost locks (gvkv) enforce per-op TA bounds and boot-cost locks (gvkv.1) pin sub-100-token boot; (4) cross-engine: at least one fz:// and one gz:// operation executed via 1TP ordinals through the ZeroStack hub with measured 1-token acks.

notes: Blocked after three implementation attempts. Correctness, packaging, ledger, and installed smoke pass, but acceptance fails repeated matched benchmarks. Three committed pre-fix runs show warm MCP read candidate slower by about 37 percent p50 and 18 to 24 percent p95 plus smaller CLI regressions. Commit 5f877f7 adds a disabled telemetry fast path, but a valid post-fix Spark comparison could not complete because isolated baseline release builds outlived worker budgets. Fresh cross-process replay also remains unverified. Evidence is committed in docs/pr28-acceptance-evidence.md and benchmarks/claims/pr28.
close_reason:
Closing: every acceptance criterion is now met, and the perf gate that blocked this
bead through three prior attempts is resolved. The blocker turned out to be a real
regression with a specific cause, not benchmark noise.

All PR28 commits (06643ec, 5f877f7, b2fb6dc, 8f994f1, 212e4dd, 68dadac, 4daf3d4) are
already ancestors of main, so the surviving question was purely acceptance.

AC "44 unrelated bead deferrals reverted": PASS. 4daf3d4 changed 45 records, restoring
44 deferred beads and creating this epic. Only 6 deferred beads remain today and all 6
are unrelated (u4d, suite-install-offer-1x2r, fs-write-mode-h0t, fs-write-mtime-l8e,
telemetry-ring-6s0, ref-index-supersession-rqh).

AC "MCP and CodeMode surfaces compile and pass targeted tests": PASS on spark via rch.

TWO REAL DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED WHILE VERIFYING THIS BEAD.

(1) 9e32e82 -- a hard crash, not a slowdown. Building the matched baseline revealed
that `tokenzero read --json` on current main exited 101 with zero stdout:
  capsule emission violated the omission rule: "capsule omitted bytes without a
  protected anchor, exact tz:// selector, or explicit lossy declaration"
while the pre-PR28 baseline d7b9551 returned clean JSON for the identical command.
finalize_capsule_omission's exact-ref branch pushed the recovery ref into
capsule.exact_refs but never into capsule.text, and validate_omission_rule requires it
in the TEXT. The struct field alone satisfies nobody: an agent cannot expand a ref it
cannot see. The branch asserted against itself on every budgeted read. Fixed, with 2
mutation-verified regression tests. Verified at the CLI: same command now exits 0 with
3012 bytes vs baseline 2759.

Worth stating plainly: this crash was on main and the benchmark harness is what caught
it. Any agent reading a large enough file through the CLI was getting an abort.

(2) e665af9 -- the actual warm-MCP-read regression this bead was stuck on. Rather than
guess, I ran `git bisect` across all 119 commits in d7b9551..HEAD with an automated
A/B perf test. It named 552c095 "feat: add path and symbol ordinals" as the first bad
commit. That commit hooked alias_repeated_paths_and_symbols into BOTH branches of
apply_session_visible_ref_aliases, so every response paid for it; on the no-refs branch
it additionally took a recovery-store lease and re-counted tokens over the whole visible
text before discovering there was nothing to alias. Direct measurement on the harness
fixture: 466us per call, finding zero candidates.

Fix is three changes confined to the "nothing to alias" path: a byte prefilter
(classify() only accepts values containing '/' or '::', so text with neither skips the
scan, the lease, and every tokenizer call), candidates() borrowing instead of allocating
a String per token into a BTreeMap, and computing the ordinal token floor once per
process. The prefilter is a conservative necessary condition, which is exactly what makes
it risky, so it is not justified by argument alone: two tests pin the implication
(scan-accepts => prefilter-accepts) and whole-function equivalence against the unfiltered
predicate, both mutation-verified by making the prefilter drop '/'.

PERF EVIDENCE, reporting ALL runs with no best-run cherry-picking, per the AC:
Matched alternating A/B, 5 repetitions at 20 trials then 3 at 80 trials, baseline
d7b9551 vs candidate, both release-built on spark, every sample retained.

  mcp_read_warm wall p50 BEFORE fix: +62.32 +12.55 +44.24 +57.40 +54.36  (5 of 5 slower)
  mcp_read_warm wall p95 BEFORE fix: +85.76 +47.41 +24.98 +56.01 +68.77  (5 of 5 slower)
  mcp_read_warm wall p50 AFTER  fix: +2.90 +14.95 -13.75                 (mixed sign)
  mcp_read_warm wall p95 AFTER  fix: +16.81 -2.50 -21.52                 (mixed sign)

An independent standalone driver with per-side isolated caches reproduced the same
before/after shift (+30-38% before, ~+5-8% after), so this is not an artifact of one
harness.

HONEST RESIDUALS, not smoothed over:
- `expand` still shows a small consistent p50/p95 delta (~+4 to +14%). This is NOT the
  alias hook: `expand --raw` returns bytes and never renders a capsule, and an isolated
  expand-only driver showed the candidate FASTER (-70% to -87%, baseline p50 16-34ms vs
  candidate 4.5-4.9ms). The harness measures full process launches, and measured startup
  alone is ~+11% (candidate binary is 192KB larger). So the residual is dominated by
  process startup, not by expand work.
- `version` is pure startup and swings both directions across runs.
- The harness itself documents that it does not pin CPU frequency, affinity, thermal
  state, or competing load, and that CLI wall time includes process startup. Spark sat
  at load ~3.2/20 cores throughout.
- tokenzero-engine has a flaky test, ledger::ledger_tests::concurrent_rotation_does_not_
  rotate_twice, which fails only under parallel fanout and passes in isolation and on a
  stashed tree. Not caused by these changes.

I am not claiming a universally green zero-tolerance gate at 0% noise on an unpinned
shared box; that gate flags sub-millisecond startup jitter on `version`. What the bead
actually required -- that the warm MCP read improvement be preserved and the workloads
not be systematically slower -- is met: the one workload that regressed reproducibly in
every single run is fixed and now varies in sign, and the reproducible crash discovered
along the way is fixed too.

title: Machine-wide analysis permit: Light CodeMode must not stack CPU across processes
description:
## Observed
Concurrent TokenZero CodeMode workers (zero.find / repo analysis) each burn a core. Multiple agent subagents spawn short-lived `tokenzero --mode=codemode` processes and together saturate CPU (~100%), even with no full cargo/rustc suites. Sample evidence: OMP long-lived worker + concurrent CLI CodeMode finds.

## Root cause
`crates/tokenzero-mcp/src/codemode/containment.rs` only acquires `/tmp/zerostack-codemode-heavy.permit` for HeavyShell / HeavyEstimatedCost. ExecutionClass::Light runs unconstrained across processes.

## Required fix
1. Machine-wide analysis permit for all non-Status plans (Light included). Default concurrency 1; env-overridable.
2. Shared permit path convention under /tmp/zerostack-codemode-*.permit so FSZero/GraphZero/ZeroStack hub can adopt the same contract (freeze protocol for fszero-ai-filesystem-excellence-jqf.2).
3. busy/retryable on permit contention; never silent ok.
4. Cap per-process analysis fanout defaults low (document env).
5. Targeted tests: two concurrent light plans cannot both hold the analysis permit; reclaim dead holders; status plans remain ungated.

## Verification (targeted only)
cargo test -p tokenzero-mcp containment -- --test-threads=2
notes: Follow-on: fair multi-tenant governor for 100 sessions (new bead).
close_reason: Light CodeMode now takes /tmp/zerostack-codemode-analysis.permit (default concurrency 1). Targeted containment tests pass; release binary rebuilt.

title: Expose TokenZero embeddable handle over the ZeroRef v1 shared CAS
description:
## Goal
Expose TokenZero as an embeddable library over the tested ZeroRef v1 CAS so a future single ZeroStack binary can host all engines without changing standalone behavior.

## Prerequisites
The real matrix (tokenzero-itl), canonical store (tokenzero-zeroref-v1-shared-cas-cqr.3), and sole policy/capability owner (tokenzero-zeroref-v1-shared-cas-cqr.7) must be stable first.

## Task
- Identify the smallest stable library entry point for execute/read/write/expand, policy gating, capability reporting, and recovery.
- Inject store handle, project/root identity, policy, clock, cancellation/deadline, diagnostics, and sibling adapters; do not read mutable globals/cwd implicitly after construction.
- Define ownership, Send/Sync, concurrency, shutdown/flush, panic/error boundaries, and resource limits.
- Keep standalone CLI/MCP by constructing the same library object from existing config.
- Share immutable CAS objects with sibling engines while keeping TokenZero recovery metadata/health/policy namespaced.
- Avoid transport dependencies and dependency cycles in the core library.
- Prove two independent project instances in one process cannot leak refs, caches, reports, or health.
- Add an embedded mixed-engine smoke using real adapters, not subprocess aliases or mocks for acceptance.
- Preserve capability descriptor equivalence embedded vs standalone.

## Acceptance Criteria
A single process constructs independent TokenZero instances and a shared explicit CAS handle; cross-engine blobs resolve byte-exact; default projects isolate; standalone CLI/MCP tests remain green; no mutable global/cwd/process assumption remains; shutdown/restart is deterministic; resource limits and policy are identical across modes.

## Verify
Run library/embedded/two-root/concurrency tests, standalone CLI/MCP smoke, tokenzero-itl-compatible embedded fixture, then cargo fmt, bounded workspace tests, and clippy.

## Integrity policy
Any size/latency numbers use reproducible committed methods and publish losses.

## Out of scope
Packaging/releasing the final all-engine binary.

## Handoff
Record public API, dependency graph, constructor/config mapping, isolation evidence, test names, and integration example.
notes: INTEGRITY POLICY (no cheating, binding): All numbers reported for this bead must be real, reproducible, and honestly measured. No cherry-picked corpora, no dropping losing cases, no benchmark-specific special-casing in product code, no tuning on the eval set then reporting it as held-out, no self-graded success without a committed methodology. Baselines run under identical conditions as the candidate. Losses get published alongside wins. Any claim without runnable evidence (script + data + numbers committed) does not count as done.
close_reason: done

title: perf: tokenzero-mcp/src/lib.rs:collect_search — line.contains(query) rebuilds a Two-Way StrSearcher per line (2.4M times); read_to_string validates whole files
description:
Hotspot: tokenzero-mcp/src/lib.rs:collect_search (lib.rs:1153-1206). Per file: fs::read_to_string (whole-file read + full UTF-8 validation; non-UTF-8 files are read in full then silently dropped). Per line: line.contains(query) constructs a fresh core::str::pattern::StrSearcher (Two-Way) every line. Per dir entry: root.is_file() re-stats (DirEntry::file_type from read_dir is discarded).
Evidence: macOS sample of release-perf find: StrSearcher::new is a top-5 leaf (36 samples) with CharSearcher::next_match (20) and is_contained_in (17) — the per-line matcher rebuild; __open 76 + stat 13 = the walk syscalls. Comparative (small cache, isolates walk from persist): tokenzero find src(36MB,4000f) ~108 ms vs GNU grep 161 ms vs ripgrep 54 ms vs unix cat 61 ms. Artifacts: .optloop/profiling/sample-find-16k-roots.txt, HOTSPOT-TABLE-PASS2.md.
Why hot: a brand-new substring searcher is built for every one of ~2.4M lines instead of compiling the needle once; read_to_string forces UTF-8 validation of every byte of every file (incl. binaries). NOTE: lower leverage — the walk is already ~on par with GNU grep and is NOT the per-op bottleneck (persist is). File as polish; do AFTER the persist beads.
Suggested levers (best first): (1) build a memchr::memmem::Finder::new(query.as_bytes()) ONCE in search() and thread it into collect_search; (2) read file bytes (fs::read) and scan with the Finder, deriving line numbers via memchr on newline — avoids UTF-8 validation and handles non-UTF-8 files; (3) use DirEntry::file_type() from read_dir instead of path.is_file()/is_dir() to drop one stat per entry (also applies to collect_tree/collect_glob).
Non-regression: find/grep must return identical file:line:text matches and line numbers for UTF-8 inputs (golden); must not match across line boundaries; non-UTF-8 behavior may improve but must not panic or mis-number. Oracle: tokenzero-mcp search_* tests + cli_contract.rs search cases; cargo test --workspace.
Bench to validate: hyperfine -N --warmup 3 against target/release-perf/tokenzero find TERM .optloop/profiling/corpus/src --cache-path <tiny fresh file> (small cache isolates the walk from persist); workload = 4000 files x 150 lines, needle absent (full walk) and needle in 20 files. Compare wall + sample StrSearcher::new leaf count before/after.
close_reason: wont_fix

title: Batched zero.token.shell calls in a JS loop return empty {} results
description: Session 2026-07-24: a plan looping 4x zero.token.shell('sed -n RANGE file') pushed into an array returned [{},{},{},{}] with telemetry '1 action' (only one action counted for 4 calls). Same commands issued as separate consts in one plan work. Either loops over token.shell are unsupported (then error loudly) or results are dropped. Violates one-round-trip self-correction.
notes: Same evidence as j0cn: batched calls DID execute (all 4 side effects verified on disk) but results dropped and action count reported as 1. Retry-on-empty would double-execute. Likely same root cause as j0cn — dedupe if so.
close_reason:
FIXED (counting half) in pi-stack 598de27. The results-dropped half no
longer reproduces. Recording the split rather than claiming both.

HALF 1 -- "results return empty {}": DOES NOT REPRODUCE.
Ran the bead's exact shape (4x zero.token.shell('sed -n RANGE file') pushed into
an array in a JS loop): all four returned full .text bodies, keys
text/exit_code/success/status/stdout_ref/combined_ref/raw_tokens/visible_tokens.
Also verified with 6x echo in a loop. Not fixed by me; verified not-broken.
Likely resolved with j0cn, which the bead itself flagged as the probable shared
root cause.

HALF 2 -- "telemetry '1 action' for 4 calls": REAL, and now FIXED.
Root cause: the router counted child ROUND-TRIPS, not operations. The fast path
sends an entire plan to ONE child in a SINGLE round-trip, so any batched plan
under-reported by exactly its batching factor. Confirmed by driving the live
router: N calls reported 1 for all N.

This is why it was worth fixing rather than closing as cosmetic. zerostack-4aa
wants observability of whether a session actually used ZeroStack, detected after
the fact from durable state -- and that durable state is this log. A count that
reads 1 whether the plan did 1 operation or 16 cannot support that measurement.

VERIFIED BY, WITH RESULT:
- Live router probe, before: 6-shell loop -> 1, 3 fs calls -> 1, 1 shell -> 1.
  After: 6, 3, 1, and mixed 2fs+2token -> 4. All four correct.
- Linearity: N=1..5 reports exactly N for both fs.compound('read') and
  token.shell. 1:1, no drift.
- DURABLE state, which is the part 4aa depends on: a probe running 6/3/1/4-op
  plans writes actions=[6,3,1,4] to the telemetry log. Verified the recorded
  numbers, not the rendered envelope.
- Mutation matrix: 7 mutations, each red then green on restore, covering all
  three plausible wrong answers (report dispatch = the original bug; always
  trust engine ops; always trust the static count) plus the dispatch floor,
  string/comment stripping, loop detection, and cross-surface summing.
- npm test 192/192, 0 failures (was 182/182; 10 new tests). b4yg/zez acceptance
  suite unchanged at 9/9.

DESIGN NOTE, because the obvious fix is wrong: I first used the engines'
logical_ops directly. It fixed ntn4 but broke two existing tests asserting
per-logical-operation accounting -- and they were right. Measurement showed
logical_ops counts ENGINE ops: the router lowers one zero.fs.compound('list')
into fs.ls + fs.expand, so a one-call plan reported 2, and coalescing inflated
further. The count now reports what the plan's AUTHOR wrote, using the substrate
count only when the plan contains a loop/map the static count cannot see.
Engine ops remain available as telemetry.extra.engine_ops for cost work
(ovn, 5u7), where substrate operations are the right unit.

DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE:
- The fs 'list' lowering doing two engine ops per call is not changed here; it
  is now correctly reported as 1 caller action with engine_ops recoverable.
- NOT pushed (goal doc: no push without explicit request). Consequence: this
  session's own zero_execute still reports the old count, because its router
  module was loaded at startup. Measured via a fresh process.

title: Eliminate missing-CodeMode-binary bootstrap deadlock
description:
When target cleanup removes tokenzero-codemode, zero_execute fails with missing binary and recommends cargo build --release. But zero.token.shell itself requires that missing binary, so the agent cannot run the remediation through CodeMode. Config-override mode also did not self-rebuild. This violates the one-round-trip self-correction contract.

Acceptance criteria:
A missing configured tokenzero-codemode binary triggers a bounded automatic rebuild or an executable recovery path that does not depend on that binary. The returned error includes the exact successful command, including --bin, --no-default-features, and --features. Add a clean-target integration test.
notes: Verified live 2026-07-25 after removing the developer TokenZero target tree. The configured protected origin-main binary at ~/.pi/agent/zerostack-origin-main/TokenZero/target/release/tokenzero-codemode exists, --help exits 0, and zero.token.shell recovered without the developer binary. pi-zerostack router substrates now owns exact CodeMode build args and managed config entries schedule bounded origin/main refresh/rebuild. Commit 196d296 supplies the exact --bin/--no-default-features/--features command. Remaining diagnostic/ref-CLI use of the legacy developer path is tracked separately as zerostack-j0j; it does not recreate the bootstrap deadlock for zero_execute.
close_reason: Already resolved by managed origin-main auto-rebuild and exact recovery command. Live clean-target recovery verified.

title: 1tp: cache-aware eviction + TTL scheduler
description: Eviction economics with cache terms: evict iff expected remaining requests x read-savings on reclaimed tokens exceeds the prefix rewrite cost (compile-amortization break-even). Exploit the tiered invalidation lattice: message-tier evictions preserve tools and system cache tiers. TTL selection from measured inter-request gap distribution with closed-form break-evens (Anthropic 5m write 1.25x breaks even at 2 requests, 1h write 2x at 3; OpenAI default retention now up to 24h). Batch evictions at cache breakpoints. Accept: scheduler simulation vs naive baseline on replay corpus shows billed-token reduction; ledger test proves no double-booked savings.

title: progressive disclosure audit: snippets-with-refs everywhere, full bytes only on expand
description: A-RAG (arXiv 2602.03442) core finding: hierarchical granularity (search snippets -> selective full read) is what makes agentic retrieval both cheaper AND more accurate; A-RAG Full retrieved 2.7-5.7k tokens vs 22-56k for the naive single-tool agent while scoring higher. TokenZero is the token-budget layer: audit every tool result surface to guarantee search/list hits return bounded snippets plus tz/fz/gz refs, and that nothing inlines full content when a ref would do. Add a conformance test that fails if any registered op returns unbounded content without a ref.

title: persist: unbuffered serde_json::to_writer causes write(2) syscall storm (95% of warm-op wall time)
description: PROFILED 2026-06-11 (run tests/artifacts/perf/2026-06-11-pushmax, git 4382839, M5 Max, release-perf, hyperfine n=20). write_json_to_tmp (crates/tokenzero-recovery/src/lib.rs:1047) passes a raw File to serde_json::to_writer, so every JSON fragment is its own write(2) syscall. With a real 2.9MB cache state: read = 388.5ms mean (332ms SYSTEM time) vs 36.4ms cold = 10.7x. samply: 95% of S2 samples and 83% of S4 (5MB shell run, 176ms) in serialize_str -> kernel write under RecoveryStore::persist (atos-symbolicated). Microbench: buffered write of identical bytes = 0.5ms. FIX: wrap in std::io::BufWriter (flush before sync_all). Expected: S2 ~388 -> <=50ms (~8x), S4 ~176 -> ~60ms. Every routed MCP call with non-trivial cache state pays this today.

title: Double F_FULLFSYNC per persist sets an 8ms floor on every cache write (macOS)
description: PROFILED 2026-06-11 (same run). write_json_to_tmp does file.sync_all() and sync_parent_dir() does another (lib.rs:1060,1067). On macOS sync_all = F_FULLFSYNC: measured 8.1ms p50 for the pair vs 0.5ms plain fsync (16x). The recovery cache is reconstructible working state, not a ledger; durability-vs-latency tradeoff is a policy choice. OPTIONS: plain fsync via sync_data, fsync file only (skip dir sync - rename atomicity on APFS journals metadata anyway), or env-gated durability mode. Quantify crash window before deciding. Evidence: hypothesis-ledger.md (fsync = floor not driver), python microbench in session log.

title: Multi-MB shell captures stored inline in cache JSON multiply every later persist
description: PROFILED 2026-06-11 (same run). Shell capture (default 4MB/stream) is stored as JSON string state, so every subsequent persist re-escapes and re-writes those megabytes (rank-4 multiplier on ranks 1-2). The 2.9MB production cache is largely shell payloads. CANDIDATE: store payloads above a size threshold as separate content-addressed files beside the cache (refs already content-addressed; expand path unchanged), keeping cache.json as a small index. Also shrinks rank-2 merge cost. Evidence: s4-shell-5mb.profile.json, cache composition.
notes: PARTIAL via 9edbe76: put_blob >=64KB -> content-addressed sidecar w/ hash-verified reads. files/units maps still inline (ocx/a73 own that); snapshot fully shrinks after those.
close_reason: Satisfied by commit 9edbe76 (fix+perf(recovery)): blob values >=64KB externalize to a content-addressed sidecar under the cache dir; tiny hash marker stays in cache JSON and travels journal/merge/delta untouched; expand resolves and hash-verifies the sidecar (torn/tampered => cache miss, never bad bytes); fail-open to inline on write failure. Multi-MB shell captures no longer multiply persist serialization. Code: crates/tokenzero-recovery/src/lib.rs externalize_blob_value/blob_sidecar_dir, referenced as bead tz8 in-source. Recovery lib suite green (150/150) in this session covering these paths.

title: persist() is O(total cache bytes) per call: full reload+merge+reserialize to add one ref
description: PROFILED 2026-06-11 (same run). persist() (lib.rs:701-717) re-reads and re-parses the entire cache from disk (load_state), runs full merge_states, evicts, and rewrites the whole state file - per persist, even for one new small ref. At 2.9MB state thats the bulk of the 382ms store-half of S2; scales linearly to the 8MB max_bytes default (~1s/call projection before bufwriter fix). load_state also runs twice per CLI command (store open + inside persist). CANDIDATES (one lever at a time, after perf-bufwriter-persist lands): skip reload when lock generation unchanged; append-only journal w/ compaction; persist only dirty entries; in-memory state cache keyed by file mtime. Evidence: hotspot-table.md rank 2, S2-vs-S6 differential (load+parse alone = 6.4ms).
close_reason: done

title: find: internal scanner beats the rg subprocess path at small/medium scan scale (16.2ms vs 22.6ms)

CANDIDATE: prefer the internal scanner below a scan-size threshold and only shell out to rg for large trees; or pre-spawn/reuse rg. Needs a scaling curve (scan size vs crossover point) before picking a lever.
close_reason: Measured the internal/rg crossover with isolated deterministic corpora: internal wins at 100 files, rg first wins at 1,000 and leads by 35.4% at 5,000; retained rg auto directory routing because an exact-size pre-scan erases the small-tree gain.

title: Retryable machine_permit_busy renders as success: (no binary output) plus ok ack plus savings claim
description: Live session 2026-07-15, evidence preserved in result blobs: a plan hit tokenzero err busy retryable machine_permit_busy (heavy permit /tmp/zerostack-codemode-heavy.permit held by a live process) and the hub rendered codemode:1 executed (no binary output) with footer ok tz1 99.8 pct savings basis=estimated. The plan NEVER RAN: four bead-create mutations were silently lost while the agent was told ok. Telemetry recorded result_surfaced=false yet status=ok, refs contained the literal sentinel tz://missing-envelope, and the savings ledger counted the failed call as a 99.8 pct win. Three failure classes in one: (1) retryable busy must surface as a typed retryable error or be auto-retried with backoff by the hub, never acked ok; (2) savings accounting must never credit unexecuted plans; (3) sentinel non-refs must never appear in refs arrays. Supersedes part of the diagnosis in tokenzero-result-cap-autopage-be8: collapses attributed there to result-cap overflow were at least partly permit-busy swallows. Cross-link: the single global permit file shared across ALL sessions is the resource-governor problem tracked as fszero-ai-filesystem-excellence-jqf.2; contention will be constant in swarms, which makes silent swallow catastrophic for trust. RACC rule: failures must be loud.
notes: Part of family CPU budget epic: busy must never render as ok/fake savings under ambient multi-session load.
close_reason: Busy now surfaces as isError/typed retryable error; no missing-envelope sentinel; no savings credit on unexecuted plans. TokenZero 9323680 + ZeroStack hub 7bbd67c.

title: Build a live Pulse terminal UI showing real token savings
description:
Pulse today is `tokenzero pulse stats|sync|doctor|export-jsonl|import-jsonl` --
a text report. The ask is a real terminal UI: someone runs `tokenzero pulse` and
gets animated graphs, sparklines/dither charts, and live numbers showing what
the compression runtime is actually doing for them.

This is the visible proof of the product's central claim. The savings number is
the whole pitch, and right now it is a wall of text.

CURRENT STATE (measured 2026-07-26)
  crates/tokenzero-pulse/src   3 files, 2,440 LOC
  CLI                          PulseCommand { Stats(alias status), Sync, Doctor,
                               ExportJsonl, ImportJsonl }
  TUI dependencies             NONE. No ratatui, no crossterm. This is a
                               from-scratch addition.

WHAT TO BUILD

  * A live view: raw tokens vs spent tokens over time, savings ratio, per-
    operation-class breakdown (the engine already tracks OperationClass and
    ExecutionPath).
  * Sparklines / dither charts for density in a small terminal area.
  * Animation only where it conveys change over time -- not decoration.
  * Sensible behavior when there is little or no data yet: a first-run user with
    three operations should see something honest, not a broken-looking chart.

CONSTRAINTS, and these matter more than the visuals

  * TELEMETRY IS DEFAULT OFF and must stay off. Pulse displays only what is
    already recorded locally. Building a dashboard must not become a reason to
    start collecting more, and must not nudge users toward enabling telemetry.
    See the telemetry bead: the allowlist is exactly execution_path, raw_tokens,
    spent_tokens.
  * Adding a TUI framework adds dependencies and binary size to a project whose
    entire premise is leanness. Weigh ratatui vs hand-rolled ANSI honestly, and
    record the measured binary-size delta in the bead before committing to a
    framework.
  * Must degrade gracefully: non-TTY, piped output, narrow terminals, no color
    (NO_COLOR), CI. `--json` must keep working unchanged for scripts.
  * The 50-test ship budget applies. A TUI is easy to over-test; assert on the
    data model, not on rendered pixels.

ACCEPTANCE

  * `tokenzero pulse` opens a live view; `tokenzero pulse stats --json` is
    unchanged.
  * Works in a plain terminal with no color and at 80 columns.
  * Measured binary-size delta recorded and justified.
  * No new telemetry fields.
  * Same treatment later for FSZero and GraphZero, once the shape is proven.

title: Regenerate northstar benchmarks and refresh README claim tables
description:
## Goal
After the post-v1.4.0 Unreleased CodeMode / math-review / permit batch lands (see CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]`), regenerate the northstar suite and rewrite the README benchmark tables so published numbers match current `main`.

## Why end-of-queue
Do this once as a release gate, not mid-stream while P1 beads are still moving numbers and claim-gate language. Depends on `tokenzero-f409` closing first; pull any other open P1s in before running.

## Acceptance
1. Build release `tokenzero` under swarm flock (`CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2`, `/tmp/zerostack-swarm-locks/tokenzero.lock`).
2. Run the canonical northstar rebaseline (retain history under `benchmarks/northstar/`; update `current.json` / `current.md`).
3. Update README tables that cite token counts / savings % (hero examples, six-row fixed suite, any other northstar-derived figures) from the new evidence — do not hand-wave.
4. Keep `claim_public_gate` green: README still carries the fixed-suite / non-population gate markers (`tokenzero-g3y.18`).
5. Run `python3 -m unittest benchmarks.test_rebaseline benchmarks.test_claim_public_gate` (and objective/claim checkers if present) — exit 0.
6. Append a one-line note under CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` that README/northstar numbers were refreshed (SHA).
7. Ship on `origin/main` (or a PR if release policy requires) with conventional commit mentioning this bead id.

## Out of scope

title: perf: recovery/src/lib.rs:atomic_write_json+PersistLock::acquire — triple F_FULLFSYNC per command dominates latency
description:
Hotspot: crates/tokenzero-recovery/src/lib.rs:902 atomic_write_json + :1084 PersistLock::acquire.
Evidence: every persisting CLI command takes ~25ms wall but only ~5ms CPU (19 voluntary ctx switches); '--help' floor is 1.7ms vs 'read' 24.6ms = ~23ms persist delta (artifact: .optloop/profiling/hyperfine-noop-vs-persist.log, hyperfine-surfaces.json). persist() issues 3 F_FULLFSYNC per command: lock-file sync_all (lib.rs:1108) + state-file sync_all (lib.rs:948) + parent-dir sync_all (lib.rs:955). On macOS Rust File::sync_all()=fcntl(F_FULLFSYNC); isolated microbench: 2x F_FULLFSYNC=7.83ms median vs 0.10ms unsynced on this APFS volume (artifact: .optloop/profiling/HOTSPOT-TABLE.md).
Why hot: F_FULLFSYNC is a full drive cache barrier (~4ms each here); three per command, mostly off-CPU wait. The lock-file sync_all is pure durability theater — the advisory flock provides mutual exclusion without fsync, and the file holds only a PID (debug info).
Suggested levers (best first): (1) drop the lock-file sync_all entirely (no correctness value); (2) coalesce state+dir durability to a single barrier, or skip the parent-dir fsync when rename atomicity already holds; (3) add a relaxed-durability/--no-fsync mode (or fdatasync) for the common interactive case, keeping strict mode opt-in; (4) only fsync when bytes actually changed.
Non-regression: byte-exact recovery across process restart must still hold (test restart_expand_is_byte_exact; concurrent_persistence_preserves_all_thread_payloads; persist_lock_file_is_stable_anchor_not_deleted_on_drop). Crash-consistency invariant: a torn write must never expose a partial cache.
Bench to validate: hyperfine --warmup 5 --runs 50 'tokenzero read .optloop/profiling/corpus/big.rs --cache-path <tmp>.json --json' (expect p50 toward the ~2-5ms floor); re-run cargo test -p tokenzero-recovery.
close_reason: 1.4x faster persist (30.3% faster empty, 28.4% faster merge, p<0.05), behavior proven (30/30 recovery tests), commit 633644b

title: perf: tokenzero-recovery/src/lib.rs:write_json_to_tmp — unbuffered serde_json::to_writer issues one write() syscall per JSON token on every persist
description:
Hotspot: tokenzero-recovery/src/lib.rs:write_json_to_tmp (lib.rs:957-963) — serde_json::to_writer(&mut file, state) writes directly to the OpenOptions File with no BufWriter, so serde emits a separate write() syscall for every key/string/delimiter token. Runs inside RecoveryStore::persist, which fires on EVERY read/find/tree/grep/glob/shell/ingest op.
Evidence: macOS sample (1ms) of release-perf find over the synthetic corpus, two independent runs: write (libsystem_kernel) is the #1 leaf self-time symbol (262 and 306 samples); call graph attributes it to persist -> atomic_write_json -> serde_json serialize_str/serialize_field -> write. Single find with the realistic SATURATED default cache (.tokenzero/recovery-cache.json ~1.79 MB, units 2048/2048, blobs 128/128): /usr/bin/time -l = 0.42s real, 0.07s USER, 0.31s SYS, 7.94B instructions — syscall-bound. Artifacts: .optloop/profiling/sample-find-16k-roots.txt, .optloop/profiling/samply-find-walk.txt, .optloop/profiling/HOTSPOT-TABLE-PASS2.md.
Why hot: the state JSON (up to max_bytes ~8 MB; 1.79 MB typical) is serialized to an unbuffered file -> hundreds of thousands of tiny write() syscalls per persist; sys time dominates user time per op.
Suggested levers (best first): (1) wrap the temp file in std::io::BufWriter::new(file) before serde_json::to_writer, then flush() before sync_all() — 1-line, byte-identical output; (2) or serialize to a single Vec<u8> via serde_json::to_vec and write_all once; (3) keep create_new + rename + sync_all atomicity unchanged. Orthogonal to and complements recovery-whole-state-rewrite (that reduces WHAT is serialized; this fixes HOW it is written) and redundant-blob-store.
Non-regression: recovery-cache.json bytes must be IDENTICAL before/after (BufWriter changes only buffering); expand round-trip stays byte-exact (RACC invariant); persist stays atomic (tmp -> fsync -> rename -> parent dir sync). Oracle: diff the serialized state file before/after; existing rust_cli_verification.json byte-exact expand check; cargo test -p tokenzero-recovery.
Bench to validate: cargo bench -p tokenzero-recovery --bench hotpaths (persist_empty/persist_merge) plus a NEW case persisting a state pre-filled near max_bytes (~1.79 MB, blobs at cap); count write() syscalls before/after (sudo dtruss -c, or macOS sample write-leaf count) on target/release-perf/tokenzero find TERM <corpus> --cache-path <prefilled 1.79MB cache>. Expect write-syscall count and sys-time to collapse by 1-2 orders of magnitude.
close_reason: duplicate

title: perf: recovery/src/lib.rs:store_payload_deferred_batch — stores full content as blob even for file-backed reads
description:
Hotspot: crates/tokenzero-recovery/src/lib.rs:243 store_payload_deferred_batch -> put_blob(text).
Evidence: 'read' of a 220KB on-disk file produces a 477,874-byte cache because the full file content is stored as a content-addressed blob in addition to the live file ref (artifact h1.json; .optloop/profiling/HOTSPOT-TABLE.md). The file ref alone can recover bytes from the on-disk source, so the blob copy roughly doubles cache bytes and directly inflates the persist/serialize/fsync cost (see [[tokenzero-recovery-whole-state-rewrite]]).
Why hot: byte-exact recovery is provided redundantly for file-backed content (file ref + full blob). The blob is only strictly needed when there is no stable on-disk source (ingested stdin, shell output, line/symbol slices).
Suggested levers (best first): (1) skip put_blob when a live file ref already covers the exact bytes, reconstructing the blob ref lazily from the source on expand; (2) store only a content hash + (path,range) pointer for file-backed reads; (3) keep full-blob storage only for ephemeral content (stdin/shell/slices).
Non-regression: expand must stay byte-exact AND correctly report staleness when the source file changes or is deleted (tests file_ref_reports_stale_after_source_changes, stale_check_uses_native_path_identity_before_display_path, restart_expand_is_byte_exact, line_range_payloads_skip_source_fingerprint).
Bench to validate: cache size after 'tokenzero read corpus/big.rs --cache-path <tmp>' must drop from ~478KB toward metadata-only; hyperfine the same read p50 should fall once the blob+fsync payload shrinks.
close_reason: Satisfied by beads tokenzero-a73 (BlobEntry::{Inline,FileRef} enum + migration, commit b812de4) and tokenzero-6ac (source-backed FileRef admission for >=64KiB complete-file reads, commit cf777a5 lineage): the evidence case (220KB file read producing ~478KB cache) now stores a FileRef pointer with content fingerprint + staleness revalidation. Bench evidence committed: measure_repeat_read_220kb_cache_bytes => 638 bytes (FileRef) vs 225,871 (Inline) for 8x220KB. Small/ranged payloads intentionally stay self-contained inline for staleness safety.

title: perf: recovery/src/lib.rs:persist — whole-state load+merge+serialize every store is O(cache) → O(n^2)/session
description:
Hotspot: crates/tokenzero-recovery/src/lib.rs:616 persist() -> load_state (:775) + merge_states (:820) + atomic_write_json (:902).
Evidence: a single 'read' of a 220KB file rewrites a 477,874-byte cache JSON (artifact h1.json); a stale 1.8MB cache temp was found in ~/.tokenzero. persist() re-reads+parses the ENTIRE existing cache, merges the whole map, then re-serializes the WHOLE state on every store. Cost is O(total cache size) per op; over a session of N stores it is O(N^2). merge_states also clones every ref_id in 'order' (lib.rs:848-850) each call. Artifact: .optloop/profiling/HOTSPOT-TABLE.md.
Why hot: durable cache uses a single monolithic JSON document rewritten in full per mutation; grows toward config max_bytes, so steady-state cost climbs with cache size independent of the work the command did.
Suggested levers (best first): (1) incremental/append-only persistence (append new refs to a log, compact periodically) instead of full rewrite; (2) persist only the session delta (session_refs) rather than reloading+merging the whole map; (3) avoid the order Vec full clone+dedup — use an index/IndexMap; (4) keep an in-memory state and write once at process exit rather than per store.
Non-regression: merge semantics (deferred_payloads_persist_in_one_batch, persist_compacts_duplicate_order_entries), eviction bounds (eviction_bounds_blob_count, evict_prefix_*), concurrent persistence (concurrent_persistence_preserves_all_thread_payloads), compact-JSON shape (persisted_cache_is_compact_json), byte-exact restart recovery.
Bench to validate: prepopulate a cache to ~1MB and ~5MB, then hyperfine 'tokenzero ingest .optloop/profiling/corpus/big.rs --kind blob --cache-path <prepop>.json --json' — cost must NOT scale with prepopulated cache size after the fix.
close_reason: done

title: ref-index: append-only supersession instead of rewrite compaction
description:
FlashDB append-then-invalidate: never update in place, flip status on the old record. Current shards rewrite-compact at 1MiB; a kill mid-rewrite risks the shard. Append supersession markers, reclaim whole shards past a stale-ratio threshold. Also add per-line commit marker or CRC so torn journal lines are detectable rather than silently tolerated (distinguishes crash-torn from truncated-by-bug).

Accept: (1) crash-injection test: kill process mid-rewrite, restart, zero data loss and zero orphan records; (2) torn-line CRC detection test: injected partial write is detected and reported, not silently loaded; (3) stale-ratio reclamation bench: space overhead bounded under 2x steady-state after reclamation; (4) linearizability test: concurrent mint + supersession + reclaim preserves read-your-writes.
notes: INTEGRITY POLICY (no cheating, binding): All numbers reported for this bead must be real, reproducible, and honestly measured. No cherry-picked corpora, no dropping losing cases, no benchmark-specific special-casing in product code, no tuning on the eval set then reporting it as held-out, no self-graded success without a committed methodology. Baselines run under identical conditions as the candidate. Losses get published alongside wins. Any claim without runnable evidence (script + data + numbers committed) does not count as done.

title: visible-budget prefix test is RED: footer displaces all payload lines (P01-001)
description:
Pre-existing failure on the current TokenZero working branch, unrelated to any conformance work. Confirmed by stashing my changes and re-running: it still fails with a clean tree, so it is not mine.

  cargo test -p tokenzero-core --lib
  tokens::tokenizer_tests::visible_budget_prefix_retains_every_fitting_line ... FAILED

  assertion `left == right` failed: prefix must retain all budget-fitting lines (P01-001)
    left: 1
   right: 2
  out = "[mode=lossy lossy_policy_id=tokenzero.visible-compression.v1
          lossy_spans=[{description=omitted-bytes reason=visible-budget
          recovery_may_be_needed=true}]]"

Result with my render/domain.rs and tests/shell.rs stashed: 0 passed, 1 failed, 82 filtered out. Same assertion.

Reading the output, the visible budget produced ONLY the lossy footer and dropped both content lines, where the invariant P01-001 says a line that fits the budget must be retained. So the compressor spent the entire budget on its own annotation and kept none of the payload. That is a degenerate case: the metadata displaced the data it was describing.

This is closely related to zerostack-spz, which I filed from the agent side after seeing truncated payloads with only a trailing lossy footer as warning. This test looks like the same defect caught from the inside, and it is currently RED, so the invariant is unenforced in practice.

Worth checking whether the budget accounting subtracts the footer's own token cost before deciding what fits. If it does not, any sufficiently tight budget will produce exactly this: a footer and nothing else.

Not fixing it in the same commit as the shell-render work, since it is a different subsystem (tokens/visible-budget vs render/domain) and deserves its own change. Filed so it is not silently carried.
close_reason: Fixed in 5d82ea2 (on origin/main). The declaration string was duplicated in three places and the test modelled a fourth, shorter variant: it predicted keep counts using a 14-token marker while the emitted marker costs 33, so with budget=17 the marker alone exceeded the budget and only the footer could be emitted. Now a single pub const VISIBLE_BUDGET_LOSSY_DECLARATION used by all call sites, with the test deriving its budget from that constant. 85 passed 0 failed, up from 84 passed 1 failed.

Include KV-incremental-upgrade style store-version migration hooks for future format changes.

title: EPIC: Build and adopt the shared ZeroStack test library
description:
The 50-test ship budget (tokenzero-slim-public-repo-4uql.6) only works if the
common parts of testing live somewhere shared. Today each of TokenZero, FSZero,
and GraphZero carries its own harness, fixtures, and assertion helpers, so the
same scaffolding is paid for three times and each repo's test count is inflated
by code that is not specific to it.

Build a lean, optimized shared test library in the ZeroStack repo, consumed by
all three products.

CONSTRAINTS

  * It SHIPS. Users do not download ZeroStack separately -- it rides along with
    the products. So it must stay genuinely small, and it will need repeated
    optimization passes. A bloated shared library is worse than duplication,
    because everyone pays for it.
  * It must not become a dumping ground. Only behavior needed by two or more
    products belongs here. Product-specific assertions stay with the product.
  * Changes here affect three repos at once, so its own contract must be
    stable and tested.

WHAT BELONGS

  * Harness setup: temp roots, engine construction, deterministic seeds.
  * Fixture loading and corpus helpers (this is where the removed fixtures/ and
    test-corpus/ content should land IF it is still needed -- see the dead-dirs
    bead).
  * Shared assertions: ref shapes, envelope/telemetry structure, token
    accounting.
  * Mutation-verification helpers, since every ship test must be
    mutation-verified.

WHAT DOES NOT

  * Anything asserting a single product's user-visible behavior.
  * Anything used exactly once.

ORDERING

This is a prerequisite for the 50-test budget in all three repos. It should land
first, or at least far enough for the TokenZero classification pass to know what
it can offload.

ACCEPTANCE

  * All three repos consume it; no duplicated harness code remains across them.
  * Its own test suite is small and mutation-verified.
  * Measured size impact on a shipped product is recorded, so we can tell
    whether it is earning its place.

title: irx9 surface bench panics with BrokenPipe writing to mcp-server stdin
description: Pre-existing failure, confirmed independent of any local edit: stashing all working-tree changes and rerunning still fails. `cargo test -p tokenzero --features surface-codemode --no-default-features --test irx9_surface_bench_process` fails real_process_surface_bench_records_starts_cpu_serialization at crates/tokenzero/tests/irx9_surface_bench_process.rs:260 with Os { code: 32, kind: BrokenPipe }. measure_mcp_framing() spawns `tokenzero mcp-server --allowed-root .. --cache-path ..` then writeln!()/unwrap()s into its stdin; the child has already exited so the write hits a closed pipe and the unwrap panics. Two defects: (1) the child exits when the bench expects a live stdio server, and (2) the bench unwraps a pipe write instead of surfacing the child's exit status/stderr, so the real cause is hidden behind a BrokenPipe. Fix should report child exit + stderr on write failure, then address why mcp-server exits early. Found while working tokenzero-j0cn.

title: Slim TokenZero to a shippable public repo
description:
Goal: make TokenZero a lean public CodeMode-first product while preserving a bounded migration path for existing MCP users.

SURFACE POLICY (owner decision 2026-07-27)
- tokenzero-codemode is canonical, default, and the surface used by Pi/ZeroStack.
- tokenzero-mcp becomes an explicitly named opt-in compatibility artifact, maintenance-only during a published deprecation window.
- Aggregate ZeroStack never calls either engine MCP or the standalone CodeMode planner; it uses TokenZero's planner-free raw worker.
- Engine MCP removal requires a separately approved major-version gate.

CLEANUP RULE
No silent capability loss. Each removal states whether behavior moved to shared ZeroStack infrastructure, remains product-critical, or is intentionally retired.

## Success Criteria
Default install/docs/agent instructions select CodeMode; CodeMode builds without MCP; compat builds without CodeMode and is never co-registered silently; migration and removal gates are published; the lean ship suite proves user-facing behavior with no private paths/secrets.
acceptance_criteria: Default install/docs/agent instructions select CodeMode; CodeMode builds without MCP; compat builds without CodeMode and is never co-registered silently; migration and removal gates are published; the lean ship suite proves user-facing behavior with no private paths/secrets.

title: Remove dead top-level directories
description:
Remove top-level directories that exist only as our own scaffolding. Measured
tracked-file counts 2026-07-26.

DELETE OUTRIGHT

  tools/         1 tracked file. Nothing depends on it.
  tests/         1 tracked file, and it contains ZERO `#[test]` fns -- the real
                 tests live in crates/. A top-level tests/ that holds no tests
                 is worse than no directory: it sends readers to the wrong
                 place. Note the 50-test ship suite (separate bead) will later
                 create a NEW tests/ with real content; this removal is about
                 clearing the empty shell first, so do these in order.
  test-corpus/   7 files, 72KB. Sample inputs for our own runs.
  results/       1 file, 12KB. A recorded output of a run we did. Results are
                 not source; they go stale the moment anything changes.
  fixtures/      7 files, 68KB. JSON fixtures for tests that should either be
                 inline or in the shared ZeroStack test library.
  benches/       7 files, 56KB. Superseded by benchmarks/ (which is itself being
                 rebuilt in a separate bead). Two benchmark directories is one
                 too many; confirm nothing in benches/ is uniquely referenced
                 before removing.
  schemas/       59 files, 260KB. Generated/derived JSON schemas. These are an
                 artifact of the ABI, not a hand-maintained source of truth --
                 the authority is `crates/tokenzero-core/src/operation_abi/`.
                 CHECK FIRST whether anything loads these at runtime or in CI;
                 if so, generate them into an ignored path instead of tracking
                 them.

KEEP

  package/       npm shim, 5 files -- user-facing install path.
  packaging/     homebrew + install.sh, 2 files -- user-facing install path.
  crates/        the product.
  xtask/         build tooling.

METHOD

Do not batch this into one commit. One directory per commit, each stating what
was checked. For each, before deleting:

  git grep -n '<dirname>/' -- ':!*.md' | head

and confirm no Cargo.toml, CI workflow, script, or crate references it. If
something does reference it, that reference is the bead -- fix or remove the
consumer first, then the directory.

    Baseline to compare against (tokenzero-mcp, measured 2026-07-26): 213
    passed, 4 pre-existing `tests::expand::*` failures. Zero NEW failures.
  * `git ls-files | wc -l` drops by roughly 80 files.

title: EPIC: Harden TokenZero raw-worker v2 framing, binding, and cancellation
description:
SCOPE
Adopt the shared raw-worker-v2 semantics: bounded inbound/outbound frames, request IDs, deadline/cancel control frames, root+session binding, typed errors, effect/ref metadata, and live cancellation propagation. Make search/per-call limits effective or stop advertising them.

INVARIANT
The worker dispatches canonical operations only; it contains no JavaScript planner or MCP catalog.

NON-GOALS
No aggregate sidecar implementation.

## Steps to Reproduce
Send an oversized raw-worker frame, then cancel a long search or shell request after dispatch; observe current frame/cancellation claims against actual work.

## Acceptance Criteria
Oversized/malformed frames fail before allocation beyond the bound; cancel stops a long search/shell and its process group; deadline reaches active work; handshake advertises only demonstrated capabilities; root/session/digest mismatch fails closed; shared v2 conformance and fuzz corpus pass.
acceptance_criteria: Oversized/malformed frames fail before allocation beyond the bound; cancel stops a long search/shell and its process group; deadline reaches active work; handshake advertises only demonstrated capabilities; root/session/digest mismatch fails closed; shared v2 conformance and fuzz corpus pass.
notes: Shared protocol contract: zerostack-codemode-first-execution-jgm.3. Aggregate consumer: pi-stack-l73.1.4.

title: EPIC: Stage tokenzero-mcp-compat migration and owner-gated removal
description:
SCOPE
Rename/package the legacy engine MCP surface as explicit tokenzero-mcp-compat; freeze new features; support security/correctness and migration-blocker fixes during the published window; provide warning, migration guide, switch/uninstall behavior, and feedback channel.

STAGES
Release N defaults CodeMode. N+1, no earlier than 90 days, requires explicit compat install. Removal is no earlier than 180 days and two stable releases after the split, then only in an owner-approved major.

NON-GOALS
No immediate deletion and no parity promise.

## Acceptance Criteria
Compat and CodeMode build/install separately; warnings stay off protocol stdout; supported fix classes and dated window are public; migration covers every public MCP operation; removal requires complete client matrix, 60 days without P0/P1 migration defects, corroborated low demand where opt-in data is representative, tested rollback package, major notice, and explicit owner approval.
acceptance_criteria: Compat and CodeMode build/install separately; warnings stay off protocol stdout; supported fix classes and dated window are public; migration covers every public MCP operation; removal requires complete client matrix, 60 days without P0/P1 migration defects, corroborated low demand where opt-in data is representative, tested rollback package, major notice, and explicit owner approval.

title: Rebuild benchmarks/ around claims we can defend
description:
benchmarks/ is 60 tracked files / 428KB and contains 29 Python files, many of
which are gates, reducers, and harness self-tests rather than benchmarks. It
needs to become a small suite that answers one question convincingly: how much
context does TokenZero save versus the alternatives.

WHY REBUILD RATHER THAN EDIT

Every number currently in the repo predates this round of work. Re-measuring is
required regardless, so the suite should be rebuilt around what we actually want
to show instead of carrying forward scaffolding.

REMOVE (self-tests of the harness, and gates that are not benchmarks)

  test_boot_cost.py, test_claim_public_gate.py,
  test_deployment_telemetry_gate.py, test_harness.py, test_paired_wall_gate.py,
  test_pulse_spend_analyzer.py, test_queue_arrival_gate.py, test_rebaseline.py,
  test_workload_token_gate.py
      Tests of our benchmarking scripts. Nobody downloading TokenZero needs
      them.

  check_pulse_sync_linearizability.py, claim_public_gate.py,
  deployment_telemetry_gate.py, deployment_telemetry_reducer.py,
  paired_wall_gate.py, queue_arrival_gate.py, workload_token_gate.py,
  pulse_spend_analyzer.py, rebaseline.py, __pycache__/
      Internal CI gates and analysis, not benchmarks. If any gate still guards a
      real regression, move it to scripts/ (see the scripts bead) rather than
      keeping it under benchmarks/.

  Stale recorded reports: cli-cold-read-table.md, code-exec-vs-mcp-report.md,
  competitor-bakeoff-report.md, million-line-nav-report.md
      Regenerate from the new suite; do not hand-carry old numbers.

KEEP / REBUILD

  A small set of real, runnable benchmarks with a single documented entry point.
  Candidates worth preserving in spirit: cli-cold-read, competitor-bakeoff,
  million-line-nav, code-exec-vs-mcp, boot-cost, wind_tunnel, northstar, claims.
  Consolidate; do not keep four spellings of the same measurement.

WHAT TO MEASURE

  * Token/context savings versus the alternatives named by the user: RTK, ZTK,
    LeanCTX, Headroom, and the other comparable tools.
  * CodeMode vs MCP on the same workload -- this is our own architectural claim
    and we should be able to show it.
  * Cold-read and large-repo navigation cost.

HONESTY REQUIREMENTS (non-negotiable)

  * Publish the exact command, tool version, corpus, and machine for every
    number. A benchmark that cannot be re-run by a reader is marketing.
  * Report where we LOSE or tie. A sweep where we win everything is not
    credible and will be assumed rigged.
  * Compare like with like: same corpus, same task, same measurement point. Do
    not compare our warm path against a competitor's cold path.
  * State variance across runs, not a single best-of.
  * Fix the tool versions compared and date the results.

ACCEPTANCE

  * `benchmarks/README.md` explains how to run everything with one command.
  * docs/benchmarks.md is regenerated from a real run, dated, with machine and
    versions recorded.
  * Tracked size of benchmarks/ drops substantially (target: under ~15 files).
  * Every published number is reproducible by following only the README.

title: Enforce a 50-test ship budget backed by a shared ZeroStack test library
description:
HARD RULE, committed to 2026-07-26.

Each shipped repo -- TokenZero, FSZero, GraphZero -- gets a budget of at most
50 tests in ONE top-level tests/ directory, and that suite alone must prove the
program works. Roughly 2,500 lines is the ceiling for the whole suite; 50
enormous tests defeats the purpose.

The rationale is the important part, and it is not "tests are bad":

  If we cannot prove TokenZero works in 50 tests, we have not optimized the
  code enough.

A program that needs 917 tests to be trustworthy is telling us something about
the program, not about the tests. The budget is a design forcing function: it
pushes shared behavior down into ZeroStack, collapses duplicated surfaces, and
makes each remaining test cover something structurally distinct.

CURRENT STATE (measured 2026-07-26)

  917  #[test] / #[tokio::test] functions total
  762  embedded in crates/*/src  (15 *test*.rs files, 7,838 LOC)
  155  in crates/*/tests
    0  in top-level tests/       (the directory exists and holds no tests)
  90,535 LOC of Rust in crates/

So the ship suite must be ~5% of today's test count.

THE TWO-TIER MODEL

  Tier 1 -- DEVELOPMENT tests. Stay where they are, in the crates. These are
  what you use while building: targeted, fast, run per-crate. Nobody proposes
  deleting these wholesale, and `cargo test -p <crate>` must keep working. They
  simply are not what ships.

  Tier 2 -- SHIP suite. One tests/ directory, <= 50 tests, proving end-to-end
  that the product does what it claims. This is what a user or CI runs to
  believe the release.

  Tier 3 -- SHARED. A lean, optimized test library in the ZeroStack repo,
  consumed by all three products. It ships with them (users do not download
  ZeroStack separately), so it must stay small; expect repeated optimization
  passes. Common harness code, fixtures, and assertions live here exactly once
  instead of three times.

METHOD -- classification before deletion

Do NOT start by deleting. Start by classifying all 917, because the count is
the symptom. For each test ask which of these it is:

  DUPLICATE     -- same behavior already covered elsewhere. Merge.
  SCAFFOLDING   -- pinned a refactor that is now finished. Delete.
  SHARED        -- generic harness/fixture logic. Move to ZeroStack library.
  DEV-ONLY      -- genuinely useful while developing, not proof of shipped
                   behavior. Keep in-crate as Tier 1.
  SHIP          -- proves a user-visible guarantee. Candidate for the 50.

Prefer tests that would have caught real, filed bugs. Recent evidence of what a
load-bearing test looks like: tokenzero-gpa0 (timeout_ms accepted then ignored
-- caught only by asserting elapsed wall time) and the ZeroRef v1 line-window
boundary tests.

CONSTRAINTS

  * Ship tests assert on OBSERVABLE behavior, not internals, so they survive
    refactors.
  * Every ship test must be mutation-verified: break the behavior it covers, and
    it must fail. A test that cannot fail is not one of the 50.
  * The budget is enforced mechanically, not by good intentions -- add a CI
    check (scripts/check_embedded_tests.py already exists and is adjacent to
    this) that fails the build if tests/ exceeds 50 tests or the LOC ceiling.
  * Coverage of user-visible guarantees must not regress. If cutting to 50 drops
    a guarantee, that is a signal to simplify the CODE until the guarantee is
    provable in fewer tests -- which is the entire point -- not to quietly ship
    it unproven.

ORDERING

This bead depends on the shared ZeroStack test library existing, and on the
top-level tests/ shell being cleared (dead-dirs bead). Classification can start
immediately; deletion should not.

ACCEPTANCE

  * tests/ contains <= 50 tests, <= ~2,500 LOC, and passes from a clean clone.
  * Every one is mutation-verified.
  * `cargo test -p <crate>` still works for development.
  * A written classification of all 917 exists, so the decisions are auditable
    rather than remembered.
  * CI enforces the budget.

title: Document the telemetry policy and keep the field allowlist honest
description:
POLICY (owner, 2026-07-26): telemetry is default OFF in all three products. If a
user turns it on, the ONLY thing ever recorded is raw tokens vs tokens actually
spent -- the aggregate savings number. Nothing else, ever.

FINDING: the ENGINE ALREADY DOES THIS. Verified 2026-07-26, no code change
needed:

  tokenzero-engine/src/config.rs:125   telemetry_env_enabled() is opt-in only;
                                       enables on 1/on/true/yes, default off.
  usage_telemetry.rs:65                ALLOWLISTED_FIELDS is exactly
                                       ["execution_path", "raw_tokens",
                                        "spent_tokens"]
  config.rs:267                        a test named
                                       telemetry_env_is_strict_and_default_off
                                       already pins the default.
  resolve_telemetry()                  opt-out beats opt-in at every precedence
                                       level.

So the policy is implemented. What is missing is that NOBODY CAN TELL. A user
evaluating whether to trust this has no statement to read, and "it's default
off, trust us" is exactly the claim every project makes.

THIS BEAD IS THEREFORE DOCUMENTATION + ENFORCEMENT, NOT IMPLEMENTATION.

1. README statement, plainly worded, near the top:
     - Telemetry is OFF by default.
     - If you enable it, the only fields recorded are execution_path,
       raw_tokens, spent_tokens.
     - How to turn it on (TOKENZERO_TELEMETRY=1) and how to turn it off.
     - Where the data goes and that nothing leaves the machine unless the user
       exports it.
   Name the three fields literally. A specific, checkable claim is worth more
   than a paragraph of reassurance.

2. Keep the allowlist honest over time. ALLOWLISTED_FIELDS must stay the single
   source of truth, with a test that fails if a field is added without a
   deliberate decision. The risk is not today's code -- it is someone adding a
   "harmless" field in six months.

3. Audit the OTHER two products for the same guarantee. FSZero and GraphZero
   must match; if either records more, cut it back to the same three fields.
   Do not assume parity -- check.

4. Verify no telemetry is emitted before the user has opted in, including on
   first run and during install.

ACCEPTANCE

  * README states the policy and names the three fields.
  * A test fails if ALLOWLISTED_FIELDS grows.
  * FSZero and GraphZero verified to match, or beads filed for the gap.
  * Fresh install with no env vars writes no telemetry -- verified by running
    it, not by reading the code.

title: Recovery persist store_payload superlinear

title: Offer the rest of the ZeroStack suite at install time
description:
DEFERRED ON PURPOSE -- see the timing note at the bottom. Filed now so it is not
lost.

Someone finds TokenZero on Twitter, runs the install command, and never learns
FSZero and GraphZero exist. The installer should offer the rest of the suite.

FLOW, after the MCP-vs-CodeMode surface question (see the install-choice bead):

  1. Surface: CodeMode or MCP? (existing bead, one or the other)
  2. THEN: "TokenZero is part of ZeroStack. Also install?"
       FSZero    -- <one line: what it does>
       GraphZero -- <one line: what it does>
       Neither / just TokenZero
  3. Install the chosen set on the SAME surface chosen in step 1. Mixing
     surfaces across products on one machine would be confusing and is not
     supported.

REQUIREMENTS

  * Declining must be completely frictionless and clearly non-punitive. An
    install prompt that pressures the user into extra software is the pattern
    everyone hates; do not build that. "Just TokenZero" should be the obvious,
    unpenalized path, and arguably the default on Enter.
  * Non-interactive installs must not hang: support an explicit flag/env
    (e.g. --suite=none|fszero,graphzero, ZEROSTACK_SUITE) so scripted and CI
    installs skip the prompt entirely.
  * Symmetric in all three products -- installing FSZero should offer TokenZero
    and GraphZero. Whatever mechanism is built belongs in shared code, not
    copy-pasted three times.
  * Verify each product installs standalone. The suite offer must never become
    a hidden dependency: TokenZero alone has to keep working perfectly.
  * Handle partial failure honestly. If FSZero fails to install, say so and
    leave TokenZero working, rather than rolling back everything or claiming
    success.

TIMING -- BLOCKED, DO NOT SHIP YET

FSZero and GraphZero are NOT PUBLIC yet. Shipping this now would produce an
installer that offers software nobody can download, which is worse than not
offering it. Sequence:

  1. FSZero and GraphZero become public.
  2. Both have working installers on both surfaces.
  3. Then land this.

Until then this bead stays deferred. Revisit when the other two repos go public.

ACCEPTANCE

  * Installing any one product offers the other two, on the surface already
    chosen.
  * Declining is one keystroke and installs nothing extra.
  * Non-interactive path documented and tested.
  * Each product still installs and works entirely on its own.

title: visible-budget line packing can exceed the budget on width boundaries
description: omega-math finding (HIGH, /tmp/zs-gates/omega-math-1-budgets.md): crates/tokenzero-core/src/tokens.rs:~51-63,185-190 sums ceil(chars(line)/q) per line + one separator token, but registered-model counting is ceil(total scalars/q) over the WHOLE constructed output incl. all k newlines. Falsifiers: eight 4-char lines admitted at budget 48 but output counts 49; five 7-char lines at 55 counts 56. Fix: apply the counter to the exact constructed candidate string (or prove a newline-inclusive bound). Add parameterized boundary tests (marker residues, blank lines, trailing newline) asserting C(E_b(s)) <= b. Likely the mathematical root cause behind tokenzero-6h6j territory — see also the marker-mismatch bug filed separately.
close_reason:
Fixed in 3b15aee.

CONFIRMED THE DEFECT IS REAL, but not at the coordinates the bead gives. The two stated
falsifiers do NOT reproduce on current code: eight 4-char lines at budget 48 and five
7-char lines at budget 55 both stay within budget under gpt-4o. A parameterized sweep
capped at line width 24 also found nothing, which is what made this look stale.

The mechanism in the bead is nonetheless exactly right. tokens.rs summed
ceil(chars(line)/q) per line + one separator token, while registered-model counting is
ceil(total scalars/q) over the WHOLE constructed output including all k newlines. Per-line
ceilings discard each line's fractional residue. Working the arithmetic out directly showed
the undercount only becomes a whole token once lines are wide enough and numerous enough
(first divergence around width 36 x 19 lines by pure arithmetic), so a narrow sweep cannot
see it.

REAL WITNESS, now a regression test: twelve 12-char lines at budget 64 -> counted 65.

FIX: enforce_token_budget_with_ref now measures the exact candidate string it would emit
(new assembled_tokens(prefix, marker)) instead of estimating. The admission test and the
emitted output are the same string by construction, so they cannot disagree at any width.

TESTS, as the AC requires (parameterized boundary tests asserting C(E_b(s)) <= b, covering
marker residues, blank lines, trailing newline):
crates/tokenzero-core/tests/visible_budget_model_counting.rs sweeps line widths 1..48,
line counts 1..24, budgets 1..220, plus blank-line/trailing-newline/no-trailing-newline
cases. It asserts only the invariant C(E_b(s)) <= b.

It is a SEPARATE TEST BINARY on purpose: the active tokenizer resolves once per process
from TOKENZERO_MODEL through a LazyLock, so in-crate unit tests only ever reach the default
lexical counter and structurally cannot catch a model-counting defect. It skips cleanly
when no model is set rather than passing vacuously.

Verified green under gpt-4o (O200K), gpt-4 (CL100K) and llama-3 (SentencePiece, the
non-round 3500-milli ratio) -- all three registered families.

MUTATION-VERIFIED: restoring the per-line estimate reproduces 'budget 64 exceeded: counted
65'.

SECOND PROBLEM FOUND AND FIXED: visible_budget_prefix_retains_every_fitting_line (the
P01-001 maximality guard) asserted its expectation by REPLAYING the packer's own per-line
formula. That pins the implementation instead of the property, so correcting the formula
turned it red even though the new packer keeps MORE lines (4 vs 3) while still fitting the
budget -- i.e. the test would have blocked a strict improvement. Rewritten to assert the
property directly: the kept prefix must fit the budget, and adding one more line must not.

The bead's 'or prove a newline-inclusive bound' alternative was not taken; measuring the
real candidate is strictly safer than a bound and costs nothing here.

VERIFICATION, targeted on spark via rch: tokenzero-core --lib 93 passed 0 failed;
--test visible_budget_model_counting green under three models.
