title: P0: Profile and eliminate TokenZero CPU/RAM hot spikes
description:
## Goal
Reproduce, profile, and eliminate observed TokenZero CPU and RAM hot spikes during real CodeMode/recovery usage.

## Field evidence
User reports visible workstation CPU and RAM spikes while this bead loop exercises zero_execute, zero.token.shell/read/expand, repeated recovery persistence, and cross-connector CodeMode plans.

## Task
1. Capture process-level CPU, RSS/peak RSS, allocations, and wall time for representative cold/warm CodeMode calls, large shell captures, fs.read spill+expand, and repeated recovery persists.
2. Attribute hotspots with Instruments/sample/heap or platform-equivalent evidence; distinguish TokenZero, FSZero/GraphZero child, router, compiler/test processes, and background refresh.
3. Fix shared root causes: runaway child lifecycle, repeated whole-cache parse/serialize, unbounded buffers, duplicate payload copies, busy polling, excessive indexing, or concurrency fan-out. No benchmark-only special cases.
4. Add regression benchmarks/tests with bounded CPU time and RSS for the reproduced workload; publish baseline and candidate under identical conditions.
5. Verify no correctness loss, leaks, zombie children, or throughput regression.

## Acceptance
Committed reproducible profiler harness and before/after evidence; peak RSS and CPU spike materially reduced on the exact field workload; repeated warm calls remain bounded; workspace tests/clippy/fmt pass. Follow benchmark-integrity policy tokenzero-bl6.
close_reason: Complete: committed guarded four-workload harness (benches/perf_hotspots.py + raw baseline/candidate/attribution JSON, Apple M5 Max macOS 26.5, commit f2c98d6 baseline). Root causes fixed: duplicate SHA-256 of >=64KiB payloads in sidecar externalization (lib.rs) and triple rehash of shell captures in telemetry (engine_shell.rs). Results: 5MiB shell -11.2% wall/-12.5% CPU, 3MiB ingest -9.5%/-10.0%, warm-read RSS -15.1%, 50-persist wall -12.0%; disclosed cold-read +5.9% wall noise. Budget check passes; recovery 132/132, mcp shell 10/10; leaks 0 bytes; no orphans. Workspace fmt/clippy/test deferred to final integration gate per goal contract. Commit 1e1f501.

title: Fair multi-tenant CodeMode governor: 100 sessions without CPU saturation
description:
## Goal
Support many concurrent TokenZero CodeMode sessions (target: 100) without aggregate CPU saturation. Concurrency=1 analysis permit is correct as a spike brake but not as the product default.

## Design
1. Machine-wide analysis slot pool sized from available_parallelism (default ~25% of cores, min 1, max configurable).
2. Per-process analysis fanout hard-capped (rg/find/internal walk = 1 thread by default).
3. Fair slot acquire with short busy/retry; identical in-flight plans continue to coalesce.
4. Idle MCP stdio workers must remain event-blocked (no spin).
5. Document env knobs for hosts that want stricter or looser budgets.
6. Targeted tests for slot pool fairness and per-process thread cap.

## Non-goals
Do not require cgroups for v1; keep portable flock/dir permits.
close_reason: Core-budgeted analysis slot pool (cores/4, cap 8), rg --threads 1, max_parallel_width=2, waiter backoff; 7 targeted containment tests green.

description:
## Mission for fast workers
Ship CodeMode so agents NEVER leave zero_execute for read/expand/write. This is higher leverage than another compression percent — field sessions prove expand/root/shell breakages invert the Pareto curve.

## Ordered queue (claim ONE, finish, close)

### Wave A — Expand correctness (serial; same owner OK)
1. **tokenzero-codemode-field-reliability-wqw.1** — expand accepts fz:// gz:// (no truncation)
2. **tokenzero-zq9** + **wqw.10** — windowed expand works
3. **wqw.8** — same-session tz:// expand after codemode
4. **tokenzero-itl** — shared blob identity conformance
5. **fszero-fz-ref-expand-broken-izj** — fs-side refs expandable

### Wave B — Recovery ladder (can parallel after A1 green)
6. **wqw.9** — crash-only tz_expand must unlock when expand unhealthy
7. **fszero-fszero-codemode-substrate-exit-3hd** — substrate stays up; stderr on death (fszero-woz)

### Wave C — Multi-project isolation
8. **wqw.2** + **fszero-child-root-misconfig-jjh** + **graphzero-multi-project-store-fact-isolation-p9rs**
9. **wqw.5** — allowed-roots follow call root

### Wave D — Write path agent DX
10. **fszero-full-file-write-api-nld** + sandbox (**7nl** + **ah3**)
11. **wqw.12** harness write escape only when substrate dead

### Wave E — Process hygiene
12. **wqw.4** shell timeout process-group kill (+ shell-background-inert-3vv)

## Definition of done for this HANDOFF epic
An agent on a foreign repo (e.g. CleanReplay) can in ONE zero_execute plan:
- read file via fs or token
- expand fz/tz ref (windowed)
- write full small file
- shell short command with clean timeout
without native Read/Write/shell outside CodeMode.

## Do NOT start first
Compression 99% moonshots, profile README, dependency version bumps — those are P2+ under other EPICs.

## Integrity
tokenzero-bl6 / fszero-ltr: honest numbers only.
notes: PR: https://github.com/AdityaVG13/tokenzero/pull/20

title: EPIC: Omega — context compilation, proof-carrying assembly, and protocol-native optimization
description:
EPIC: Omega — context compilation, proof-carrying assembly, and protocol-native optimization

Omega is the post-1TP research frontier: context assembly as compilation (IR + optimization passes + PGO), machine-checkable certificates on every shipped context, tiered model servicing for context faults, and silence-as-consent protocol defaults. All omega beads depend on 1TP ring 0-2 foundations (atom harness, prefix-stability, COW forking, decision-equivalence replay).

Beads: ozzf (ctxc context compiler), o96j (proof-carrying context), on1w (tiered MMU), 5u7a (context autotuner), 6cjj (counterfactual replay debugger), fi0i (live codebook negotiation), upd0 (silence-as-consent protocol), noes (protocol-native model, PARKED P4).

Acceptance (epic-level): (1) O0 vs O3 context compilation measured on replay corpus showing token/latency/decision-equivalence delta (ozzf); (2) injected certificate violations caught 100% in CI at negligible overhead (o96j); (3) context-fault servicing by cheap model with decision-equivalence verified and cost delta measured (on1w); (4) CMA-ES tuned params beat hand-set on held-out sessions with anytime-valid confidence bounds (5u7a). noes remains parked and excluded from acceptance.

title: Report CodeMode microtask limit with a corrective batch size
description:
A zero_execute audit using six independent zero.fs.compound reads failed with only sandbox final max microtasks exceeded. A twelve-operation plan failed identically. The response omitted the configured limit, observed count, and a corrected batching example, so the agent had to guess repeatedly.

Acceptance criteria:
Preflight or runtime errors report the effective microtask limit and estimated/observed count, identify which combinator expanded the count, and show a valid split or bounded-batch example. Add tests for sequential and Promise.all plans at and above the limit.
close_reason:
Stale: already implemented and verified against current code, no change needed.

Every acceptance criterion is met at crates/tokenzero-mcp/src/codemode/exec.rs:663-675. The
error the bead complains about ('only sandbox final max microtasks exceeded') is gone; the
runtime now emits:

  'sandbox: microtask cap exceeded: drained {drained} promise continuations against limit
   {max_microtasks} with no host op pending ({ops} host ops completed, {parallel_groups}
   parallel groups so far). Plan-authored promise churn drives this count - batch
   independent host calls with Promise.all (host width is capped at {max_parallel_width}),
   split the work into smaller zero_execute plans, or pass limits.max_microtasks to raise
   the cap for this call.'

Mapping to the ACs:
- effective limit -> 'against limit {max_microtasks}'
- observed count -> 'drained {drained}'
- which combinator expanded the count -> the message identifies plan-authored promise churn
  and distinguishes it from executor bookkeeping; exec.rs:659-662 explicitly RESETS the
  drain counter while a host op is pending, so the count reported can only be plan-authored
  continuations. That is the substantive fix behind the bead's confusion: six independent
  compound reads were being blamed on a budget they were not actually spending.
- valid split / bounded-batch example -> names Promise.all, the max_parallel_width cap,
  plan splitting, and the limits.max_microtasks knob.
- 'Add tests for sequential and Promise.all plans at and above the limit' -> all three exist
  and pass:
    microtask_cap_error_reports_limit_count_and_batching_fix (sequential chain ABOVE the
      cap; asserts the message names 'limit 16', 'drained 16', Promise.all, and
      limits.max_microtasks)
    promise_all_host_batch_stays_under_microtask_cap (six host ops batched via Promise.all
      UNDER the cap -- this is the one that proves the corrective advice actually works
      rather than merely being printed)
    host_shell_output_does_not_exhaust_microtask_budget

VERIFICATION on spark via rch. Note these tests are gated behind the surface-codemode
feature, so a default-feature run silently filters all 3 out and reports '0 passed' -- worth
recording, since that is exactly how this could look unimplemented. Correct invocation:
  cargo test -p tokenzero-mcp --lib --no-default-features --features surface-codemode microtask
Result: 3 passed, 0 failed.

title: EPIC: ZeroRef v1 and real cross-engine shared-CAS interoperability
description:
## Goal
Deliver TokenZero's complete side of ZeroRef v1 and replace same-store scheme retagging with verified, byte-exact interoperability across the real TokenZero, FSZero, and GraphZero binaries.

## Why
TokenZero currently rewrites fz:// and gz:// blob schemes into tz:// and looks in its own recovery store. Its IDs use a 17-character short form derived from the first eight SHA-256 bytes, its store format is TokenZero-specific, and #B can be ignored/degraded. Those behaviors cannot satisfy the public cross-engine claim. This epic establishes the shared identity/store contract, migration, truthful policy/capability surfaces, real conformance, rollout, and later performance/durability work.

## Current state
- PR17 and PR18 are merged into main with stable recovery-tool registration, server-owned limits, safer store health, Windows command resolution, strict #L OOB, and one FastMCP policy gate.
- crates/tokenzero-recovery currently canonicalizes schemes but has no foreign/shared-store adapter.
- tokenzero-itl's existing conformance description is too vague and its prior tests used synthetic scheme retagging.
- tokenzero-codemode-field-reliability-wqw.1 was closed on same-store alias behavior and must be reopened for the real fix.
- Existing tokenzero-9pb, tokenzero-485, and tokenzero-lwt cover later zero-copy, telemetry, and embedding outcomes and will be expanded rather than duplicated.

## Workstreams
1. Correct current claims and fail unsupported fragments explicitly.
2. Adopt the shared ZeroRef v1 contract and golden vectors.
3. Implement the canonical shared CAS and full-hash/legacy migration.
4. Implement strict fragments and real foreign blob expansion.
5. Preserve safe store-root compatibility and expose one versioned policy/capability descriptor.
6. Run the real three-binary matrix on macOS/Linux/Windows.
7. Prove zero-copy behavior and per-hop telemetry only after correctness.
8. Add crash-safe CodeMode mutation journaling and conservative CAS pins/GC.
9. Expose an embeddable handle and gate releases/claims on retained evidence.

## Success criteria
- All canonical blob refs use full lowercase 64-hex SHA-256 and resolve exact bytes across all three built binaries.
- Only blob refs are cross-engine; non-blob refs route explicitly or fail.
- #B is zero-based half-open; #L is one-based inclusive; all malformed/OOB cases fail without clamp/degrade.
- Reads verify complete-object integrity before fragmenting.
- Project-local isolation remains default; explicit shared roots interoperate and are diagnosable.
- Legacy short refs are deterministic, bounded, collision-safe, migratable, and removable after a documented window.
- Tool registration/list/call/recovery/capability behavior derives from one policy owner.
- Cross-engine performance claims have reproducible raw evidence after the correctness matrix passes.
- CAS GC never removes live objects from any engine.

## Constraints
Do not retag refs in conformance tests, prefix-match silently, fake sibling binaries, weaken corruption errors, expose secrets/private paths, or claim transactionality for arbitrary shell side effects. Preserve standalone CLI/MCP behavior and existing data through explicit migration/rollback.

## Verification baseline
Rust changes require cargo fmt --all -- --check, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 cargo test --workspace -- --test-threads=2, and CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings. Cross-repo tests pin sibling SHAs and retain OS artifacts. Benchmark claims retain scripts, data, environment, raw results, and losses.

## Handoff
Close only when all correctness/release children are complete. P2 performance, embedding, journal, and GC children may remain as explicitly tracked follow-ons, but no broad claim may outrun tokenzero-itl and the release gate.
close_reason: done

title: P0: Make current TokenZero ref claims and #B behavior truthful
description:
## Goal
Stop advertising real cross-engine expansion before it exists and prevent unsupported #B fragments from silently returning the wrong payload.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Store any TokenZero recovery blob and request its ref with a #B0-1 fragment.
2. Observe that unsupported #B may be dropped/degraded and the full payload can be returned.
3. Retag a TokenZero-owned ref as fz:// or gz:// and observe it resolves only because lookup is still against the TokenZero store.
4. Write the same bytes through an isolated sibling binary/store and observe TokenZero cannot resolve that original foreign ref.

## Current evidence
crates/tokenzero-recovery/src/lib.rs currently normalizes fz:// and gz:// blob schemes into tz:// and looks up the TokenZero store. This is a same-store alias, not a foreign-store adapter. TokenZero emits a 17-character short ID based on the first eight SHA-256 bytes, not the full ZeroRef v1 identity. #L is supported, but #B can be ignored/degraded to a full result. Existing cross-scheme tests retag TokenZero-owned fixtures.

## Task
1. Audit README, docs/core.md, docs/mcp.md, tool catalogs/schemas, CLI help, errors, examples, and tests for cross-engine claims.
2. Describe current fz/gz acceptance precisely as scheme aliases over objects already present in the effective TokenZero store.
3. Remove or qualify wording that says refs written by FSZero/GraphZero resolve until tokenzero-itl passes with real binaries.
4. Detect #B before store lookup and return stable unsupported_fragment with the complete untruncated ref and remediation; never return the whole blob.
5. State that current short IDs are TokenZero legacy refs, not portable full SHA-256 ZeroRef v1 IDs.
6. Replace tests whose only proof is scheme substitution with tests explicitly named same_store_scheme_alias; add a negative fixture using a valid foreign full hash absent from TokenZero.
7. Keep existing #L behavior/tests and PR17 recovery listing stable.

## Acceptance Criteria
- No public surface claims write in one engine/read in another without an evidence gate.
- #B never returns a full or wrong payload and has regression coverage through recovery, MCP, and CodeMode surfaces.
- Same-store alias support remains tested and clearly scoped.
- Full refs/errors are never truncated.
- tokenzero-itl and reopened wqw.1 are linked as the work that restores broad support.
- Docs/claims test fails if unqualified cross-engine wording reappears before the matrix marker is green.

## Verify
Run focused tokenzero-recovery and tokenzero-mcp ref/expand tests, docs/claim snapshots, then cargo fmt, bounded workspace tests, and clippy -D warnings.

## Out of scope
Shared CAS, full-hash migration, or implementing #B.

## Handoff
Record every corrected claim, before/after #B behavior, exact tests, and remaining intentionally limited behavior.
close_reason: Completed: #B returns unsupported_fragment, fz/gz qualified as same-store aliases, tests renamed, negative fixture added, docs corrected

title: Adopt the canonical ZeroRef v1 contract and golden vectors
description:
## Goal
Encode one versioned contract for portable blob refs in TokenZero and use the exact shared fixtures owned across the three repos.

## External contract
Canonical counterpart beads:
- GraphZero: graphzero-zeroref-v1-shared-cas-1ghi.1
- FSZero: fszero-c6q.1
Any difference must be a reviewed cross-repo decision recorded in all three annexes and fixture versions, not a TokenZero-only interpretation.

## Contract to encode
- Portable scope: (tz|fz|gz)://blob/<full-hash> only. Execution/error/session/file/graph/index refs remain engine-specific and must be routed to their producer or rejected.
- Identity: full lowercase 64-hex SHA-256 of complete unfragmented bytes. Emit full; reject short, prefix, uppercase, non-hex, extra segments, and ambiguity for v1.
- #Bstart-end: zero-based half-open, checked arithmetic, start == end allowed, reversed or end > byte length rejected.
- #Lstart-end: one-based inclusive, exact newline retention per fixtures; zero/reversed/OOB rejected; non-UTF-8 is a typed error.
- Complete-object digest verification precedes fragment selection.
- Default storage is project-local; explicit shared root enables content sharing. Mutable engine metadata stays namespaced.
- Stable errors distinguish malformed, unsupported, missing, I/O, corruption/digest mismatch, policy denial, incompatible version, and legacy ambiguity.
- Layout/version, trust boundary, size limits, migration, and threat model are normative.

## Task
Update the TokenZero ADR/docs, parser/formatter model, public schema comments, and committed machine-readable valid/invalid golden vectors. Search every ref consumer/emitter; list it in the design so no surface is missed. Clarify that scheme denotes producer/provenance, not authorization or storage location.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Contract annex and fixture version/hash match GraphZero and FSZero.
2. Parser/formatter round-trip canonical fixtures and reject the full negative set.
3. Non-blob foreign refs cannot be canonicalized into TokenZero storage.
4. Error taxonomy and fragment/newline/empty-range behavior are explicit.
5. Downstream CAS/migration/fragment/capability tasks can be implemented from this bead alone.
6. Any reviewed change updates all three fixture copies atomically in coordinated PRs.

## Verify
Run focused parser/serialization/docs tests, then cargo fmt, bounded workspace tests, and clippy -D warnings.

## Out of scope
Store I/O and legacy data migration.

## Handoff
Record fixture version/hash, all consumers/emitters, exact tests, and cross-repo review references.

title: Implement TokenZero canonical shared-CAS adapter
description:
## Goal
Publish and resolve full-hash ZeroRef v1 blobs through the canonical shared CAS instead of relying on TokenZero's private JSON recovery store.

## Current evidence
crates/tokenzero-recovery has a TokenZero-specific store and scheme normalization but no adapter that can read FSZero/GraphZero objects. Store/root selection already supports project-local isolation and explicit TOKENZERO_SHARED_STORE/ZEROSTACK_SHARED_STORE opt-in; preserve those guarantees.

## Canonical layout and algorithm
- Under the effective ZeroStack root, immutable objects live at blobs/sha256/<first-two-hex>/<64-lowercase-hex>.
- Hash complete bytes before deriving the path.
- Write a unique sibling temp file; flush/sync where supported; publish atomically.
- If destination exists, verify digest and length. Identical is idempotent success; mismatch is collision/corruption and must not overwrite.
- Concurrent identical writers converge on one valid object.
- Reads use exact full hash, enforce regular-file/size policy, verify complete digest/length, and only then return to fragment logic.
- Corruption is terminal and never falls through to another store tier.
- Default project-local root remains isolated. Explicit shared mode shares immutable blobs only; recovery metadata, health, indexes, provenance, and policy remain project/engine-namespaced.
- Preserve a clearly documented legacy private-store read tier for migration; no implicit prefix matching.

## Implementation requirements
Define an injectable store interface/handle with typed missing/I/O/corruption/policy errors and no mutable global state. Reuse it across CLI/MCP/CodeMode. Review symlink/traversal, object size, temp cleanup, Windows publication/contention, and read/write health separately. Do not expose private absolute paths in errors/capabilities.

## Acceptance Criteria
Exact bytes survive restart; two explicit-shared checkouts deduplicate while defaults isolate; concurrent writers and interrupted writes never publish corruption; wrong bytes under a digest fail; read-only and permission failures are typed; standalone behavior remains green; a full ref produced by a sibling fixture can resolve when it points to the configured CAS.

## Verify
Add tempdir/concurrency/corruption/restart/root-isolation tests on macOS/Linux/Windows, run focused recovery/MCP tests, then cargo fmt, bounded workspace tests, and clippy.

## Out of scope
Legacy short-ID bulk migration, fragment slicing, GC, and remote replication.

## Handoff
Record store interface, layout/config precedence, failure table, exact tests, and fresh-root/restart smoke transcript.
close_reason: SharedCas adapter with canonical layout, atomic publish, digest verification, typed errors, tests

title: Migrate TokenZero legacy short refs to full SHA-256 identities
description:
## Goal
Move TokenZero from its 17-character short blob IDs (prefix plus first eight SHA-256 bytes) to canonical full 64-hex identities without data loss or silent collision resolution.

## Task
1. Inventory every current emitter, parser, JSON/store key, cached ref, report, execution error, fixture, and persisted schema using short IDs.
2. Canonical writes publish one full-hash CAS object and emit the full v1 ref. If a compatibility alias is needed, store a mapping, not a duplicate payload.
3. Continue reading supported legacy refs for one explicit compatibility window through an exact verified alias index.
4. Build/rebuild the alias index by hashing legacy bytes completely. One short ID mapping to multiple full hashes is ambiguous and must fail deterministically; never choose first/prefix match.
5. Provide an idempotent migration/verify command or gated startup flow with versioned manifest, resume after interruption, dry-run, counts, and no content/path leakage.
6. Do not delete legacy data until all objects/manifests verify and a separate explicit cleanup command runs.
7. Add deprecation warnings/telemetry and doctor output with deadline/state; document upgrade, rollback/downgrade, repair, and cleanup.
8. Ensure cache keys and report/error refs cannot collide between legacy/full modes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- New writes emit full canonical refs and one CAS payload.
- Fixtures for every supported legacy schema/ref resolve byte-exact after migration and restart.
- Ambiguous-prefix, corrupt, missing, interrupted, repeated, read-only, and low-disk/error-injection cases fail safely with original data intact.
- Migration is idempotent/resumable and pre/post manifests prove hash/size equality.
- Legacy lookup has a bounded removal criterion and can be disabled/tested.
- No test relies on finding a natural SHA prefix collision; deterministic injected fixtures exercise it.

## Verify
Run migration fixtures and collision/error-injection tests, fresh/upgraded/rollback smoke, then cargo fmt, bounded workspace tests, and clippy.

## Out of scope
Foreign binary orchestration and CAS GC.

## Handoff
Record supported versions, manifest/alias schema, commands, compatibility deadline, exact tests, and rollback transcript.
close_reason: Complete: dry-run-first migrate/verify/rollback/cleanup with resumable manifest, collision-safe aliases, durable deletion tombstones, unified CAS root derivation. Verified: CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 cargo test -p tokenzero-recovery --lib -- --test-threads=1 => 132 passed 0 failed; cargo build -p tokenzero exit 0; CLI lifecycle smoke 26/26 assertions (dry-run immutability, apply, verify, confirm-gated cleanup persistence, alias expand after cleanup, rollback, missing-confirm exit 2). Commit fe0fe0f.

title: Implement strict TokenZero ZeroRef #B/#L fragment algebra
description:
## Goal
Apply the shared byte/line fragment contract consistently across TokenZero recovery, MCP, and CodeMode after whole-object integrity verification.

## Current evidence
TokenZero supports #L, including PR17's end-OOB fix, but does not implement canonical #B and may degrade it to a full blob. Parser and surface behavior must be unified.

## Task
- Centralize parsing/canonicalization for all expansion surfaces.
- #Bstart-end is zero-based half-open with checked integer conversion; start == end returns empty bytes; start > end or end > length is a typed OOB/reversed error.
- #Lstart-end is one-based inclusive, never clamps, and preserves exact selected source bytes/newlines from shared golden vectors.
- Define empty file, final unterminated line, LF, CRLF, Unicode, and trailing newline behavior.
- #L on non-UTF-8 returns non_utf8_line_fragment; whole/#B reads remain byte-exact.
- Verify complete object digest before slicing so a valid window cannot mask corruption elsewhere.
- Reject malformed/duplicate fragments, overflow, zero line, unknown fragment kind, and fragments on unsupported non-blob refs.
- Preserve complete untruncated refs and stable error classes through recovery/MCP/CodeMode.
- Until full implementation ships, the P0 truth bead's explicit #B rejection remains.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: Make the PR18 policy descriptor the sole tool and ZeroRef capability owner
description:
## Goal
Finish the PR18 architecture so registration, listing, call authorization, recovery exposure, aliases, mutation class, and ZeroRef capabilities cannot drift across FastMCP/legacy surfaces.

## Current state
PR18 merged with SurfaceHealth::gate_tools_call as the runtime policy owner, while PR17 preserved stable recovery listing and server-owned limits. Remaining metadata is still spread across registration/list/call/catalog paths and is vulnerable to future mismatch.

## Task
1. Inventory every tool descriptor, alias, registration path, list filter, call gate, recovery flag, mutation/read class, health gate, timeout/limit, and capability serialization path.
2. Define one typed/generated policy descriptor per canonical tool. All surfaces consume it; no duplicate hand-maintained allowlist.
3. Represent aliases as references to a canonical descriptor and prove they cannot change authorization, limits, or mutation class.
4. Preserve stable recovery-tool registration/listing when unhealthy, while call authorization returns the policy-owned health error.
5. Extend the same descriptor source with ZeroRef v1 capability data: contract version, hash/fragment/layout support, local-only vs configured foreign read/write, legacy mode, size limits, and health.
6. Use existing listChanged/capability notification semantics where supported. Notify only when effective exposed capability changes; coalesce flapping and do not create loops.
7. Validate peer descriptors before routing; incompatible major/hash/layout fails early with actionable error. Additive minor fields remain forward-compatible.
8. Generate catalog/schema/docs snapshots from the descriptor and add property/parity tests across FastMCP and retained legacy paths.
9. Descriptor output must not expose secrets/private paths.

## Acceptance Criteria
Every callable canonical name and alias is registered/listed/gated from one descriptor; parity tests enumerate all tools and fail on drift; unhealthy recovery listing remains stable; mutation classification matches actual handler; capability negotiation distinguishes code support/configured state/health; notifications are deterministic; PR17/18 regression tests remain green.

## Verify

## Out of scope
Adding new user-facing tools or redesigning transport protocols.

## Handoff

title: Add crash-safe plan-scoped mutation journaling to CodeMode
description:
## Goal
Give multi-step CodeMode plans a truthful crash-recovery boundary for reversible TokenZero/engine mutations without pretending arbitrary shell side effects are transactional.

## Design requirements
- Classify every policy descriptor operation as read-only, reversible store mutation, irreversible/external side effect, or unknown.
- Before the first reversible mutation, create a plan-scoped intent journal with version, plan/execution ID, project/store identity, ordered operations, preconditions, and undo/compensation refs. Sync it before applying.
- Record prepare/apply/commit/rollback progress atomically so restart can distinguish never-started, partially applied, committed, rolling back, and manual-intervention states.
- Use idempotency keys and compare-and-swap/precondition checks so replay cannot duplicate mutations or overwrite newer data.
- Roll back completed reversible steps in reverse order after a later failure; preserve both original and rollback errors.
- On startup/doctor, detect incomplete journals and support safe inspect/resume/rollback. Never auto-delete evidence before resolution.
- Shell/network/external operations are not rollbackable. Reject them inside an atomic block or explicitly downgrade the plan to non-atomic before execution; never label a mixed plan fully transactional.
- Redact secrets and blob bodies; journal refs/digests and bounded diagnostics.
- Bound journal size/retention and integrate pins so undo refs cannot be GC'd.
- Property/error-injection tests crash at every durable boundary.

## Acceptance Criteria
A plan with multiple reversible mutations commits atomically from the user's perspective or restores verified pre-state; restart at every injected boundary recovers deterministically; replay is idempotent; concurrent conflicting plans fail before overwrite; rollback failure is actionable and retains evidence; shell boundary is explicit/tested; doctor lists unresolved journals.

## Verify
Run state-machine/property tests with deterministic fault injection, multi-process conflict tests, restart smoke, and policy classification parity, then cargo fmt, bounded workspace tests, and clippy.

## Out of scope
Distributed transactions across remote services or undoing arbitrary shell commands.

## Handoff
Record state machine, durable format/version, operation classification table, recovery commands, fault points, exact tests, and known non-atomic boundaries.
close_reason: Complete: tokenzero.plan-journal.v1 crash-safe plan-scoped journaling in CodeMode. Classification (read_only/reversible/irreversible_external/unknown) from the PR18 descriptor; atomic temp+rename+fsync journals under plan-journals/; state machine prepared/applying/committed/rolling_back/rolled_back/manual_intervention; idempotency keys + CAS preconditions (no clobber of newer data); reverse rollback preserving both errors; doctor/inspect/resume/rollback surface; zerostack.cas-gc.v1 pins for unresolved undo refs; durable atomic:false downgrade for mixed plans. Verified under machine guard: cargo test -p tokenzero-mcp journal -- --test-threads=1 => 13 passed 0 failed + 1/1 conflict child; git diff --check clean. Commit f2c98d6.

title: Implement conservative shared-CAS pins, mark-sweep GC, and repair
description:
## Goal
Bound shared-CAS disk growth without deleting blobs still reachable from TokenZero, FSZero, GraphZero, legacy aliases, active readers/writers, or mutation journals.

## External inputs
- FSZero reachability: fszero-c6q.9
- GraphZero reachability: graphzero-zeroref-v1-shared-cas-1ghi.9
This TokenZero bead owns the coordinator/collector and shared schema. Coordinate schema changes across all three repos.

## Task
1. Define versioned engine/project-namespaced roots/pins outside immutable blob bytes.
2. Enumerate TokenZero roots: recovery/index/error refs, reports/caches that promise durability, legacy alias maps, active plans, and journal undo refs.
3. Use atomic reachability snapshots plus leases/epochs so a concurrent reader/writer cannot lose an object between mark and sweep.
4. Mark from all recognized engine roots. Unknown/newer/corrupt/missing root metadata is conservative: retain affected objects and report why.
5. Sweep only canonical object paths older than a configurable grace period and absent from the stable mark set; recheck identity/state immediately before delete.
6. Default first release to dry-run/report. Require explicit apply, show counts/bytes/reasons, and never print blob contents/secrets.
7. Quarantine malformed/corrupt objects and unsafe temp files; do not treat deletion as repair. Provide verify/repair commands and resumable state.
8. Preserve legacy-ref reachability through the compatibility window.
9. Serialize or safely coordinate concurrent collectors; crash during sweep resumes idempotently.
10. Test symlink/path attacks, cross-project/engine namespace collision, clock skew, stale leases, partial metadata, concurrent expansion/write/migration/journal, restart, and Windows contention.

## Acceptance Criteria
All live fixtures across three engines survive; unreachable aged objects are reported/deleted exactly; active operations and journals survive concurrent sweep; uncertainty retains data; dry-run/apply are reproducible; collector crash resumes; two collectors cannot double-corrupt state; macOS/Linux/Windows coordinator fixtures pass.

## Verify
Run deterministic three-engine root fixtures, property/error-injection/concurrency/restart tests, dry-run/apply smoke, then cargo fmt, bounded workspace tests, and clippy.

## Out of scope
Remote object-store lifecycle policies or content retention law.

## Handoff
Record schema/version, root inventory, grace/lease algorithm, repair flow, dry-run/apply transcript, cross-repo pins, and exact tests.
close_reason: Implemented in PR https://github.com/AdityaVG13/tokenzero/pull/23. 22 shared_cas unit tests pass including fault-injection mid-sweep resume test.

title: Converge TokenZero, FSZero, and GraphZero on one repo structure
description:
POLICY (owner, 2026-07-26): TokenZero, FSZero, and GraphZero should share one
structure. Same crate layout, same surface split, same tests/ shape, same docs
set, same install flow.

The reasoning is diagnostic, not aesthetic: when the three repos are shaped
alike, a bug found at a given layer in one is immediately checkable at the same
layer in the other two. When they diverge, every investigation starts by
relearning the repo. Boring and identical beats clever and bespoke.

TARGET SHAPE (set by TokenZero once its cleanup lands)

  crates/<product>-codemode    CodeMode surface, optimized hard
  crates/<product>-mcp         MCP surface
  crates/<product>-<core...>   shared base both surfaces call
  tests/                       <= 50 ship tests
  docs/                        command-coverage, development, install, mcp,
                               codemode, pulse, racc, benchmarks
  demo/                        README + .sh and .ps1 runners, no npm
  benchmarks/                  small reproducible suite
  (shared)                     ZeroStack test library

MEASURED STARTING POINTS (2026-07-26)

  FSZero    ALREADY SPLIT. crates/ has fszero-codemode, fszero-mcp, fszero-shim,
            and fszero-codemode selects `features = ["surface-codemode"]` on the
            root crate. So FSZero solved this before TokenZero did -- study its
            layout BEFORE designing TokenZero's split
            (tokenzero-slim-public-repo-4uql.8), and where FSZero's approach is
            better, copy it rather than inventing a second pattern.
            Remaining work here is the rest of the parity checklist, plus
            fszero-on5z (already filed) for reorganization.

  GraphZero HAS NO CODEMODE SURFACE AT ALL. crates/ is graphzero-{cli, coverage,
            extract, pack, query, reserve, scip, semantic, store, test-support,
            types, why}. There is no graphzero-codemode and no graphzero-mcp.
            This is not a split -- it is building a surface that does not exist,
            and is substantially more work than the other two. Scope it
            honestly; do not file it as "same as TokenZero".
            Note graphzero-test-support already exists and likely overlaps the
            shared ZeroStack test library -- reconcile rather than duplicate.

WHAT TO FILE, PER REPO

Each of FSZero and GraphZero needs its own tracked work for: surface split (or
creation), 50-test ship budget, docs set incl. codemode.md, demo consolidation,
benchmark rebuild, telemetry policy statement, install surface choice, and
directory pruning.

FILE THOSE BEADS IN THEIR OWN REPOS -- fszero-* and graphzero-* -- not here.
Each repo's .beads/issues.jsonl is tracked and pushed to its own public GitHub,
and work should live where the people who can act on it will look.

ORDERING

TokenZero goes first and sets the shape, EXCEPT for the surface split, where
FSZero is already ahead and should inform TokenZero's design. Do not propagate a
pattern to three repos until it has been proven in one.

ACCEPTANCE

  * A written parity checklist exists, with per-repo status.
  * Beads filed in fszero and graphzero for their own gaps.
  * Someone who knows one repo can navigate the other two without relearning.
  * Divergences that remain are deliberate and documented, with the reason.

title: Windowed expand ref_not_found
description:
## Goal
Windowed expand returns exact line ranges so agents never pull multi-k tokens for 50 lines.

## Why (Pareto)
Field zerostackbug5: start_line/end_line → substrate ref_not_found. Agents fall back to shell sed. Blocks capsule-default (wqw.13) and fixes negative compression (wqw.11).

## Context
- Baseline: S4_window/symbol fails in perf artifacts
- Siblings: wqw.10 field confirm, wqw.8 same-session miss
- HANDOFF Wave A #2

## Task
1. Trace windowed expand (start_line/end_line/symbol)
2. Fix registry miss vs window application order
3. Distinct errors: unknown-ref / bad-window / store-mismatch
4. Tests: full, middle window, edges, OOB
5. Measure visible_tokens window vs full

## Constraints
- Exact line fidelity (document 1-index inclusive/exclusive)
- Blob must not require re-read of source path if stored
- No silent truncation

## Acceptance (done_when)
1. expand(ref,{start_line:N,end_line:M}) returns exact lines N..M
2. Out-of-range → structured error, not ref_not_found
3. Same-session codemode blob is window-expandable
4. Visible tokens for 50-line window << full file (record numbers)
5. Regression test + field repro path covered

## Verify
Store multi-line fixture via codemode; expand 120-190; assert content; cargo test windowed_expand.

## Out of scope
Cross-scheme fz/gz (wqw.1); product policy of capsule-default (wqw.13)

## Handoff
Golden fixture + command failing on main / passing on branch.
notes: VERIFIED NOT A DEFECT (main agent, same-store repro): windowed expand works when mint and expand share --cache-path; the profiling run minted refs in one store and expanded against another (refs are per-store by design). Remaining work: re-baseline S4 windowing overhead with same-store refs so the windowed-vs-whole cost claim gets a real number.

SHA on fix/codemode-expand-p0. cargo test -p tokenzero-recovery --lib windowed_expand (3 ok); cargo test -p tokenzero-mcp --lib windowed_expand (2 ok). Theory cite: W5-SOL-MDC-Q4-FULL-18-19 (Cont-2, DR+EC): parity ledger dominates full no-recovery prefix hull on Theta4 down/cap at (40,20) iff 1<=m<=18; fails m>=19.
Acceptance: checkers reproduce frozen PASS lines; lane never blocks product release; no general-n claims (BP1 general-n OPEN, arbitrary-n Cont-2 NOT frozen).

title: E8: Docs / non-claims / operator guide
description:
Epic: docs / operator: how to read RATC reports; explicit non-claims (no 99.9% always, no global Pareto dominance, no MDC peer merge, formal gauge != production measurement).
Acceptance: docs published; promotion-gate output references them.
Out of scope: marketing claims.

title: Import Formal Core v1 freeze into docs/spec + statement lock
description:
Context: freeze inventory lives only in the attach pack (.radc-pack/impl-attach-FLAT/00_RADC_FORMAL_CORE_V1_FREEZE.md). Import it as docs/spec/RADC_FORMAL_CORE_V1.md and add a statement-lock table mapping formal ledger symbols (M visible/message cost, L latency cost, D distortion, m demand count, gauge (rho,lambda)=(40,20)) to concrete code counters (tokenzero.ledger.v1 fields, CrossEngineTelemetry).
Acceptance: (1) doc lists frozen IDs (W4-DP/FLOOR/PHASE/AFF-Q4-40/DA-RATE/OPAQUE-CAS-ALIAS/DIRECT-HASH-KILL/CORRIDOR-Q4; W5-SOL-AGRD-THETA; W5-SOL-MDC-Q4-FULL-18-19); (2) explicit NOT-frozen list copied verbatim (no 99.9% claim, no MDC peer merge, BP1 general-n OPEN, arbitrary-n Cont-2 NOT frozen, production Pareto dominance NOT frozen); (3) statement-lock table reviewed against crates/tokenzero-engine/src/ledger.rs field names; (4) docs-only diff, no code changes.
Out of scope: proving anything; Wave-6 theory.
Proof status: PRODUCT doc citing DR/EC theorem IDs; IDs marked claim-until-EC-rerun per freeze rule.
Paths: docs/spec/RADC_FORMAL_CORE_V1.md (new), docs/racc.md (reference only).

title: Forbidden-claims register + optional grep CI
description:
Context: freeze section 5 lists claims that must never appear in product docs or release notes (99.9% compression always; global Pareto dominance; Fable=Kimi MDC; R_ag(D) on arbitrary real agent policies; BP1 general-n).
Acceptance: (1) docs/spec/RADC_FORBIDDEN_CLAIMS.md enumerates each forbidden claim + why (freeze citation); (2) optional CI/xtask grep fails on forbidden strings outside allowlisted theory docs; (3) allowlist mechanism documented.
Out of scope: rewriting research distill docs.
Proof status: PRODUCT.
Paths: docs/spec/RADC_FORBIDDEN_CLAIMS.md, xtask/ (optional lint).

title: Ledger v2 schema: recovery-adjusted fields + RATC identity
description:
Context: KPI = recovery-adjusted tokens per successful task = visible + expand + weighted(fail/retry). tokenzero.ledger.v1 (crates/tokenzero-engine/src/ledger.rs) records dedup/diff visible savings only; expand/fail costs are uncounted, so visible-only wins can be smuggled (evidence-ladder violation).
Acceptance: (1) tokenzero.ledger.v2 record adds visible_tokens, expand_tokens, expand_count, retry_count, fail_count, rho_fail, lambda_fail, task_success, anchor_recall_ok, dangling_ref_count, ratc = visible + expand + rho_fail*retries + lambda_fail*fails; (2) v1 records still readable (schema version field, migration note); (3) golden fixture tests assert RATC identity arithmetically; (4) no payload bytes in ledger records (telemetry-only rule preserved).
Out of scope: per-task grouping (E1.2); tokenizer measurement of expand tokens (E1.3/E5).
Proof status: PRODUCT (ledger identity is accounting, not a theorem).
Paths: crates/tokenzero-engine/src/ledger.rs, crates/tokenzero-engine/src/usage_telemetry.rs, schemas/tokenzero.ledger.v2.json.

title: Per-task cost roll-up: TaskCostSummary report (CSV/JSON)
description:
Context: KPI is per SUCCESSFUL task; raw per-response records need grouping by task/session id to compute RATC-per-task and success rate for the pilot report.
Acceptance: (1) roll-up reads ledger v2, groups by task_id, emits TaskCostSummary {task_id, success, visible, expand, retries, fails, ratc, expand_count, dangling_refs}; (2) xtask or report_tool subcommand writes CSV + JSON; (3) golden test on fixtures with hand-computed expected summaries; (4) tasks with fail>0 counted in success rate denominator, never silently dropped.
Out of scope: A/B comparison logic (E4.2).
Proof status: PRODUCT.
Paths: crates/tokenzero-engine/src/ledger.rs, crates/tokenzero-engine/src/report_tool.rs, xtask/.

title: Count expand tokens + typed misses at the expand surface
description:
Context: RACC contract: a response emitting only an exact ref has high visible savings, but honest evaluation must count any later expand output the agent used. Expand bytes must become tokens via the tokenizer registry, and dangling-ref misses must be counted as weighted fails, never as success (RACC H3; W4 survival gate: typed miss without exact fallback scores D>0).
Acceptance: (1) engine_expand.rs records expanded bytes -> tokens into ledger v2 expand fields per call; (2) dangling-ref / stale-ref / ref-not-found each increment typed counters and fail weights; (3) unit tests cover success expand, dangling after eviction, unknown ref; (4) counters appear in CrossEngineTelemetry or ledger without payload bytes.
Out of scope: eviction policy changes (E6).
Proof status: PRODUCT (implements RACC contract; cites W4 survival-gate freeze as motivation only).
Paths: crates/tokenzero-engine/src/engine_expand.rs, crates/tokenzero-engine/src/expand_params.rs, crates/tokenzero-recovery/src/telemetry.rs.

title: Opaque handle emission: alias must not be raw content hash
description:
Context: W4-OPAQUE-CAS-ALIAS + W4-DIRECT-HASH-KILL (frozen, EC): visible hash != opaque; two-level alias -> CAS. A visible tz:// handle that embeds the content hash leaks membership/identity and fails the opacity claim; audit current handle formats and route emission through a random or non-content-derived alias with an internal alias -> CAS map.
Acceptance: (1) visible handle bytes are independent of payload content hash (random alias or keyed derivation); (2) opacity regression test: with mode=exact-ref, rendered transcript contains neither raw payload nor its content hash; (3) alias -> payload resolution stays internal to recovery store; (4) existing tz:// ref tests updated, not deleted.
Out of scope: changing CAS addressing internally (content hash stays as internal key); cross-engine alias federation.
Proof status: EC-cited (W4) + PRODUCT.
Paths: crates/tokenzero-recovery/src/session_aliases.rs, crates/tokenzero-recovery/src/shared_cas.rs, crates/tokenzero-engine/src/render.rs.

title: Expand API hardening: selector -> bytes; typed errors; never wrong bytes
description:
Context: RACC H1 (exact recovery while entry exists) + H3 (never wrong bytes on miss). Expand must return exact bytes for a live ref, and typed errors (dangling-ref after eviction, stale-ref on generation mismatch, ref-not-found) otherwise. Generation counter prevents stale alias ABA reuse (W4 bead blueprint freeze).
Acceptance: (1) expand resolves selector (byte range, line range, symbol, search hit) against stored payload and returns byte-exact slice; (2) proptest: roundtrip put/expand equals source for all ref kinds; (3) eviction yields dangling-ref, never substitute bytes; (4) generation/ABA regression test; (5) typed errors surfaced to ledger as misses (feeds E1.3).
Out of scope: KV-splice / prefill research (F1 not frozen); fallback re-read pricing (E4 report only).
Proof status: PRODUCT (H1/H3 invariants); W4 survival-gate cited as EC motivation.
Paths: crates/tokenzero-recovery/src/embedded_store.rs, crates/tokenzero-recovery/src/shared_cas.rs, crates/tokenzero-engine/src/engine_expand.rs.

title: Inline-payload invariant: eviction never dangles surviving refs
description:
Context: docs/racc.md: every ref kind stores its payload inline, so dropping one entry never dangles another; oldest-first eviction under per-kind counts + byte ceiling.
Acceptance: (1) proptest: random interleavings of put/evict/expand across ref kinds preserve the invariant that any non-evicted ref expands exactly; (2) test byte-ceiling + per-kind-count eviction order; (3) docs/racc.md semantics re-verified against code comments.
Out of scope: changing eviction policy (E6.2 aligns policy, this bead only pins the invariant).
Proof status: PRODUCT.
Paths: crates/tokenzero-recovery/src/embedded_store.rs, crates/tokenzero-recovery/src/embedded_store_tests.rs.

title: Capsule policy v1: exact-ref preference above threshold + omission enforcement
description:
Context: RACC omission contract (docs/racc.md, already backported as runtime validation): omit payload from visible capsule only when protected anchor, exact ref with concrete selector, or declared lossy with lossy_spans + lossy_policy_id + visible lossy text. Policy v1: local payloads above a configurable byte threshold default to exact-ref; below threshold inline.
Acceptance: (1) policy decision function unit-tested on fixtures across threshold boundaries; (2) capsule emission validates omission evidence (anchor / tz:// ref+selector / lossy declaration) - rejects unclassified omission; (3) lossy declaration repeated in visible text; (4) tiny-budget floor: declaration may exceed budget rather than degrade to bare "omitted".
Out of scope: learned/trainable policies; semantic summarization quality.
Proof status: PRODUCT (RACC contract floor).
Paths: crates/tokenzero-engine/src/render.rs, crates/tokenzero-engine/src/engine_read.rs, crates/tokenzero-engine/src/config.rs.

title: Demand-aware expand hooks: slice/range/symbol selector grammar
description:
Context: W5-SOL-AGRD-THETA (DR): R_ag,theta(D)=1-H2(D) - expand AFTER demand is revealed is the right shape for sparse decisions; product consequence: expand API must let the agent request minimal selectors (line range, byte range, symbol, error block) instead of whole payloads.
Acceptance: (1) selector grammar documented + parser unit tests; (2) range/symbol expand returns exactly the selected bytes (golden fixtures); (3) expand_tokens accounting reflects selector-sized output, not full payload (with E1.3); (4) invalid selectors yield typed errors.
Out of scope: demand prediction (E6.3 speculative); natural-language selectors.
Proof status: DR-cited motivation; PRODUCT implementation.
Paths: crates/tokenzero-engine/src/expand_params.rs, crates/tokenzero-engine/src/engine_expand.rs.

title: Config surface: rho_fail, lambda_fail, handle cost estimates (h,q,c)
description:
Context: RATC weights (retry/failure penalties) and corridor parameters h (handle tokens), q (selector serialization tokens), c (CAS round trip) need config homes with measured-later placeholders; E5 fills real values.
Acceptance: (1) config.rs parses ratc {rho_fail, lambda_fail} and corridor {h, q, c} with documented defaults; (2) RATC computation reads weights from config (E1.1 identity parameterized); (3) unknown-key rejection tests; (4) values clearly marked ADVISORY until E5 measurement.
Out of scope: auto-tuning.
Proof status: PRODUCT.
Paths: crates/tokenzero-engine/src/config.rs.

title: Pilot suite: 10-20 fixed file-heavy agent tasks + deterministic runner
description:
Context: return = exact-ref policy beats paste-full baseline on recovery-adjusted tokens per successful task at equal-or-better success/anchor recall, on a FIXED suite. Suite defined in IMPL_PILOT_SUITE.md (14 tasks: single/multi-demand expands, eviction stress, dangling handling, secret-mask, lossy mode, cross-session reuse).
Acceptance: (1) suite fixtures under test-corpus/ or benchmarks/pilot/ with per-task success predicates + anchor lists; (2) runner executes each task in baseline mode (paste full) and exact-ref policy mode against the real engine; (3) deterministic (seeded, no network); (4) every task tagged with demand count m and expected expand count.
Out of scope: live/production traffic; new task authoring after promotion freeze without versioning the suite.
Proof status: PRODUCT.
Paths: benchmarks/pilot/ (new), xtask/ runner, fixtures/.

title: A/B report: success, RATC, expand rate, dangling rate, Pareto CSV/JSON
description:
Context: pilot output must make visible-only smuggling impossible: report both first-response visible savings AND recovery-adjusted cost per task, per mode.
Acceptance: (1) report consumes TaskCostSummary stream (E1.2) for both modes; (2) per-task and aggregate: success rate, anchor recall, mean/median RATC, visible tokens, expand tokens/rate, dangling-ref rate, fail/retry counts; (3) CSV + JSON + Pareto-plottable (visible, ratc) pairs; (4) golden sample report test; (5) deltas exact-ref vs baseline computed per task.
Out of scope: statistical significance framework beyond fixed-suite deltas (document limitation).
Proof status: PRODUCT.
Paths: xtask/, crates/tokenzero-engine/src/report_tool.rs.

title: Promotion gate: RATC win required, success/anchor regression forbidden
description:
Context: RACC promotion rule (docs/racc.md): never promote on visible savings alone; needs no dangling handles, recovery-adjusted savings above baseline, no task-lossless regression, no protected-anchor regression, task success on validation set. Gate automates this on pilot output.
Acceptance: (1) xtask gate consumes A/B report and exits nonzero unless: RATC_exact_ref < RATC_baseline (aggregate + no per-task catastrophic regression), success >= baseline, anchor recall >= baseline, dangling_unresolved == 0; (2) fixture test: visible-only-win report is REJECTED; (3) gate verdict written into report; (4) E8.1 doc explains reading the verdict.
Out of scope: promoting anything (decision stays human/operator).
Proof status: PRODUCT.
Paths: xtask/.

title: Measure h_tau, q_tau, c_tau on pilot tokenizer; compare to (40,20) corridor
description:
Context: W4-CORRIDOR-Q4 (EC): at registered gauge (rho,lambda)=(40,20), dominance corridors require 2h+q<=7 and h+q+c<=3 with at least one strict inequality, measured with the DECLARED production tokenizer (never assume a URI is one token; no cross-tokenizer numerical transfer). Advisory only until pilot validates.
Acceptance: (1) harness measures h (rendered handle tokens), q (selector serialization tokens), c (CAS construction + expand round trip, tokens and wall-clock) on the pilot tokenizer; (2) values recorded into config (E3.3) and report; (3) corridor inequalities evaluated + printed as ADVISORY; (4) measurement repeated for at least one secondary tokenizer to document non-transfer.
Out of scope: hard ship block; re-deriving corridor math.
Proof status: EC-cited (W4-CORRIDOR-Q4) as advisory; PRODUCT measurement.
Paths: xtask/ or benches/, crates/tokenzero-engine/src/config.rs.

title: Document formal-gauge vs product gaps (docs/radc-corridor.md)
description:
Context: freeze: formal information rate is not measured token cost (Cont-1 failure log: production corridor needs empirical tokenizer/store map with tail bounds).
Acceptance: doc records measured h,q,c; corridor inequality outcomes; known gaps (tokenizer drift, multi-model fleets, wall-clock vs token ledger); explicit statement that formal dominance at (40,20) is motivation, not a production claim.
Proof status: PRODUCT doc citing EC/DR.
Paths: docs/radc-corridor.md.

title: Cross-turn/task CAS reuse + hit-rate telemetry
description:
Context: recovery-adjusted rate improves when expands hit warm cache across turns/tasks (cache multiplier motivation, RACC distill F3 paging frame - hypothesis-level). Reuse must preserve opacity + generation invariants from E2.
Acceptance: (1) CAS entries reusable across sessions where workspace/root binding allows; (2) cache-hit vs miss columns in ledger v2 report; (3) tests: second task expanding same ref pays hit cost, emits no new CAS write; (4) no cross-workspace leakage (root binding test).
Out of scope: pre-warm (E6.3); distributed cache.
Proof status: PRODUCT (F3 cited as hypothesis, not proof).
Paths: crates/tokenzero-recovery/src/shared_cas.rs, crates/tokenzero-engine/src/warmkeeper.rs, crates/tokenzero-engine/src/cache_meter.rs.

title: Eviction + dangling semantics aligned with racc.md contract
description:
Context: docs/racc.md: bounded cache (per-kind counts + byte ceiling), oldest-first eviction, evicted ref reports dangling-ref, never wrong bytes, eviction cannot break surviving refs. Code and doc must agree exactly; E2.3 pins the invariant, this bead aligns policy knobs + docs.
Acceptance: (1) eviction policy parameters (per-kind counts, byte ceiling) configurable + documented; (2) eviction order test (oldest-first per kind); (3) dangling-ref surfaces through expand API + ledger consistently; (4) docs/racc.md wording diff if implementation diverges.
Out of scope: new eviction strategies (LRU-K etc.).
Proof status: PRODUCT.
Paths: crates/tokenzero-recovery/src/embedded_store.rs, crates/tokenzero-engine/src/eviction_scheduler.rs, docs/racc.md.

title: SPECULATIVE: predictive pre-warm of expand candidates (flag-gated, off by default)
description:
Context: RACC distill F2 speculative recovery (ski-rental/newsvendor motivation - HYPOTHESIS, not a frozen theorem). Wrong guesses cost RAM only; pre-warm must never change the correctness set (H1/H3 unaffected).
Acceptance: (1) flag-gated, default off; (2) pre-warm only warms CAS/handle table, never injects model-visible tokens unrequested; (3) miss cost bounded + measured; (4) correctness test: task outcomes identical with flag on/off (telemetry may differ).
Out of scope: bandit training; claiming ski-rental bounds in product.
Proof status: SB (speculative); no theorem citation as product truth.
Paths: crates/tokenzero-engine/src/warmkeeper.rs.

title: Vendor Cont-2 checkers (Python+C++) into xtask radc-check with SHA256 pins
description:
Context: Cont-2 certificate pack (.radc-pack/impl-attach-FLAT/20-26): W5_FULL_PREFIX_CHECKS.py, w5_full_prefix_check.cpp, sol_m_demand_grid.cpp, expected .out files, SHA256 pins. Theorem: W5-SOL-MDC-Q4-FULL-18-19 (DR+EC) - parity ledger dominates full no-recovery prefix hull on Theta4 down/cap at (40,20) iff 1<=m<=18; fails m>=19. Motivates multi-demand/multi-expand cost accounting; NOT a hard product limit of 18 tools.
Acceptance: (1) checkers vendored with hash verification against 26_SOLPRO_CONT2_SHA256.txt pins; (2) xtask radc-check reproduces frozen PASS lines (exact C_16(r) table; p10 fraction; m=17/18 margins; m>=19 universal no-message obstruction); (3) runs in optional CI lane, never blocks product release; (4) README states scope: formal regression only.
Out of scope: general-n extension (BP1 general-n OPEN; arbitrary-n Cont-2 NOT frozen); rewriting checkers in Rust.
Proof status: EC (vendored re-run of DR+EC theorem).
Paths: xtask/, formal/cont2/ (vendored).

Acceptance: (1) DP enumeration reproduces the frozen split count; (2) result recorded next to Cont-2 lane; (3) failure does not block product.

title: Guide: how to read RATC reports (docs/radc-ratc-report.md)

Context: operators must distinguish first-response visible savings from recovery-adjusted cost; evidence ladder: mechanism PASS must not smuggle efficacy/release claims.
Acceptance: doc explains every report field (success, anchor recall, RATC, expand rate, dangling rate, weighted fails), the promotion-gate verdict meaning, and the evidence-ladder level a pilot win supports (efficacy on fixed suite only, NOT release).

Context: freeze section 5 + dual-track rule. title: Never worse than raw CLI: break the Pareto frontier on token compression
description: Invariant: TokenZero output tokens <= raw CLI tokens on EVERY task, no exceptions. Current suite (2026-07-27, M5 Max, v1.4.0): edit_verify 195 vs 5 (39x WORSE), grep_read 242 vs 370 (34.6%), tree_glob_read 555 vs 10492 (94.7%), multi_step 443 vs 27831 (98.4%), read_500 24 vs 5817 (99.6%). Root cause found via envelope forensics: fixed per-call JSON envelope metadata (~600-1200B) dominates small ops. refs=343B + telemetry=237B + accounting=125B + detail_ref=74B per call for a 15-byte edit. Children carry the levers.

title: edit_verify: TokenZero costs 39x raw CLI on tiny edits (195 vs 5 est tokens)
description: Suite row: edit_verify tokenzero=779 output bytes (195 est tokens) vs raw-cli sed=17 bytes (5 tokens). Forensics (release binary, fresh cache): a 15-byte file edit emits a 1204-byte JSON envelope; breakdown: refs=343B, telemetry=237B, accounting=125B, detail_ref=74B, visible=31B. Only 31 of ~1200 bytes are content. Levers: (a) inline-small-payload policy: when visible content < N bytes, emit content inline and skip detail_ref/refs; (b) drop or aggregate telemetry/accounting unless --verbose or TZ_TELEMETRY=1; (c) quiet success mode for mutations (sed-like: emit nothing on success beyond ack). Acceptance: edit_verify est_tokens <= raw-cli on the suite, byte-exact edit semantics unchanged, verified by benchmarks/run_all.sh.

title: Slim the JSON envelope: telemetry/accounting/refs are ~85% of small-call bytes
description: Measured on v1.4.0 release binary: per-call envelope carries refs=343B + telemetry=237B + accounting=125B + detail_ref=74B + schema/status/tool/mode/content_type ~50B, versus visible content that is often <100B. Levers to evaluate and implement: (1) minimal envelope mode (content + status only) as DEFAULT for --json, full schema behind --json=full; (2) session-level dedup: refs/telemetry emitted once per cache session, subsequent calls emit deltas; (3) refs array limited to NEW refs this call (currently unions prior refs); (4) telemetry behind TZ_TELEMETRY=1 or --telemetry flag. Coordinate with tokenzero-jfet (R-020 envelope unification) and tokenzero-1cwf (envelope consistency epic) so schema changes land in one version bump. Acceptance: envelope overhead <=20% of bytes for sub-1KB payloads; claim-audit and MCP surfaces migrated; docs/benchmarks.md regenerated showing the delta.

title: grep_read: 34.6% savings is unacceptable, target >=85%
description: Suite row: find TokenZero README.md -> 966 bytes (242 est tokens) vs grep -rn raw 1477 bytes (370 est tokens): 34.6%. A single grep over one file should be >=80-85%. The find envelope emits match lines wrapped in ~600-800B of envelope (refs/telemetry/accounting/detail_ref) plus match-line absolute paths repeated per hit. Levers: (a) strip common path prefix per result set (path stated once, lines carry offsets); (b) minimal envelope (tokenzero-0ok7); (c) match-context dedup: repeated file URI emitted once; (d) consider returning compact capsule with match COUNT + inline top-k lines instead of full line payloads when lines > threshold. Acceptance: grep_read row >=85% savings in docs/benchmarks.md, byte-exact recovery of every match line preserved.

title: tree_glob_read: 94.7% to >=97% via envelope amortization across chained calls
description: Suite row: tree+glob+read = 2218 bytes (555 est tokens) vs raw 41966 (10492): 94.7%. Three sequential calls each pay the fixed envelope toll (~600-800B); amortizing session metadata (tokenzero-0ok7 lever 2/4) plus path-prefix stripping should lift this to 96-97%. Acceptance: row >=96% in regenerated docs/benchmarks.md.

title: multi_step: 98.4% to 99% (kill the residual fixed costs across the 4-step chain)
description: Suite row: 4-step chain 1769 bytes (443 est) vs raw 111324 (27831): 98.4%. Residual = 4x envelope metadata. After envelope slimming (tokenzero-0ok7) lands, re-measure; target 99%. Acceptance: row >=99% in docs/benchmarks.md.

title: Add never-worse-than-raw assertion to the benchmark suite (hard gate)
description: benchmarks/competitor-bakeoff.sh and million-line-nav.sh should FAIL (not just print a row) whenever a TokenZero row has est_tokens > raw-cli est_tokens for the same task. Wire as a budget assertion section in docs/benchmarks.md like the 32k budget check, and a make target (perf-persist-gate style) so CI enforces the invariant. Acceptance: suite exits nonzero when any row violates TokenZero <= raw; docs/benchmarks.md shows the gate result.

title: [bug-hunt] EPIC: CodeMode/MCP root allowlist bypass via workspace-evidence markers
description:
GOAL
Close the P0 sandbox hole where CodeMode execute_code accepts a foreign root that is outside the server allowlist whenever the path contains workspace markers (.git, Cargo.toml, package.json, pyproject.toml, go.mod, .zerostack, CHANGELOG.md).

WHY
F-MCP-011 / F-INT-010 / Round2 CONFIRM. In tools.rs, root is accepted when path_allowed OR has_workspace_evidence. Engine then unions that root into the plan workspace, so subsequent ops can touch the foreign tree. allowed_root* is strict; root is not — inconsistency (F-R2 sibling).

RISK
Agent or malicious plan can pivot MCP session from a locked root into any recognizable project tree on the host filesystem. Local multi-tenant / shared-host risk.

PATHS / SYMPTOMS
- crates/tokenzero-mcp/src/tools.rs has_workspace_evidence (~80) and execute_code root handling (~222)
- Engine root union in codemode options

CONSTRAINTS
- Preserve intentional multi-root workflows only when each root is allowlisted or explicitly admin-granted
- Do not break legitimate workspace rebase inside already-allowed trees
- Security audit inventory must include execute_code root path

done_when
1) Foreign path with Cargo.toml/.git outside allowlist is rejected for execute_code root
2) allowed_root and root use the same allowlist gate
3) Regression test covers marker-present escape and marker-absent denial
4) Security audit / robot-docs mention the contract

verify
Static: grep shows has_workspace_evidence not used to skip allowlist; tests assert deny.
NO full cargo workspace run required for close if targeted tests green.

anti-goals
- Do not disable multi-root entirely
