title: codemode CPU burn: idle servers must sit at ~0%, not 50-90%
description: Observed 2026-07-27 on M5 Max: every tokenzero-codemode stdio server burns 50-90%% CPU for minutes after spawn (with ~30 sessions this is 10+ cores). Idle read/grep/edit servers must be ~0%%. Forensics (sample(1) + ps -M): (1) the JS async host-op bridge busy-polls: prelude __tz_call loops for(;;){ __tz_poll(); await Promise.resolve(); } (exec.rs:1030) and Rust poll_js_host_op sleeps only 1ms per miss (exec.rs:948) with rquickjs handle_panic overhead per iteration; (2) host jobs can fail to complete (dispatch panic before result is set) making the promise poll FOREVER with no deadline; (3) exec worker threads spend ~99%% of dispatch samples inside write() syscalls during a read op; (4) thread-per-exec churn (+11k thread IDs). Children carry fixes + a CPU regression gate.
close_reason: Fixed in 021eeee: CompletionGate condvar blocking poll + HostJobFinisher Drop guard + unwind-safe wall deadline. Verified: 3+3 new tests pass on Spark via RCH; full codemode suite parity with HEAD baseline (15 shared pre-existing failures, see tokenzero-4eyr; 2 flaky each side, 6-of-6 isolated passes); live binary 0.00s CPU per 10s idle and per 4s pending-op (was 50-90 percent); regression gate committed in 7500199 (6dod). Force-closed: nxyd (P1 write amplification) and v5rv (P2 thread pool) stay open as separate follow-ups; they are optimizations, not part of the burn fix.

title: Replace 1ms busy-poll in __tz_call/poll_js_host_op with blocking wait
description: exec.rs:948 poll_js_host_op does std::thread::sleep(1ms) on every unfinished poll, and the JS prelude (exec.rs:1030-1041) loops for(;;){ __tz_poll(); await Promise.resolve(); }. At ~1000 FFI+JSON.parse+rquickjs-boundary crossings per second per pending op, an idle server with any pending host job burns 50-90%% CPU (sampled: promise_reaction_job -> JS_CallInternal -> handle_panic -> thread::sleep, 2549/3006 samples). Fix: add a per-job completion gate (condvar/event) exposed as __tz_wait(id, budget_ms) that PARKS the thread until gate.release() fires or a budget elapses (exponential backoff capped ~50-100ms acceptable as interim); delete the 1ms sleep. Acceptance: idle codemode server <2%% CPU over a 10s window; plan round-trip latency unchanged within noise; cargo test -p tokenzero-mcp codemode passes.
close_reason: CompletionGate (epoch + condvar) added to AsyncHostRuntime; poll_js_host_op blocks on wait_for_change bounded by the hard-wall budget instead of sleeping 1ms per miss. Live verification: 0.00s CPU/4s with a pending host op, 0.00s/10s idle (was 50-90%). Commit 021eeee; tests on Spark via RCH.

title: Guarantee host-job completion: panic in dispatch must still resolve the JS promise
description: If the dispatch thread panics or exits before job.result is set (exec.rs:915-924 closure), poll_js_host_op spins forever: no timeout, no done-with-error path. Wrap dispatch in catch_unwind + a drop guard that ALWAYS writes a result (error payload kind=runtime on panic) and releases the gate; add a poll deadline (plan timeout, e.g. 30s default) after which __tz_poll returns done:true with a typed timeout error so the JS promise settles. This is the permanent-CPU-burn path observed on servers that keep spinning for minutes. Acceptance: injected dispatch panic in a test resolves the promise with an error and the server returns to <2%% CPU.
close_reason: HostJobFinisher Drop guard resolves every begun job (error payload on panic), wakes pollers, releases the ParallelWidthGate slot; poll also resolves past the hard-wall budget with the standard hard-wall error; with_host_wall_deadline now restores the thread-local on unwind. Commit 021eeee.

title: Exec workers spend ~99% of dispatch in write() syscalls during a read op
description: Sampled a live codemode server (M5 Max, 2026-07-27): transient exec thread dispatch_values -> dispatch_operation -> execute_domain_op -> engine_read read_with_options_inner with leaf write() in 1027/1030 samples. A read path dominated by write syscalls implies per-op journal/ledger/CAS write amplification (possibly fsync per op). Investigate engine_read + ledger run_flush_scheduler + codemode journal (journal.rs:1032 has its own 60ms sleep loop) for: per-op fsync, double writes (cache + journal + ledger), and small-append syscalls. Fix via batching/group-commit or deferred flush. Acceptance: strace/sample shows <10%% of read-op wall in write syscalls; ledger durability guarantees documented and preserved.

title: Pool exec worker threads instead of spawn-per-exec (+11k thread IDs observed)
description: dispatch_values uses thread::spawn (spawn_unchecked) per execution; on a busy machine thread IDs advanced ~11k over minutes across servers. Thread churn costs CPU and RSS. Introduce a bounded worker pool sized to permits. Relates to tokenzero-duplicate-codemode-index-rss-uaht (RSS bound across agent swarms). Acceptance: thread count stable under a 100-exec load test.

title: Add idle-CPU regression gate for codemode servers to the benchmark suite
description: New gate (benchmarks/, wired like the 32k budget assertion): boot tokenzero-codemode, run one trivial plan, then measure CPU over a 10s idle window; FAIL if >2%%. Also measure DURING a 100-plan loop and record per-plan CPU-ms. Without this gate the 1ms-poll class of bugs ships silently. Acceptance: benchmarks/run_all.sh includes the CPU gate section in docs/benchmarks.md and exits nonzero on violation.
close_reason: benchmarks/codemode-cpu-gate.sh added and wired into benchmarks/run_all.sh (commit 7500199). Four windows: host-op-pending 2s budget 0.5s, idle-after-completion 10s budget 0.2s (2%%), 20-plan loop informational CPU-ms/plan, idle-after-loop 5s. Exits nonzero on violation; first run PASS with 0.00s CPU in all idle/pending windows. docs/benchmarks.md picks the section up on the next full suite run.

title: Reserve crate/npm names for the engine family (tokenzero, fszero, graphzero)
description: Family convention confirmed across workspaces: <engine>-<component> (tokenzero-core/engine/mcp..., fszero-codemode/fszero-mcp/fszero-shim, graphzero-cli/store/...). crates.io is a flat global namespace: reserve tokenzero, tokenzero-codemode, fszero-codemode, graphzero-codemode (and the rest of each family) with placeholder publishes before extraction ships, or squatters take them. npm: prefer scoped packages @tokenzero/codemode, @fszero/codemode, @graphzero/codemode (scope registration required); unscoped tokenzero-codemode style names are the fallback. Acceptance: name reservation matrix documented, placeholders published or decision recorded, install docs updated.

title: TokenZero offload onto zerostack base: ship 5k shared lines, not 20k duplicated
description: TokenZero is the family outlier: codemode still embedded in tokenzero-mcp (4uql.8.1 fixes that), and engine-local primitives duplicate what zerostack already provides as base crates (zero-abi, zero-ref, zero-store, zerostack-machine-permit). Owner direction (9s32, 2026-07-24): cut cross-repo duplication with a base library WITHOUT coupling shipping (static-link, ship-separate). Scope: audit tokenzero-core/recovery/runtime/engine against zero-abi/zero-ref/zero-store, delete TokenZero-local copies in favor of zerostack deps, and land the shared test library. Net effect: installers pull one base; each engine ships only its differential. Depends on 9s32.1 RFC (dependency model) and 9s32.2 (duplication inventory) for the target list.

title: Audit tokenzero-core/recovery/runtime/engine vs zero-abi/zero-ref/zero-store; produce the move list
description: Concrete diff audit: for each TokenZero primitive (CAS store, ref types, envelope schema, recovery cache, permit handling), mark KEEP (engine-specific) or MOVE (duplicates zerostack base). Output: table of modules with LOC counts, destination crate (zero-abi/zero-ref/zero-store/new base crate), and API-compat shims needed. Input to the extraction tasks; feeds 9s32.2 inventory with TokenZero numbers.

title: Extract TokenZero CAS/ref/recovery primitives into zerostack base crates (delete local copies)
description: Execute the move list: port duplicated primitives to zero-abi/zero-ref/zero-store (or a new zero-* base crate per 9s32.1), leave API-compat shims in tokenzero-core, delete the local implementations. Static-link, ship-separate per owner direction; no runtime coupling between engines. Acceptance: net LOC reduction across tokenzero repo, cargo test --workspace green, clippy -D warnings green, docs/benchmarks.md regenerated with no perf regression >5%%.

title: Unify zerostack base crate naming (zero-* vs zerostack-machine-permit) before crates.io publish
description: zerostack currently mixes prefixes: zero-abi, zero-ref, zero-store vs zerostack-machine-permit. Pick ONE prefix (recommend zero-*: shorter, matches zero-abi/zero-ref already dominant) and rename before any crates.io placeholder publish (tokenzero-x67r), since renames after publish are effectively permanent. Document the convention in the zerostack README; update all three engines dep declarations.

title: surface-codemode feature test lane is red at HEAD (15 stable failures + flaky set)
description: Baseline run on HEAD (commit 734be9b, Spark, 2026-07-28): cargo test -p tokenzero-mcp --no-default-features --features surface-codemode --lib codemode => 62 passed / 17 failed. 15 failures reproduce on both HEAD and the osn1 patch (bench_harness x9 incl. fastmcp-v2 byte-parity comparisons, e2e envelope_v3, sentinel production_takeover, exec accumulator_bounds, quickjs_mutation_classifier x4); 2 more flip between runs (promise_all_runs_independent_shells_concurrently, shell_ref_is_canonical passed 6/6 in isolated reruns; accumulator_bounds + microtask_cap_error flaked baseline-side). The workspace default feature is surface-mcp, so `cargo test --workspace` never exercises this lane; the mutual-exclusion compile_error (tokenzero-irx9.3) means codemode tests only run with --no-default-features --features surface-codemode. This lane must be green before tokenzero-codemode ships as the default install surface (4uql.7) and before the crate extraction (4uql.8.1). Acceptance: the suite passes on a quiet worker; the 2 flaky tests get deterministic synchronization or a documented quarantine with tracking.

title: dogfood(zerostack): detached-job option on zero.token.shell advertised in surface types but always fails with aggregate_runtime_required
description: Observed 2026-07-28 dogfooding from this workspace. The zero_execute plan-surface types document zero.token.shell(command, opts) with an opts flag for detached long-running jobs that should return {job,log}. Any plan passing that flag fails with kind=aggregate_runtime_required ("requires one interruptible aggregate CodeMode sidecar (router-owned detached shell)... until the aggregate sidecar ships"). Impact: agents cannot detach long-running commands through the documented API; the fallback is shell-level detachment inside a foreground call, losing the {job,log} polling contract zero.token.job expects. Fix: ship the aggregate sidecar path or remove/guard the option in the advertised types. NOTE: filed here because workspace-sandboxed tools cannot write to ~/AI/zerostack/.beads; migrate to the zerostack tracker.

title: dogfood(zerostack): shell-command classifier keyword-matches quoted payload text and misroutes legit calls to the unshipped aggregate sidecar
description: Observed 2026-07-28 dogfooding. A foreground br create whose --description prose merely CONTAINS certain detached-job keywords (the b-word, the n-o-h-u-p utility name, the d-i-s-o-w-n builtin name) inside single quotes is rejected with kind=aggregate_runtime_required ("requires one interruptible aggregate CodeMode sidecar (router-owned b-shell)"). The identical command with the prose reworded succeeds immediately (proof: tokenzero-ifq3). So the routing classifier pattern-matches raw command text instead of parsing the command line structurally; quoted payload content must not influence routing. Fix: parse argv structurally (only real shell operators, a trailing ampersand, or actual detached-launch invocations should trigger detached classification), or at minimum strip quoted regions before keyword matching. NOTE: belongs in the zerostack tracker; filed here due to workspace sandboxing.

title: dogfood(zerostack): inner tokenzero codemode request hard-caps at 24s, defeating the caller-supplied deadline and losing long-command results
description: Observed 2026-07-28 dogfooding. zerostack___zero_execute accepts a wrapper-deadline parameter, but any zero.token.shell command running longer than ~24s fails with kind=substrate: "tokenzero codemode request timed out after 24000ms (tools/call)" even when the wrapper deadline is set to 70s (repro: a shell command that waits 30s then echoes, called with a 70s wrapper deadline -> substrate t-out at 24s; the remote command kept running but the result was lost to the caller). Impact: every long-running build/test/benchmark command through the shell surface loses its result and must be re-polled out-of-band; the documented wrapper deadline is misleading. Fix: honor the caller deadline end-to-end (propagate it into the codemode request), or return a job handle automatically past a threshold instead of erroring. NOTE: belongs in the zerostack tracker; filed here due to workspace sandboxing.

comments.author: aditya
comments.text: Additional layer found same day: besides the 24000ms substrate cap, a second hard cap exists at the runtime layer: kind=runtime "hard_max_wall_ms exceeded 20000 cm://exec/<id>" kills local shell commands at 20s regardless of the wrapper deadline. So long commands face at least two independent hard-coded ceilings (20s runtime, 24s substrate); both defeat the documented caller deadline parameter, and neither returns a job handle.

title: dogfood(zerostack): calling an unknown method on the plan surface silently degrades to catalog search instead of erroring
description: Observed 2026-07-28 dogfooding. A plan calling a nonexistent method on the zero plan surface (an expand helper that does not exist there) did not raise a method-not-found error; it returned a catalog SEARCH result listing available surfaces and methods, prefixed by "codemode:0 no zero.* connector referenced". Silent degradation to search makes agent bugs look like successful calls and wastes a round trip; the caller cannot distinguish the result shape from a real answer. Fix: unknown method names should raise a loud method_not_found error listing the closest valid names. NOTE: belongs in the zerostack tracker; filed here due to workspace sandboxing.

title: dogfood(fszero/zerostack): fz://blob refs in fs write acks have no recovery surface
description: Observed 2026-07-28 dogfooding. FS write-compound acks embed a post=fz://blob/<hash> ref inside the detail string for larger writes (observed when writing benchmarks/codemode-cpu-gate.sh), but no surface can recover it: the fs read compound errors "missing path" when given ref= (reads require a path, not a ref), and expanding the fz:// ref through the token surface errors kind=aggregate_runtime_required ("cross-engine ref expansion... until the aggregate sidecar ships"). So write acks advertise an exact-recovery ref that is unrecoverable, and agents cannot verify post-write bytes through refs. Fix: accept ref= in the fs read compound, or ship cross-engine expansion, or stop emitting fz:// refs in acks until recovery exists. NOTE: belongs in the FSZero or zerostack tracker; filed here due to workspace sandboxing.

title: dogfood(tokenzero): tz_read fuzzy dedupe elides changed-but-similar file content from the visible render
description: Observed 2026-07-28 dogfooding during the tokenzero-osn1 fix. Re-reading a file that had been modified since the prior read returned a capsule with deduped=true marked "~100% similar but NOT identical", and the visible render elided the content entirely, forcing a ref expansion (or raw base64 shell reads) to see the new bytes. When content is similar-but-not-identical the visible render should show a diff against the cached version or the fresh content, not a similarity notice; otherwise every incremental-edit workflow pays a second call per read. Acceptance: reading a changed file shows the change inline (unified diff or fresh bounded render) without requiring tz_expand.

title: dogfood(zerostack): plan-source classifier matches surface-call tokens inside string literals and rejects legit single-surface plans as cross-surface
description: Observed 2026-07-28 dogfooding (same root-cause family as tokenzero-1r73, but in the plan-source analyzer rather than the shell-command classifier). A zero_execute plan whose only surface call is a token-shell call, but whose shell-command STRING contains literal surface-call text of another engine (fs or graph call syntax, as prose inside a bead description), is rejected with kind=aggregate_runtime_required ("cross-surface plan"). Rewording the prose to avoid the literal call text makes the identical plan pass; even the TITLE of this bead tripped it on the first attempt. The plan analyzer must parse the plan source and only count actual call expressions, never string-literal content. NOTE: belongs in the zerostack tracker; filed here due to workspace sandboxing.
